evidence_log.note: 2026-09-05: the physical-AI capital wave that this idea underwrites got materially larger. Lyte AI raised a $165M Series C at $1.6B (Maverick Silicon) for custom robot-perception silicon and Atoms raised $1.7B led by a16z; the YC Summer 2026 batch names physical AI as its largest industrials cluster with robots moving into homes, warehouses and data centres, and 1 in 8 companies building hardware. Two deployment signals bear directly on behavioural certification of learned policies: Meta is running dual-armed Watney, Kinova and ABB robots on live cabling and repair work in its Iowa and Ohio data centres with internal estimates of automating up to 80% of specific technician workloads, and Norbert Health raised a $14M Series A to run robots doing nursing-assistant work in skilled-nursing facilities, explicitly investigational pending FDA clearance. Learned policies are now being pointed at people and at revenue-critical infrastructure, which is where third-party policy assurance becomes purchasable. Still no occupant found; status unchanged at watching.

2026-09-10: the buyer for this idea changed, and that is the update. Through 2026 the assumed customer was the robot maker or the deploying enterprise; the insurance market has now moved in front of both. Goodfault underwrites humanoids and software agents on one engine, explicitly 'priced on what the machine is permitted to do, with credits for safeguards enforced in code' and from fleet telemetry where it exists, and the trade press states plainly that ISO 10218 and ISO 3691-4 are 'the difference between a risk an underwriter can price and one they have to decline'. An underwriter buying behavioural evidence is a better customer than a robot maker buying a stamp: it pays because the evidence reduces its own loss cost, it renews annually, and it can make the certificate a condition of cover. Standards evidence tightened in the same direction - ISO 10218-1:2025 and 10218-2:2025 replaced the 2011 editions and absorbed ISO/TS 15066, but the mobile-robot and humanoid provisions are not expected until 2027-2028, leaving a two-year window in which learned policies are deployed near people with no applicable standard. Capital context: physical AI took $47.4B across 521 deals in H1 2026, roughly 4x H2 2025, and robotics startups have raised $18.8B in 2026 against $15B in all of 2025. Still no occupant found for independent behavioural certification of learned policies. A fourth re-point of this shape (ts-0359) was killed this run as a duplicate; the evidence belongs here. Status unchanged at watching, but this is the third consecutive run in which the surrounding conditions improved and the seat stayed empty.

2026-09-12: the first credible occupant of the neighbouring seat has appeared, and it narrows this idea rather than killing it. Robocurve (YC Summer 2026, Demo Day 2026-09-10) is building 'real-world evaluations of physical AI' - open-source tooling and independent, reproducible benchmarks scoring how well robot models do real jobs, from Jenga and sandwiches up to constructing a data centre, on the explicit argument that labs evaluate in-house, no independent group runs continuous benchmarking as a service, and simulation-strong models degrade on contact with the world. That is the same observation this entry was founded on. What it is not: Robocurve is a Public Benefit Corporation publishing open benchmarks, and a PBC whose legitimacy rests on openness structurally cannot also sell the confidential, per-deployment, liability-bearing certificate an underwriter conditions cover on - the two products poison each other. So the seat this entry actually claims (paid behavioural assurance sold to the insurer, re-run on every over-the-air policy update) remains empty, but the public-benchmark half of the thesis is now taken, and any version of this idea that leads with 'independent benchmarks' rather than 'insurable evidence' is dead. Context strengthened again: humanoid startups raised $8.6B by mid-2026, 1.8x all of 2025; Agility's Digit is past 65,000 operating hours across nine customer facilities (GXO, Schaeffler, Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada, Mercado Libre); the widely-cited payback arithmetic - break-even against one worker at about 14 months - is stated to assume 80% uptime, which is an assurance question wearing an operations costume. Fourth consecutive run in which conditions improved; first run in which somebody moved into the neighbourhood.

2026-09-22: the open question carried since 2026-09-19 - is the buyer the deploying enterprise's insurer, or the robot maker who needs a stamp to sell? - is now answered, and the answer is the insurer, because the maker-stamp flank has been taken by the platform owner. NVIDIA launched Halos for Robotics on 2026-06-22, extending its autonomous-vehicle safety architecture to industrial and humanoid robots and standing up an inspection lab to help partners reach third-party certification; ISO 10218-1:2025 and 10218-2:2025 have replaced the 2011 editions with system-level integration, functional safety, cybersecurity and a robot classification scheme. A robot maker who needs a stamp to sell will take the one the silicon vendor arranges, for free, inside the stack it already builds on. The insurer cannot: the 2026 assurance literature makes the point directly, that a governance discount conditioned on third-party certification is only as good as the certifier, and that insurers who accept certifications uncritically create a race to the bottom in assurance quality - which is an explicit instruction to underwriters not to accept the vendor-arranged stamp. That is a conflict NVIDIA cannot resolve for policies trained and served on its own stack, and it is the seat this entry should claim. Two cautions recorded against it. First, the shape is now visibly being built one category over: Artificial Intelligence Underwriting Company came out of stealth in July 2025 with a 15M dollar seed selling insurance, audits and the AIUC-1 certification standard for autonomous agents - software agents today, and there is no structural reason it stops there. Second, this entry has now been held at watching for three months. The recommendation for the next run that opens it is to stop re-validating and either commit to the insurer-facing version or kill it; the evidence has improved for five consecutive runs and the marginal value of a sixth confirmation is close to zero. Status unchanged at watching; scores still carry rubric_version 2 and are not comparable to v3 composites.

ideas.summary: Correlated-AI-failure catastrophe/accumulation model + per-insured AI-exposure score for primary P&C carriers: maps the foundation-model dependency graph across a carrier's whole commercial book (CGL/D&O/E&O/professional) and simulates the joint loss when thousands of insureds relying on the same few models/agents fail at once, so carriers can move from blanket AI exclusion to selectively pricing the fastest-growing exposure in the economy.

Carriers are blanket-excluding because they cannot price the peril - but AI is embedded in ~97% of companies (Gartner: 80% of enterprise apps shipped/updated in Q1 2026 embed an agent), so excluding the whole economy is unsustainable. Reinsurers are already pricing AI into treaties (Swiss Re sigma 07/2026 'Insuring AI'; Munich Re), 200+ active AI-liability cases, and the AI ecosystem's reliance on a few foundation models makes systemic correlated exposure the defining underwriting fear.

evidence_log.note: 2026-09-10: the accumulation question this idea prices has become concrete rather than theoretical. Enterprise agent security and governance took $435M across 12 financings between April and September 2026 - Zenity ($125M Series C) and Obsidian ($85M Series D) inside 48 hours, and AIR out of stealth on 2026-09-01 with $50M in two rounds weeks apart ($10M led by Sequoia, $40M led by Greenoaks), 20+ customers with about a quarter large enterprises. The datapoint that matters for correlated loss: AIR reports filtering out about 27% of the agent add-ons and skills it finds online, and its strongest early demand comes from financial services and pharmaceutical companies. A quarter of a shared, externally-sourced skill supply being unsafe is precisely the shape of a correlated exposure - many insureds pulling the same component from the same public registry - and it is now measured rather than hypothesised. On the pricing side Goodfault has begun underwriting AI agents and physical AI on one engine, which means primary carriers will shortly need a view on aggregation across their book whether or not they write the risk deliberately. Status unchanged at watching; no occupant found for the correlated-AI-failure accumulation model itself.

2026-09-12: two datapoints, one supportive and one that sharpens who the buyer is. Supportive: AI startups took 95.2% of all insurtech funding in Q1 2026 on $1.63B of total insurtech investment, and the industry's own commentary now states flatly that existing policies are silent, ambiguous or exclude autonomous software, that cyber and E&O are excluding AI claims, and that traditional insurers lack the data and technical capability to assess deployed AI systems. That last clause is the thesis of this entry restated by the market. Sharpening: Risklytics (YC Summer 2026) is selling insurance for frontier-technology businesses including robotics and data centres - a primary writer entering the risk, exactly as Goodfault did, and the third such entrant logged in five weeks. The pattern to note is that the money keeps arriving on the primary-writing side and never on the accumulation side; nobody is building the correlated-failure model that tells a carrier what its whole book does when the shared dependency fails. That asymmetry is the reason this entry is still open, and it is also a warning: if primary writers keep multiplying, the accumulation model gets bought by a reinsurer rather than sold to fifty carriers, which changes the venture-scale story. Worth revisiting the expansion path next time this entry is touched.

2026-09-17: the accumulation thesis keeps being confirmed by the shape of the funding rather than by anyone building the model. Of nineteen AI-agent financings tracked across August and September 2026, eight target the control layer - Zenity (125M), Obsidian (85M), Alice (140M), AIR Security (50M from Sequoia and Greenoaks), Cymphony (30M), AI Score (5.4M), Arrakis Security (8M) and FriskAI (3.6M) - the third consecutive month in which governance leads the category by deal count, summarised in the trade coverage as investors buying the brakes faster than the car. Every one of those is a control on a single insured's own agents; none of them measures what happens across a book when the shared dependency fails. The asymmetry logged on 2026-09-12 is now four months old and unchanged, which is the argument for the entry staying open and also the argument that the window is a finite one. Status unchanged at watching. The open question from 2026-09-12 - whether this gets acquired by a reinsurer rather than sold to fifty carriers - was not re-tested this run.

ideas.summary: Independent 'demand-realism / probability-of-energization' + correlated-materialization risk engine for the AI grid buildout: a frontier model that fuses cross-utility interconnection filings, permits, transformer/equipment supply chains, construction and satellite signals, chip-allocation and financing data, and developer behavior to score which announced data-center loads (and the power/grid projects meant to serve them) will actually materialize and how correlated their fates are - the independent source of truth utilities/PUCs use to avoid stranded overbuild and lenders/ABS investors/hyperscalers use to avoid stranded capital.

cross.ai_signal: Frontier multimodal models can now fuse heterogeneous, messy, unstructured signals (interconnection-queue filings across many utilities, permit and construction records, equipment/transformer lead-time and chip-allocation data, hyperscaler capex guidance, project-finance terms, satellite imagery, developer filing behavior) into a per-project probability-of-energization AND simulate the CORRELATED materialization of thousands of projects whose fates are linked through shared hyperscaler demand, shared equipment supply chains and shared power constraints. Classical integrated-resource-planning load forecasting is single-point, historically-grounded and assumes independent, stable demand - it structurally cannot model strategic 'phantom' duplicate requests or correlated materialization, the same independent-rate blind spot that made ts-0048 and ts-0054 AI-native.
cross.structural_signal: A ~$1.4T US utility grid buildout (top-5 hyperscaler capex ~$602B in 2026; >$9B data-center securitization) colliding with an acute demand-truth crisis: developers file duplicate 'phantom' interconnection requests across multiple utilities, NERC's 10-yr peak forecast jumped 24% (+224 GW) almost entirely on speculative data-center load, ~$700B of the buildout is projected to hit residential ratepayers, and 23 states have approved large-load tariffs (300+ bills in 6 weeks) explicitly to weed out speculative requests. Ratings agencies (Moody's, S&P) and bond investors are openly 'questioning the modeling assumptions' (financing treats contracted demand as actual demand); the live debate is overbuild-stranded-asset risk (utilities/ratepayers) vs under-delivery-stranded-capital risk (lenders/hyperscalers) - both sides need the same demand-realism truth, and the emerging concept ('probability-of-energization-weighted capacity') is acknowledged by analysts (Janus Henderson, E3) but productized by no one.

ideas.buyer: Beachhead: the resource-planning / load-forecasting lead at a large electric utility (or the staff/consumer-advocate side of a state PUC) facing a flood of speculative large-load interconnection requests right now, who must decide how much transmission/generation to build and how to set cost-causative tariffs without saddling ratepayers with stranded assets. Expansion: project-finance lenders, data-center ABS/CMBS investors and ratings agencies underwriting the $1.4T buildout who need independent demand-truth (their assumptions are 'under scrutiny'); then hyperscalers/developers themselves and the industry-standard demand-realism layer all sides price against.
ideas.trigger: 2026 demand-truth crisis is live and dated: 23 states approved large-load tariffs (51 tariffs, 300+ bills in 6 weeks) explicitly to filter speculative requests; NERC +24% forecast (Dec 2025/2026) on speculative load; Moody's/S&P and Bond Buyer flagging that data-center financing assumptions are 'under scrutiny' (2026); PowerLines ~$700B ratepayer exposure; and frontier multimodal models newly make cross-source demand-realism + correlated-materialization modeling possible. The overbuild-vs-underdelivery debate means urgency persists regardless of which way demand breaks.
ideas.why_incumbents_cant: Supply-side capacity finders (GridCARE - generative-AI mapping of hidden grid capacity sold to developers; Pearl Street - interconnection-study automation, ts-0014) answer 'where can I get power,' not 'is this announced demand real and correlated'; utility IRP tools and load forecasters (Itron, consultancies E3/Brattle/ICF) use classical single-point historical methods that the phantom-load problem breaks and are advisory, not an independent productized model; ratings agencies (Moody's, S&P) and investors (Janus Henderson's PoE framing) write commentary but ship no independent platform; flexibility players (Emerald AI ts-0056, Verrus) make load curtailable, a different problem. No independent, cross-utility, correlated-materialization demand-realism engine exists - and utilities/PUCs/cedents structurally want a source of truth NOT owned by the developers or their own relationship-conflicted advisors (the same independent-model demand that sustains third-party CAT modelers).

BUT novelty SOFTENING on two fronts: (1) the incumbent 'solution' so far is tariff design (AEP Ohio 25-MW eligibility / 85% min-billing / termination fees cut its queue 30->13 GW), a policy lever, not a demand-realism model; (2) GridUnity (interconnection-queue management software) is now publicly framing 'phantom data centers flooding the load queue' - adjacent and could extend toward per-project materialization scoring. ERCOT is now working a 438 GW large-load queue (up from the 410 GW figure carried in the 08-13 scan) against a 2,600 GW national interconnection backlog with median time to commercial operation approaching five years. The realism gap is now measured rather than argued: data-centre project cancellations more than quadrupled to 25 in 2025, 30-50% of the 2026 US pipeline is expected to be delayed or cancelled, only about a third of announced capacity is actually under construction, and at least 188 local opposition groups now operate across 40 states. Equipment is now an independent, shared, correlating constraint on energization, not a footnote to it.

ideas.revalidation: 2026-07-25 first re-check since 06-30: SURVIVES and the thesis is now QUANTIFIED in public - but novelty is softening because a competitor holds the observation layer. Validation: an analytics group signals at least 40% of AI data centers slated for 2026 completion will be delayed (Microsoft/OpenAI projects slipping 3+ months) with companies denying holdups while satellite imagery contradicts them; reporting now describes half of US builds delayed or cancelled and a 7 GW capacity crisis; transformer lead times exceed five years in extreme cases against 12-18 month compute cycles. Practitioners now name electrical equipment as the single most common cause of data-centre delay: switchgear beyond 60 weeks (44 in late 2025), transformers averaging 128 weeks, GSUs 144, high-capacity units to four years, with GSU demand up 274% and substation transformer demand up 116% since 2019 and only ~$2B of North American capacity expansion arriving by 2028. Cancellations quadrupled to 25 in 2025 and 30-50% of the 2026 pipeline is expected to slip or die. ideas.summary: Clearing market for long-lead electrical-equipment positions: value, match and transfer reserved factory production slots and in-flight orders for transformers, switchgear and gensets between projects, cleared by a frontier multimodal model that reads a bespoke engineering specification and decides whether a unit being built to spec A can be made to satisfy project B - the interchangeability judgement that is the actual reason this market cannot clear today.

cross.ai_signal: Frontier multimodal reasoning over engineering specification corpora. A power transformer is defined by a 100-300 page bespoke utility specification plus drawings, test requirements and site constraints - MVA and impedance, BIL, winding and vector configuration, tap changer type and range, bushing arrangement, cooling class, seismic qualification, sound level, footprint and clearances, protection and monitoring, and the buyer's own decades-old standards clauses. Deciding whether an in-flight unit can satisfy a different project is an engineering-judgement task over exactly that kind of dense, heterogeneous, partly-scanned, partly-contradictory document set, and it is what an application engineer at an OEM does over weeks. August 2026 makes this economically new twice over: DeepSeek V4-Pro went GA on 2026-08-12 with a 1M-token context, 384k-token output and explicit low/high/max reasoning-effort tiers, so a max-effort pass over an entire specification pair is now a cheap, routine operation; and OpenAI and Cerebras previewed GPT-5.6 Sol Ultrafast on 2026-08-13 at a claimed 750 output tokens/second against ~53 standard - 14x - so the same judgement can be returned inside a trading conversation rather than a procurement cycle. Interchangeability at deal speed is the product.
cross.structural_signal: The scarcest asset in the American build-out is a place in an electrical-equipment factory queue, and it is stranded in the wrong hands. As of mid-2026 switchgear lead times run beyond 60 weeks (44 in late 2025), standard power transformers average 128 weeks, generator step-up transformers average 144 weeks and high-capacity units reach four years. GSU demand rose 274% and substation transformer demand 116% between 2019 and 2025. Data centres alone need roughly 74 GW of three-phase transformer capacity in 2026 - about the same as everything replaced annually across the entire US grid. Manufacturers hold a production slot for 10-30% of equipment cost, so the slot is already a paid-for, priced, financially distinct instrument. And a float of orphaned positions exists right now: data-centre project cancellations more than quadrupled to 25 in 2025, 30-50% of the 2026 US pipeline is expected to be delayed or cancelled, only about a third of announced capacity is actually under construction, and ERCOT is working a 438 GW large-load queue. Practitioners argue in print that this is a procurement-information failure rather than a manufacturing shortage - buyers place duplicate speculative reservations to hedge, OEMs cannot tell a hedge from a real order, so they quote scarcity, which makes buyers hedge harder. That bullwhip is an information problem a neutral clearing party can fix; ~$2B of North American capacity expansion does not arrive until 2028.

ideas.summary: Underwritten carrier selection: adjudicate, at tender time, whether a specific motor carrier on a specific lane is a defensible choice - and then indemnify the freight broker for the negligent-selection liability the Supreme Court handed the entire industry in May 2026. cross.ai_signal: Frontier models can now read the full unstructured safety record of all ~600,000 US motor carriers - individual roadside inspection narratives, crash reports, FMCSA authority and insurance filing history, cancellations, chameleon-carrier reincarnation patterns, and civil dockets - and resolve entities across reincarnations, then adjudicate a named carrier on a named lane within the seconds a spot tender allows. Existing vetting products resell FMCSA SMS/BASIC percentiles because structured scores were all that was machine-readable; the narrative text, which is where the actual predictive signal about a small carrier lives, was not.
cross.structural_signal: On 2026-05-14 the Supreme Court decided Montgomery v. Caribe Transport II unanimously, holding that FAAAA does not preempt state-law negligent-hiring claims against freight brokers because they fall within the safety savings clause. The pleading-stage preemption defence that protected the industry is gone. This lands on a commercial auto liability line that has been unprofitable fourteen years running through fifty-six consecutive quarters of rate increases, with nuclear verdicts up 52% year over year, a median nuclear verdict of $51M, and an average trucking verdict over $22M. Many broker policies exclude negligent-selection claims outright, and Justice Kavanaugh's concurrence explicitly warned that litigation and insurance costs to brokers may be significant even when brokers win.

ideas.buyer: The risk or compliance owner at a mid-market freight broker doing $50M-$1B of gross revenue, at the contingent-auto and E&O renewal following the ruling, when the carrier adds or reprices a negligent-selection exclusion. They tender thousands of spot loads a week to small carriers on informal judgement recorded in Slack messages and spreadsheet notes, which is exactly the evidence that fails under cross-examination.
ideas.trigger: Montgomery v. Caribe Transport II, decided 2026-05-14, unanimous. The defence disappeared on a single day and the 2026-2027 renewal cycle is where the cost lands.
ideas.why_incumbents_cant: Highway, Carrier Assure, Truckstop/RMIS, Assure Assist's MyCarrierPackets and DAT CarrierWatch all sell scores and monitoring on a SaaS seat and expressly disclaim liability for the selection - taking the tail would destroy both their margin structure and their balance sheets, and their pricing has no relationship to loss. The AI-native trucking insurers that raised real money (Nirvana, HDVI, Koffie) underwrite the fleet's own driving behaviour, not the broker's choice of fleet, and price a book annually rather than a decision per load. Legacy broker E&O and contingent-auto carriers have no per-load data ingestion and are responding to the ruling by excluding the peril rather than pricing it, which is what leaves the gap open.
ideas.revalidation: 2026-08-22 update with substantial new evidence. The severity half of this thesis got confirmed in the hardest possible way: a jury returned a $604M verdict against C.H. Robinson over a 2021 six-vehicle pileup, apportioning liability across broker, carrier and driver with the largest share potentially falling on the broker; C.H. Robinson is appealing (Bloomberg, 2026-08-20). This is the first nine-figure post-Montgomery datapoint and it lands on the exact peril the idea underwrites - the broker's selection decision, not the fleet's driving. Trade coverage is simultaneously reporting that stakeholders see 'limited operational change' in day-to-day brokerage practice, which is the tell: the exposure repriced and the behaviour did not, so the gap between what brokers do and what they are now liable for is widening rather than closing. The open question from the 2026-08-20 run is unchanged and now more urgent - pull five broker contingent-auto or E&O forms written after 2026-05-14 and establish whether negligent selection is being excluded or merely surcharged.

evidence_updates.note: Confirmed and strengthened. Montgomery v. Caribe Transport II was decided 9-0, holding that state negligent-hiring claims against freight brokers are not preempted by the FAAAA; two months later a Texas jury returned $604M against C.H. Robinson, its motor carrier and the driver over a 2021 fatal pileup, with the largest share of liability potentially falling on the broker. The August 2026 compliance picture adds two things the original entry did not have: FMCSA is now under direct industry pressure to publish an adequate-carrier-vetting standard, and brokers tightening their own vetting are beginning to shut carriers with Conditional safety ratings out of brokered freight entirely. That is the market pricing selection risk without an underwriter - which is the demand signal - but it also raises the competitive question of whether a published federal standard would commoditise the determination and leave only the indemnity. Keep watching; do not promote until FMCSA's direction on a vetting standard is clearer.

ideas.summary: Coverage-cliff underwriting for the 22M people hit by the enhanced-premium-tax-credit lapse: price and finance an episode of care for the newly uninsured.
ideas.kill_reason: Duplicate of killed ts-0124. PayZen, PatientFi, Cherry, AccessOne and ClearBalance already occupy non-recourse patient financing, and Carrum, MDsave and Sesame occupy pre-priced episodes. The 2026 signal is much worse than when ts-0124 was killed - enhanced subsidies expired 2026-01-01, average subsidised premiums went from $888 to $1,904, the Urban Institute projects 4.8M more uninsured, hospitals face a $31.9B revenue decline and $6.3B more uncompensated care in 2026, and 734 rural hospitals are at closure risk - but a worse version of a solved problem is not a new company.

ideas.summary: Long-horizon agent that carries an immigration case end to end through the 3.2M-case backlog.
ideas.kill_reason: Occupied plus a diffuse consumer buyer. Immigration legal AI is one of the most crowded vertical-legal niches (Casium, Borderwise, Lawfully, Boundless, Docketwise and others), the work is episodic per matter, and the payer is an individual in financial distress rather than an institution with a recurring budget. The backlog itself is spectacular - 3,195,137 cases at the end of June 2026, 2.31M pending asylum applications, roughly 900-day average waits and about 3,300 cases per judge - but a longer queue does not make a saturated consumer legal market venture-scale.

ideas.summary: Requalification engine for the Chinese absorption of European auto manufacturing: machine-generate the type-approval and PPAP/production-part-approval packages when a Chinese OEM takes over an idle European plant and must requalify the tier-2/3 supplier base.
ideas.kill_reason: Trips the standing services-replacement filter and duplicates the ledger. The barrier is document reasoning over engineering and quality records, which is exactly the barrier a seed-stage services-replacement company clears, and killed ts-0185 (qualification-collapse engine) and ts-0217 (no-quote capacity unlock for engineered-to-order equipment) already cover the transfer-learning-through-requalification template. The structural signal is real and worth keeping - Chinese brands hit 15% of the European market, Chery is moving into Nissan Sunderland's freed Line 1 for Q3 2027, Stellantis and Dongfeng formed a JV in May 2026 for Rennes, and China is buying the European parts base - but it points at an engineering-services motion.

ideas.summary: Voyage-level IMO 2026 Carbon Intensity Indicator optimisation and green-surcharge minimisation for container lines and shippers.
ideas.kill_reason: Occupied by funded maritime-AI incumbents - ZeroNorth, Nautilus Labs and Bearing AI have sold vessel performance and voyage optimisation into exactly this buyer for years and CII compliance was the obvious extension the day the regulation was written. The surcharge is real ($150-$400 per container depending on route) but it is a line item the incumbents already manage.

ideas.summary: Terminal throughput engine for US ports whose automation is frozen by labour contract: raise container capacity without new automated equipment.
ideas.kill_reason: Concentrated buyer and a non-technical constraint. There are a few dozen US terminal operators, the ILA contract explicitly froze new semi-automated and automated equipment outside a narrow list through 2030-09-30, and the ILWU/PMA negotiation covering 22,000 workers at 29 West Coast ports has automation as its defining dispute. The binding constraint is a labour agreement, not an algorithm - shipping a throughput model into a bargaining fight is selling into the middle of someone else's war.

ideas.summary: Experience-manufacturing platform for the entry-level hiring collapse: build the competence that vanished junior jobs used to create.
ideas.kill_reason: Duplicate of killed ts-0068 and ts-0084, and the same weak-why-now failure mode. The data got dramatically worse - no-experience hiring down roughly 73% from its 2022 peak, recent-graduate unemployment above the overall workforce rate for the first time in decades, 21% of companies freezing entry-level hiring explicitly because of AI - but the party that suffers is the graduate and the enterprise cost lands five to ten years out, so there is still no buyer with a phone ringing today. AI corporate upskilling remains crowded.

ideas.summary: Packaging reformulation engine for the EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation obligations that begin in August 2026, including the near-total PFAS ban in food-contact packaging.
ideas.kill_reason: Duplicate of killed ts-0222 plus the standing compliance-rail filter. Citrine Informatics, Albert Invent and ChemCopilot already sell PFAS and problematic-ingredient reformulation; a new regulation is a new reason to buy from them, not a new product. Logged because the deadline is genuinely current and will keep surfacing in scans.

ideas.summary: Beneficial-reuse certification and land-application indemnity for treated Permian produced water.
ideas.kill_reason: Premature rather than occupied, and better as supply for ts-0239 than as a company. The Permian handles more than 22M barrels a day of produced water rising an estimated 39% by 2035, and TCEQ's land-application rulemaking would open treated oilfield water to Texas farmland - but the rules are not final, the long-tail liability regime for what happens to a farm that irrigated with it is entirely unformed, and there is no loss history to price against. Underwriting an indemnity into an undefined liability regime is not a risk position, it is a guess. Revisit when TCEQ finalises.

ideas.summary: AI-native childcare capacity platform for the $172B/yr childcare crisis.
ideas.kill_reason: Fails the AI-native gate outright. The crisis is severe and well-measured - $172B/yr in economic cost, $38B of it borne by employers, 455,000 women out of the labour market between January and August 2025, $13,128 average annual cost - but the binding constraints are staff-to-child ratios, state licensing and physical real estate. Frontier AI does not relieve any of the three, and a matching or benefits layer on top is a marketplace, not an AI-native company.

ideas.summary: Municipal credit repricing engine for the property tax revolt: reprice every ad valorem-secured bond against each state's new statutory cap language.
ideas.kill_reason: Duplicate of killed ts-0138. MuniBonds.AI, DPC Data's structured municipal corpus and the Lumesis/MMA/Solve/ICE analytics layer already occupy continuous municipal disclosure intelligence, and this is that product with a new input variable.

ideas.summary: AI-native MGA writing liability for micro-fleet trucking companies priced out by the hard market.
ideas.kill_reason: Occupied by funded AI-native operators - Nirvana, HDVI and Koffie all underwrite motor carrier liability off telematics and have raised substantially. Logged deliberately alongside ts-0240 as its nearest neighbour: the trucking insurtech capital went to insuring the fleet's own driving, which is precisely why the broker's selection decision is still uninsured.

ideas.summary: Turnaround scope-compression engine for refineries: read the plant's full inspection, corrosion-loop and prior-workpack history to decide which equipment actually has to be opened, riding record refining margins and ~11M b/d of global capacity offline.
ideas.kill_reason: Occupied and quantified. iFactory sells AI risk-prioritised turnaround planning claiming 40-60% reduction in scope additions and 40% reduction in total inspection scope; Prometheus Group and IAMTech both sell shutdown/turnaround/outage platforms; risk-based inspection is a mature codified discipline (API 580/581) with incumbent vendors. The category is not merely occupied, it is occupied by vendors already publishing the exact benefit this idea would claim.

ideas.summary: Construction delay-claim underwriter: read a contractor's entire project record (RFIs, submittals, daily logs, schedule updates, photos) to price a delay or change-order claim, then advance cash against it, riding the 349k-worker construction labour gap and systematic schedule slippage on the data-centre buildout.

The monetisation wrapper is a restatement of ts-0111 (AI case-outcome underwriting for litigation finance), already killed.

ideas.kill_reason: Fails the AI-native gate and the why-now is contingent. The hard part is microsecond counterfactual simulation over depth-of-book tick data - classical quantitative microstructure work that frontier models do not obviously improve - and the transaction-cost-analysis field (S3, Abel Noser, BestEx Research, kdb-based stacks) already owns it. The rescission of Rules 611 and 610(e) is also still only a proposal (SEC 2026-06-11, comments closed 2026-08-17), so the liability the whole business depends on may never be created.

ideas.summary: Forward bid on the ROAD Act's mandatory build-to-rent exit: sell an institutional BTR owner a firm per-parcel price today for the retail sale to an individual homeowner that the statute forces within seven years.
ideas.kill_reason: Correlated risk - the ts-0243 lesson applied directly. Every put in the book is written on the same national housing market and the same statutory supply wave hitting simultaneously; when it goes wrong it goes wrong for the whole book at once, which is what makes a risk unfinanceable regardless of how good the per-parcel prediction is. The seven-year horizon also removes any urgency to buy it now.

ideas.summary: Merchant of firm memory supply: hold DRAM allocation and inventory positions and sell OEMs a guaranteed delivered quantity on a date, using machine-proven part interchangeability to satisfy commitments with whatever silicon is obtainable.
ideas.kill_reason: Occupied by real merchants and duplicative of live book entries. The interchangeability-proving half restates ts-0185 (qualification-collapse engine) and ts-0231, both killed, and the merchant structure restates ts-0202 (slot exchange), which is already in the book.

ideas.kill_reason: Duplicate and episodic. ts-0183 (airworthiness-substantiation engine generating FAA PMA/DER approval packages) is the same product and was already killed. ideas.kill_reason: Fails the venture-scale gate on buyer concentration. The reachable customer set is three or four national carriers, the FAA, and a handful of satellite operators - a market that can support a valuable consultancy or a licensed tool, but not a billion-dollar company, because there is no expansion path to more buyers.

ideas.summary: Rack-level fuel basis fixing for commercial fleets: predict terminal-by-terminal rack price from refinery outage, pipeline nomination, terminal inventory and weather, and sell trucking, farm, marine and municipal buyers a fixed all-in delivered price for a term, taking the un-hedgeable basis risk.

A national product-supply shock - the very thing the thesis is built on, with ~11M b/d of refining capacity offline and US inventories heading to their lowest since 2000 - moves every rack in the country at once, so the book has no independence. Mansfield Energy, Breakthrough Fuel and the fuel-hedging desks already sell fixed delivered pricing to exactly these buyers.

ideas.summary: Sub-threshold single-family operating platform: run large scattered-site rental portfolios on behalf of many independent sub-350-home owner entities, since the ROAD Act makes aggregation above 350 homes illegal but leaves the operating economics intact.
ideas.kill_reason: Occupied and legally fragile. Doorstead, Belong, Poplar Homes, Latchel and EliseAI already sell AI-assisted institutional-grade single-family property management. Worse, the statutory definition of 'investment control' explicitly reaches managing members and investment managers, so a platform that actually controls the portfolios would itself be aggregated over the threshold - the structure defeats itself.

ideas.summary: Tenant-to-owner conversion engine for the ROAD Act's build-to-rent carve-out: put every sitting tenant on a machine-run twelve-to-twenty-four-month path to mortgage readiness so the mandated seven-year sale to an individual homeowner has a buyer.
ideas.kill_reason: Occupied by a bruised category. Home Partners of America (Blackstone), Divvy Homes, Landis and Pathway have all built lease-to-own or path-to-ownership products at scale, and several have contracted sharply. The forcing event is also seven years out, so there is nothing that makes a customer buy this in 2026.

ideas.summary: Control of record: an adjudicated, continuously maintained national map of 'investment control' over US single-family homes, sold as a per-acquisition determination with an indemnity behind it - because from 2027-01-07 the ROAD to Housing Act makes any purchase by an entity controlling 350+ homes a $1M-per-violation offence, the statutory control test reaches through affiliates, GPs, managing members, investment managers and any non-passive 25% equity holder, and Treasury's implementing regulations will almost certainly arrive after the prohibition already bites.

cross.ai_signal: Two things arrived together. Long-horizon agents that hold a whole corpus for a single decision - Grok 4.6 (2026-08-12) completing jobs across ~53 turns and ~0.5B input tokens, Claude Opus 5 topping the Artificial Analysis agentic index at 55.3, Fable 5 shipping 1M-token context for Mythos-class long-horizon work - make it economic to resolve one entity's full control graph end to end rather than in human-reviewed fragments. And frontier document reasoning is now good enough to apply a statutory test with eleven carve-outs to heterogeneous source text: 3,100+ county deed and assessor records with no common grantee format, 50 state entity registries, operating agreements and LPAs, SEC and state fund filings, and the deed language that distinguishes a passive LP from an entity with investment control. Nobody built this map before because nobody had a reason to know how many homes an entity controls, and the cost of finding out by hand ($500-$5,000 per entity chain) exceeded the value of the answer. The statute created the reason and the models collapsed the cost in the same quarter.
cross.structural_signal: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R.6644) became law on 2026-07-11 without signature under the ten-day presentment rule. Section 1001 bars any 'large institutional investor' from purchasing or contracting to purchase single-family homes from 2027-01-07, with civil penalties of up to $1M per violation or three times the purchase price, whichever is greater. 'Large institutional investor' means any for-profit entity that, alone or with affiliated entities, has direct or indirect investment control over 350 or more single-family homes in aggregate; 'investment control' expressly reaches general partners, managing members, investment managers and any holder of more than 25% of any class of equity in the owning entity unless genuinely passive; and the aggregation rule defeats splitting a portfolio across LLCs. Homes held on 2026-07-11 are grandfathered permanently and there is no divestiture requirement, so the entire compliance burden falls on the forward transaction. Treasury must write implementing regulations in consultation with HUD, FHFA and the SEC, but the Act forbids any regulation from altering the definitions, narrowing the exceptions, expanding the covered class or moving the 350 threshold - and practitioners expect the prohibition to take effect before the regulations are finalised. Separately, California enacted its own institutional investor reporting law in early 2026, so the same determination is being demanded by states as well.

ideas.buyer: First: the general counsel or head of compliance at an SFR aggregator, build-to-rent sponsor or real-estate credit fund in the weeks before 2027-01-07, who has to certify to an investment committee and to lenders that a pending acquisition does not cross the threshold - and who discovers that the 25%-non-passive limb sweeps in fund stakes and JV interests nobody had ever counted as 'homes'. Second, and larger: the title underwriter or closing agent asked for an affirmative endorsement that a transaction is not a prohibited acquisition, on a deal where a prohibited purchase is potentially voidable and the penalty is three times the price.
ideas.trigger: 2027-01-07 - the date Section 1001's prohibition and penalties take effect, on statutory definitions Treasury is barred from narrowing, with implementing regulations likely still unfinished.
ideas.why_incumbents_cant: The property-data incumbents (Cotality/CoreLogic, ATTOM, Regrid, Reonomy, PropertyRadar, Batch) sell bulk records and skip-tracing contact resolution; their product is a licensed file, not an adjudicated determination, and their business model cannot carry indemnity on a legal conclusion. The AI title-search vendors (Pippin, TerraLedger and the rest) work the chain of title on one parcel - liens, encumbrances, marketability - which is a different question from aggregate control across an entity's whole national footprint. The big title underwriters have the balance sheet to indemnify but no national entity-control graph and a century of underwriting practice organised parcel by parcel. Law firms are producing excellent client alerts on the statute and will bill hours per entity, which is precisely the cost structure that makes per-transaction determination impossible. And the institutions themselves cannot self-certify credibly: the counterparty, the lender and the securitisation trustee all want a determination from someone other than the buyer.

ideas.summary: AI-native importer of record for foreign sellers, taking full US customs liability as the June-3-2026 'Strengthening Customs Enforcement' EO restricts foreign entities from serving as IOR and imposes bond / tangible-domestic-asset thresholds.
ideas.kill_reason: Existing category, and the liability does not actually stop with the provider. Importer-of-record-as-a-service is already sold at scale (Tecex, Carra Globe, GCE Logistic, 24hour-ar, Zonos), and practitioner guidance is explicit that appointing a thinly capitalised IOR 'simply adds another party to a shared liability position - if the IOR cannot pay or disputes the debt, the foreign seller is next in line.' The EO reshuffles who is allowed to play by raising capital requirements; it does not create a new product. Folded into ts-0281 as the own-the-entry expansion path instead.

ideas.summary: Rules-of-origin change hedge: sell a manufacturer a multi-year contract that pays out if USMCA rules of origin move adversely for their specific part, now that the US declined extension on 2026-07-01 and the pact runs on annual reviews to 2036.
ideas.kill_reason: No beachhead, so it fails Step 3 before novelty. The structural signal is real and large - Art. 34.7.4 annual reviews collapse a 16-year rule horizon to twelve months across ~$1.8T of North American trade - but a derivative on trade-rule outcomes has no counterparty, no reserve base, no reference index and a sales cycle measured in board approvals; you cannot land it fast and you cannot price the first one. The insurable slice of the same signal is determination error, not policy change, which is ts-0281.

ideas.summary: Part 108 operational-area safety-case and BVLOS approval engine: generate and continuously maintain the systematic safety programme and operational-area approvals the FAA's final BVLOS rule will require of every drone operator.
ideas.kill_reason: Occupied before the rule has even published. The final Part 108 rule reached OIRA on 2026-07-10 and the drone-ops platforms (Aloft, Airdata, DroneDeploy, FlytBase, Kittyhawk) are already marketing Part 108 readiness on the explicit pitch that compliance records are 'a byproduct of how you operate' - they hold the operator's mission planning, crew briefing and post-flight logging and will absorb the safety-programme layer. The ledger has also already killed two aviation approval-package plays for the same shape (ts-0183 PMA/DER, ts-0265 FAA STC).

ideas.summary: Roadside exception and law-enforcement interface network for driverless freight: diagnose any highway exception from truck telemetry, decide remote-fix versus dispatch, and give officers a machine-readable counterpart now that driver-out operations scale in 2026 with no federal rule.
ideas.kill_reason: Duplicates two prior kills and is only half AI-native. ts-0205 (fleet-level exception resolution for physical AI) and ts-0174 (remote-operator marketplace) were both killed because managed teleoperation and intervention is an established category and every autonomy company treats intervention data as core training IP - Aurora, Kodiak, Waabi and Volvo AS all build launch-and-land terminals and remote assistance in-house. The remaining half, dispatching physical responders to a shoulder, is a service network with no model edge.

ideas.summary: Cross-national qualification mutual-recognition engine for European defence: prove statistical equivalence so a component qualified in one member state is accepted in another, unlocking the ramp blocked by fragmented national certification regimes.
ideas.kill_reason: Third pass at the same square. ts-0185 (qualification-collapse engine) was killed by government-funded incumbency - Senvol ML is running a US Navy programme through July 2027 whose stated goal is exactly to substitute in-situ monitoring evidence for the qualification battery, and the standard it produces will be the standard - and ts-0247 (requalification for the Chinese absorption of European auto plants) was killed for duplicating that template. The European fragmentation is real and named as a constraint, but the product is the same transfer-learning-through-requalification engine already killed twice.

ideas.summary: Program-management judgment agent for capital projects: hold the whole multi-party schedule, detect critical-path threats weeks early and act on them, so one experienced superintendent can run three jobs instead of one.
ideas.kill_reason: Occupied and previously killed. The signal is sharp - industry reporting now names experienced superintendents, project managers and estimators, not trades labour, as the binding constraint, and European defence names the same scarcity of programme managers - but nPlan, Alice Technologies, Trunk Tools, Buildots, Doxel and Procore's own copilot already occupy schedule risk and look-ahead. The ledger also killed ts-0122 (breaking the supervision ratio in the trades) and ts-0170 (construction schedule-feasibility and labour-supply underwriting).

ideas.summary: Customs refund-claim purchaser: advance importers cash today against duty drawback and post-Supreme-Court IEEPA refund entitlements, priced by machine-reading their full entry history.
ideas.kill_reason: Occupied, and already killed inside ts-0028. YC alone has funded Pax ('AI-native broker that automates and maximises tariff refunds through duty drawback') and Forge (duty drawback as a white-glove service on AI tooling), alongside Charter Brokerage, Alliance Drawback and Tariff Refund HQ. Buying the claim rather than brokering it is a balance-sheet variation on a funded, competitive service.

ideas.summary: EU AI Act Article 50 rail: machine-readable synthetic-content marking and AI-interaction disclosure for every provider and deployer touching the EU, live 2026-08-02.
ideas.kill_reason: Trigger eroded and provenance is owned. The Digital Omnibus entered into force 2026-07-27 and deferred the Annex III high-risk obligations to 2027-12-02 and embedded-product high-risk to 2028-08-02, so what actually bit on 2026-08-02 is transparency plus the penalty regime - a disclosure widget, not a market. Content provenance is held by C2PA, Truepic, Adobe and the model providers themselves. Duplicates ts-0195 (consent and value metering for synthetic performance) and ts-0225 (content-contribution clearing house).

ideas.summary: Subsurface helium discovery and recovery intelligence, triggered by the 2026 Qatari production strikes that doubled spot helium against semiconductor and MRI demand.
ideas.kill_reason: Fails the AI-native and venture-scale gates together. The scarcity is real and fresh, but the value accrues to whoever owns the reservoir - Pulsar Helium, Blue Star Helium, Total Helium and New Era Helium are resource companies - and subsurface inference is a capability inside an exploration company rather than a product sold to one. Software sold into a few dozen helium juniors is not a $1B path.

ideas.summary: Defence sub-tier capacity merchant: contract with primes to deliver parts on a firm date and fulfil through a machine-modelled network of Tier-2/3 shops, absorbing the schedule risk primes cannot.
ideas.kill_reason: Occupied by well-funded companies doing exactly this. Hadrian builds AI-native precision factories for defence and aerospace, Xometry runs the manufacturing marketplace at scale, and Vendra and Silkline AI are both funded to turn a technical requirement into parts from qualified US suppliers. It also duplicates the ledger's own supply-discovery template (ts-0217, folded into ts-0202). Kept separate from ts-0282 deliberately: the distinction is take-the-order versus fund-the-shop.

ideas.summary: Origin of record: an underwritten country-of-origin determination for imported goods - reconstruct a part's true multi-tier bill of materials, issue a written origin and regional-value-content determination, and indemnify the importer for back duties, interest and penalties if CBP later denies the claim. Tax-liability insurance, but for origin, at the moment the US declined to extend USMCA (2026-07-01) and put rules of origin on an annual review cycle, and the 2026-06-03 customs-enforcement executive order removed the mitigation that used to soften a wrong answer.

cross.ai_signal: Reconstructing regional value content to the sub-tier has always been an evidence problem, not a math problem: a part contains parts contain parts, from suppliers on three continents who will not disclose their cost build-ups, and CBP wants material-supplier invoices, bills of lading, production records and the cost analysis behind the RVC percentage. Doing that by hand costs more in professional-services diligence than any premium could justify, which is precisely why no one has ever been willing to insure the answer. Frontier long-context models changed the arithmetic in 2026 - twelve models from seven providers shipped in August alone, agentic jobs now run across ~53 turns and ~0.5B input tokens, and GPT-5.6 Luna sits at $0.20/$1.20 per million tokens after an 80% cut - so an underwriter can now afford to actually do the search on every part it insures, and to redo it continuously off the customer's ERP and purchase-order feed as suppliers change. The insurable object is determination error, which is fortuitous and diligence-sensitive, not the duty rate, which is neither.
cross.structural_signal: Two dated triggers landed seven weeks apart. On 2026-07-01 the United States declined to confirm extension of the USMCA for a further sixteen years; Mexico and Canada both supported extension, so the agreement now runs on annual joint reviews under Article 34.7.4 until it is extended or expires on 2036-07-01, with a US push for country-specific automotive content thresholds live into the September round and rules of origin widely expected to tighten. On 2026-06-03 the 'Strengthening Customs Enforcement' executive order directed CBP, within 90 days (2026-09-01), to revise every penalty mitigation standard to a floor of not less than 50% of the assessed penalty and to eliminate mitigation for repeat offenders; it also creates a 'good standing' threshold for import privileges and raises bond and tangible-domestic-asset requirements for importers of record. Underneath: CBP verification and audit activity is already up sharply in 2025-26, verification reaches back five years from entry, and a denied claim reliquidates at MFN plus stacked Section 232/301 duty plus interest plus penalties up to four times the unpaid duty. Meanwhile the comparable market proves the appetite - Euclid took a record 554 global tax-liability insurance submissions in 1Q26 against 418 in 1Q25 - and there is no equivalent product for customs.

ideas.buyer: The VP of trade compliance or CFO at a US mid-market manufacturer or importer with roughly $50M-$1B of annual entered value in USMCA-claimed or Section 232/301-exposed goods - auto parts, industrial machinery, electrical equipment, appliances - at one of two trigger moments: a CBP verification letter or Form 28/29 lands on a claim made up to five years ago, or they have to re-certify origin for the coming year under rules that now change annually and cannot be relied on from last year's file.
ideas.trigger: 2026-09-01, the executive order's 90-day deadline for CBP to floor penalty mitigation at 50% and eliminate it for repeat offenders - which converts a wrong origin call from a negotiable assessment into a fixed, compounding, five-year-deep liability and, via the new 'good standing' test, a threat to import privileges themselves.
ideas.why_incumbents_cant: Customs brokers are agents, not principals - their powers of attorney and terms explicitly push origin liability back to the importer, and they have no balance sheet to stand behind an answer. Trade-compliance software sells the determination as SaaS and will not put capital behind it: e2open, Descartes, Thomson Reuters ONESOURCE and Trade Insight AI's BOM-driven rules-of-origin engine all ship 'audit-ready' determinations with the risk left where it was, and YC has now funded four companies in the same layer (MarkIt, Trava, Pax, Forge), none of which takes the loss. Sureties write customs bonds that guarantee CBP gets paid; the importer remains fully liable to the surety, so the bond moves the collection risk, never the determination risk. And conventional insurers have reasoned themselves out of the market: the market view is that a duty bill is a known cost imposed by policy rather than a fortuitous event and the Government Action exclusion catches it - correct about the duty, and precisely wrong about the determination, which is the same insurable object as an uncertain tax position or a defect in title.

evidence_updates.note: The first of the two dated triggers landed on schedule. The 2026-06-03 'Strengthening Customs Enforcement' executive order's 90-day deadline is 2026-09-01: CBP's revised penalty mitigation standards, with a floor of not less than 50% of the assessed penalty and no mitigation for repeat offenders, take effect today. The 180-day provision - every importer of record must hold minimum tangible domestic assets or bonding, submit expanded disclosures and maintain 'good standing' - falls around 2026-11-30 and is the one that actually determines who is allowed to carry origin risk. Enforcement priorities are named as forced labour, misclassification, undervaluation and illegal transshipment; the middle two are exactly what an origin determination is about. Nothing here weakens the thesis; the next checkpoint is the November good-standing rule, which sets the capital bar for the underwriter itself.

ideas.summary: Capability credit for the defence sub-tier: a lender that underwrites a Tier-2/Tier-3 shop's ability to execute a specific qualified order by machine-reading the technical data package, the shop's machine base, its first-article and non-conformance history and the prime's schedule, then advances the pre-delivery working capital the shop needs to ramp - the $2M-$20M tickets that banks decline on reputational and compliance grounds and DoD's Office of Strategic Capital is too big to write.

cross.ai_signal: The underwriting question is an engineering judgement, not a credit score: can this forty-person shop actually make twelve thousand of this part, to this print, on this schedule. Answering it means reading a technical data package - drawings with GD&T, material and process specifications, special-process callouts - and mapping it against the shop's actual machine base and spindle availability, its historical first-pass yield on comparable features, its non-conformance and corrective-action record, its raw-material dependency, and the prime's delivery schedule. That is multimodal engineering reasoning over unstructured artefacts, and until 2026 no lender could put a manufacturing engineer on a $5M loan and still make money. Frontier multimodal models now form that judgement per deal at near-zero marginal cost, and every loan written adds a labelled promised-versus-delivered observation that nobody else is accumulating. This is deliberately the opposite of ts-0041, killed for underwriting structured GPU telemetry that needed no frontier model.
cross.structural_signal: Demand doubled and the sub-tier cannot finance the ramp. An Oliver Wyman survey of 160-plus US defence supply-chain companies in May 2026 puts the backlog on a path to roughly $900B and describes sub-tier suppliers as the structurally exposed segment with the least financial, operational and digital room to absorb the surge. In Europe, defence orders roughly doubled between 2025 and early 2026 while industrial production edged up only marginally, with limited advance payments to sub-tier suppliers named as a specific named constraint alongside skilled labour and fragmented certification. Banks decline defence SMEs on compliance and reputational grounds and for contracts that may be classified or unpredictable; up to half of lower-tier suppliers do not seek debt finance at all; and payment terms are typically on delivery or milestone, which is the wrong side of the cash-flow problem. Public capital is arriving above the gap, not in it: the FY26 NDAA expanded the Defense Industrial Base Fund and $20B of credit subsidy supports industrial-base lending, while OSC's own credit programme writes $10M-$150M tickets on government timelines. BENS states the thesis directly - private investors cannot underwrite what they cannot see - and Sequoia is steering roughly $10B toward reindustrialisation including defence manufacturing.

ideas.buyer: The owner of a US Tier-2 or Tier-3 defence machine shop, forging, castings house or electronics manufacturer with 20-200 employees, at the moment a prime offers or awards a multi-year or surge order worth two to five times current revenue and the shop needs $2M-$20M of pre-delivery working capital for material, tooling, a second shift and a machine - the exact ticket its bank declines, its factoring line cannot reach because there is no receivable yet, and OSC will not write because it is too small.
ideas.trigger: An awarded or offered surge/multi-year order the shop cannot fund to delivery, against a backlog heading to ~$900B and a European order book that doubled while production did not.
ideas.why_incumbents_cant: Banks carry explicit compliance and reputational exclusions on defence SMEs and have no mechanism to price execution risk on a print they cannot read. Factoring and purchase-order finance price the receivable, which exists only after delivery - the shop's problem is entirely upstream of that. Equipment lenders underwrite the resale value of the machine, not the order, so they fund the wrong asset in the wrong amount. JPMorgan's defence supply-chain inventory finance and the ECA/SBLC stack serve primes and Tier-1s with treasury departments. OSC starts at $10M and moves at government speed. And private credit funds decline for the reason BENS names: they cannot see inside a small shop, and the diligence to see inside costs more than the loan earns - which is exactly the cost that frontier models just collapsed.

ideas.summary: AI-native complex-rehab and home-mobility provider: enter through the repair backlog the PE-owned CRT duopoly will not economically serve - diagnose a broken power wheelchair remotely from photos, video and controller logs across a mixed-vintage multi-brand installed base, identify the exact part, dispatch a generalist technician or ship a self-fit kit - then use the earned patient relationship to take the new-chair sale, reconstructing the user's seated posture and function from consumer capture, generatively designing the seating and mobility configuration, and additively manufacturing it instead of assembling someone else's catalogue.

cross.ai_signal: Every hard part of this is multimodal reasoning that did not work at consumer capture quality until now. Fault diagnosis and part identification run against an installed base with no VIN system, no standard parts catalogue, mixed vintages and six manufacturers, from a user's phone photos, a video of the failure, and a controller error log - the same class of problem as reading a technical data package, applied to a device rather than a print. Configuration means reconstructing seated posture, pelvic and trunk alignment, anthropometry, pressure distribution and functional reach from ordinary video plus the clinical record, then generatively designing a seating geometry that satisfies clinical, anatomical and manufacturability constraints at once. And the money only arrives if a model writes the medical-necessity, face-to-face and repair-justification documentation that survives a Medicare or Medicare Advantage audit - the same rulebook-repair mechanism Candid Health is compounding at 190% YoY, pointed at a device claim rather than a professional claim.
cross.structural_signal: The US complex rehab technology market was $5.27B in 2024 and is forecast at $8.26B by 2034; the wider US home medical equipment base and the $44B-to-$90B global medical equipment repair services market sit behind it. Delivery of a custom power chair takes two to five months and roughly a third of prescribed mobility devices are not delivered before discharge. Repairs are worse: routine multi-month waits, 7-21 days just for Medicare Advantage paperwork approval, and a June 2026 bill from Rep. Pressley aimed specifically at streamlining wheelchair repair. The two PE-owned providers that hold the market - Numotion with 150 branches, 500+ ATPs and 1,000+ service techs, and National Seating & Mobility - carry the exact cost structure that makes fast repair unprofitable. Meanwhile three funded companies in twelve months (Hike Medical $22.5M, CustoMED $6M, Kalogon $5.75M in June 2026 with a Medicare-coded 3D-printed cushion line) have proven that AI-driven design plus additive manufacture plus owning the reimbursement is a working combination in adjacent custom-device categories.

ideas.source_pattern: Hike Medical raised $22.5M across seed and Series A (2026-08-25 roundup) for an integrated orthotics/prosthetics system combining software, insurance and 3D printing, naming a $100B addressable market; CustoMED raised $6M for AI-powered 3D-printed orthopaedic solutions; Kalogon raised $5.75M in June 2026 led by Enable Ventures and shipped a Medicare-coded 3D-printed variable-density lattice seating line. Three funded companies at the same job - collapse a craft-labour-bound, reimbursement-funded custom device category with AI design plus additive manufacture - inside twelve months. The documentation half is validated separately by the 2026 autonomous-RCM cluster: Candid Health's $120M Series D on 2026-07-22 at 190% YoY contracted run-rate growth, 180% net dollar retention and 200+ provider organisations, alongside Commure $70M, Adonis $40M, Anomaly $17M and Amperos $16M - more than $500M into machine-repaired claims in one year.
ideas.wedge: Channel conflict plus labour-model cannibalisation, on both halves. Numotion and NSM are distributors: their gross margin is the spread and the rebate on Permobil, Quantum and Sunrise product, so manufacturing their own additively-designed seating attacks the supplier relationships that are their P&L. Their service revenue is billed per visit against a field organisation of 500+ ATPs and 1,000+ technicians, so remote diagnosis and self-fit kits destroy the utilisation of the asset they own. Both are PE-owned and levered, which makes deliberate cannibalisation strictly harder to authorise, not easier. The manufacturers cannot follow either: Permobil already ships connected-chair remote diagnostics through MyPermobil, but it reaches only its own new chairs and it sells through Numotion and NSM, so going direct on service or on the sale would blow up its distribution. Kalogon, the nearest AI-native player, sells its cushions through Numotion and NSM - it is a supplier to the incumbents, not a replacement for them. Nobody in the chain is structurally free to serve the mixed-vintage installed base directly.
ideas.buyer: Initially the wheelchair user or their caregiver - an adult with a spinal cord injury, MS, ALS, muscular dystrophy or advanced cerebral palsy who depends on a Group 3 power chair - and behind them the payer (Medicare, Medicare Advantage, Medicaid or commercial) who is billed for the repair or the replacement. Later the referring seating clinic and the rehab hospital discharge planner, who currently have no provider they can promise a date to.
ideas.trigger: The chair breaks and the user is immobilised - a dead motor, a failed joystick or controller, a torn sling, a battery that will not hold - and the incumbent quotes weeks for an assessment visit before the paperwork even starts. Secondary trigger: the five-year Medicare replacement window opens, or a discharge planner needs a custom chair configured before a patient leaves inpatient rehab.
ideas.why_incumbents_cant: See wedge. Numotion and NSM would have to abandon per-visit field labour revenue, become a manufacturer against their own supplier rebates, and rebuild the intake around consumer capture - three simultaneous reversals, not a config change. Permobil's connected diagnostics cannot reach other manufacturers' chairs or older units and cannot be sold direct without destroying its channel. Kalogon and Matrix supply the incumbents. Hike Medical and CustoMED sit one device class over in orthotics, prosthetics and orthopaedic surgery, with different codes, a different credentialed clinician and a different fabrication process.
ideas.expansion_path: Repair on the CRT installed base (roughly $0.5-1B of US service spend, urgent, unserved, and the cheapest possible way to earn the patient) -> the new custom chair and seating sale on the same relationship, inside the $5.3B-to-$8.3B US CRT market -> all custom-fitted mobility and seating -> the full home medical equipment base an ageing and disabled population depends on, a ~$60B US category whose service layer alone is a $44B-to-$90B global market, and where every incumbent is a low-margin distributor of someone else's catalogue.

ideas.summary: Autonomous claim repair for workers' compensation and auto no-fault medical billing: hold every state's fee schedule and jurisdictional form rules and get the provider's bill paid first time, re-pointing the autonomous-RCM mechanism at the payer system that does not adjudicate under X12 commercial rules.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. DaisyBill already owns this exact square: daisyWizard applies the correct state fee schedule and calculates exact reimbursement per bill, it runs a proprietary network of electronic connections to comp payers and their clearinghouses, and it is used by thousands of US providers with a task-based workflow covering authorisation, payment and appeal. Medata and Mitchell hold the bill-review side. The segment is not underserved - it is served by a specialist that has been compounding the fee-schedule corpus for a decade.
ideas.source_pattern: Candid Health $120M Series D 2026-07-22, 190% YoY contracted run-rate growth, 180% NDR, 200+ provider organisations; >$500M into AI RCM in 2026 (Commure $70M, Adonis $40M, Anomaly $17M, Amperos $16M).

ideas.summary: Autonomous dental revenue cycle for DSOs: adjudicate CDT claims against per-payer rules with the clinical image attachment, in a market Candid's CMS-1500 professional-claim data model does not fit.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test, decisively. Overjet is the enterprise dental AI vendor with 300+ payer integrations for insurance verification, a payer layer that ties claims to clinical findings, named large-DSO logos, and published claims of 25% case-acceptance lift and 18x ROI; Zentist's Remit AI, VideaHealth, Ventus and Pearl fill the rest. DSOs with 50+ locations are already being sold 40% RCM cost reduction in 90 days. The image-attachment data-model argument that made this look structural is exactly the capability the occupants were founded on.
ideas.source_pattern: Candid Health $120M Series D and the 2026 autonomous-RCM cluster.

ideas.summary: Frontier re-adjudication of every claim paid on a self-funded employer's behalf, checked against the plan document and the network contract, sold to plan sponsors under their ERISA fiduciary exposure - the mirror image of provider-side autonomous RCM.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. Payment integrity is a mature multi-billion-dollar industry, not an opening: Cotiviti, Zelis, Machinify, Rialtic, 6 Degrees Health, ClaimInformatics and the TPA-side audit firms all sell exactly this, and the large carriers run their own. The ERISA fiduciary why-now is real but it changes who is anxious, not what product exists.
ideas.source_pattern: Candid Health $120M Series D and the 2026 autonomous-RCM cluster.

ideas.summary: Agentic provider enrolment and credentialing: unblock the 90-180 days of dead revenue before a new clinician can bill, the step upstream of every RCM product.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. Medallion, Verifiable, Certify, Andros and Modio are all funded and selling into this precise workflow, and the CAQH/PECOS/state-portal plumbing they have built is the entire moat. There is no structural block on anyone here - just a queue of competitors.
