ideas.summary: Emerald AI for industrial process loads: a model that predicts the metallurgical, yield and product-quality consequence of curtailing an arc furnace, electrolyser or chlor-alkali line, so a heavy industrial can sell firm flexibility and jump the interconnection queue.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the config-change and occupancy tests together. Industrial demand response is already the largest DR segment on earth at roughly 75 GW; Voltus manages 8.1 GW, delivered 816,000 MWh of grid relief in 2025 and paid its customers a record $240M; CPower forecasts VPPs as an imperative and, with Bentaus and Supermicro, already demonstrated AI compute responding to CAISO dispatch in under 20 milliseconds in February 2026. Adding a process-impact model is a feature these aggregators buy or build, not a company they cannot become.
ideas.source_pattern: Emerald AI $150M Series A at $1.05B on 2026-08-25 (DCVC and Energize, with NVIDIA, Siemens, GE Vernova, RWE, Aramco, Samsung, In-Q-Tel), five completed demonstrations, a 256-GPU cluster cut 25% for three hours in Phoenix, and the first-in-the-nation Flexible Load Interconnection Program with Silicon Valley Power.

ideas.summary: Firm-curtailment guarantee for flexible-load interconnection: stand between the utility and a large load, sell the utility a bankable megawatt of curtailability, and pay the penalty when the load fails to curtail.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the config-change test. Demand-response aggregators already carry performance obligations with penalties for non-delivery - that is what a capacity DR contract is - so the risk-bearing half is a pricing decision for Voltus or CPower rather than a new company. Emerald itself is selling 'verified, dispatchable flexibility' into the Silicon Valley Power programme, and the transferable-flexibility market this idea needs does not exist in any tariff yet.
ideas.source_pattern: Emerald AI $150M Series A at $1.05B, 2026-08-25.

ideas.summary: Adversarial assurance for the agent that has write access: continuously attack a deployed enterprise agent inside the customer's live systems and certify what it is allowed to do.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. This is the most heavily funded square in AI security right now - Zenity took $125M in the first half of August 2026, Patronus $50M for simulation worlds that stress-test agents, Arga Labs $10M from General Catalyst on 2026-08-26 for exactly the enterprise-complexity training and testing problem, and the agent-identity half belongs to Okta XAA, Microsoft Entra Agent ID, Astrix and Oasis. The pattern is real and the square is full.
ideas.source_pattern: Alice raised $140M in August 2026 with roughly $100M ARR, 500%+ growth over two years, and engagements with 8 of the 10 leading AI model labs.

ideas.summary: Post-hoc forensic reconstruction of what a deployed AI system actually did, to an evidentiary standard, sold to plaintiffs, regulators and insurers as the EU AI Act penalty regime bites.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the segment-viability test. The buyer is episodic - a matter, not a subscription - the delivery is expert services with a courtroom-shaped cost structure, and nothing compounds between engagements because each system, log format and legal theory is bespoke. It also duplicates the shape of ts-0133 in the operator's own book, which already covers evidence-constrained reconstruction for litigation.
ideas.source_pattern: Alice ~$100M ARR; the EU AI Act penalty regime and GPAI enforcement powers effective 2026-08-02; California's chatbot transparency law effective 2026-08-02.

ideas.summary: Independent adversarial assurance lab for AI agents given supervisory control of chemical, refining, water and power processes, producing the IEC 61511 / ISA-84 safety case a non-deterministic controller cannot otherwise get.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed as a duplicate of the operator's own book. This is the third re-point of the same shape already held as ts-0031 (behavioural certification for robot foundation-model policies) and ts-0032 (test-and-evaluation assurance harness for DoD autonomous systems), both still watching. Generating a fourth instance of an idea already sitting unacted-on twice is template-following, not discovery.
ideas.source_pattern: The August 2026 agent-assurance cluster: Alice $140M at ~$100M ARR, Patronus $50M, Arga Labs $10M.

ideas.summary: HappyRobot's operational voice-agent mechanism narrowed to a vertical where the call is itself a regulated legal act - collections, emergency dispatch, or utility outage handling.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the config-change test at the top and the occupancy test underneath. HappyRobot has explicitly named insurance, energy, telecoms and airlines as its expansion path off this round, so 'a vertical they have not reached' is a roadmap item rather than a structural block. The genuinely regulated niches are already held: Skit.ai, Prodigal and TrueAccord in collections; Prepared, Carbyne and RapidSOS in 911; Assort Health and Hello Patient in clinical.
ideas.source_pattern: HappyRobot $150M Series C at $1.2B on 2026-08-04, revenue up more than fivefold since its Series B, net dollar retention above 150%, 150+ enterprise customers including DHL, Kuehne+Nagel, Naturgy, Repsol and Uber, and one customer expanding tenfold in a year.

ideas.summary: AI-native value-based enablement for the independent rural practice: take the risk contract on an existing rural physician's panel and supply the documentation, risk-capture and care-management labour that makes a small panel profitable, instead of building clinics.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test, immediately. Aledade is this company at national scale and is explicitly rural-weighted, with thousands of independent practices under management, alongside Privia, agilon, Evolent, Pearl Health and Wellvana. The AI layer is what all of them are now adding; it is not a wedge into a market they cannot reach.
ideas.source_pattern: Hopscotch Primary Care $53M Series D (2026-08-18 roundup): 15,000+ rural patients, 90%+ retention, profitable in one region.

ideas.summary: Driverless paratransit and non-emergency medical transportation: apply bounded-ODD autonomy to the fixed, geofenced, catastrophically expensive trips that transit agencies are legally obliged to provide at $40-70 each.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the segment-viability test and the ts-0213 lesson. The binding constraint is not the driving - it is a human physically securing a wheelchair and providing door-through-door assistance, which the statute effectively requires and no autonomous vehicle supplies, so removing the driver removes the wrong cost. May Mobility and Waymo are already running accessible AV pilots with transit agencies on top of that.
ideas.source_pattern: Gatik $200M Series D on 2026-08-25 with $600M+ contracted revenue and 85,000 fully driverless orders completed.

ideas.summary: Cross-silicon numerical-equivalence certification: prove that a model deployed on inference ASICs, GPUs and hyperscaler accelerators behaves identically, for regulated buyers who cannot accept silicon-dependent output.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test and buyer concentration. The compiler and quantisation stack that owns this - MLIR, ONNX, the vendor toolchains and MLPerf - is where the work already happens, and the buyer set is roughly a dozen chip vendors and four hyperscalers, all of whom treat numerics validation as core internal engineering rather than something to purchase.
ideas.source_pattern: Etched $700M growth round on 2026-08-18 with $1B+ in customer contracts and Jane Street as a customer; Velaura AI $110M Series A engaged with three of the four largest cloud providers.

ideas.summary: Underwritten packaging-compliance determination for the EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation, whose core obligations became applicable on 2026-08-12: recyclability grade, recycled content and modulated EPR fee per SKU per member state.

Extended-producer-responsibility compliance is a mature service industry - Ecoveritas, Lorax EPI, Reconomy, Source Intelligence and Assent on the software and filing side, SGS, Intertek and UL on the testing and certification side - and the PPWR gives all of them a well-signposted product extension they have been building toward since February 2025. The determination half also restates ts-0281 (origin of record) one regulation over.

ideas.summary: Franchisee-side AI operator: the AI chief marketing and technology officer for the multi-unit franchisee - local demand generation inside brand constraints, unit-level P&L truth, and a machine-read of the franchise agreement, operations manual and mandated-supplier price files to establish what the franchisor is actually permitted to charge.

FRANdata/IFA 2026: 19.3% of franchisees control 58.8% of all franchise locations.

The buyable halves are all taken: SOCi and Rallio own localised marketing for franchise units at scale, Operandio and Delightree own multi-unit franchise operations, GrowthFactor (from $200/mo, self-serve) owns franchise unit-economics and site analytics, and MarginEdge, xtraCHEF/Toast and Buyers Edge Platform already do invoice line-item price-compliance auditing against contracted price files. The one genuinely empty seat - representing the franchisee against the franchisor - is empty for a reason that blocks us rather than the leader: that demand routes to lawyers and forensic accountants as an episodic matter, not a subscription, which is the ts-0001 and ts-0291 failure again. Owner's inability to follow is real and irrelevant, because Owner is not the leader in this segment.

ideas.summary: Closed-loop silicon validation service for AI chip-design agents: standing shuttle capacity plus an automated bring-up and test harness, so a design agent can get real measured silicon back in weeks instead of two quarters - the Adaptyv mechanism moved from proteins to transistors.
ideas.source_pattern: Adaptyv Bio $40M Series A on 2026-08-28 (Highland Europe, with YC doubling down): 100+ customers including Roche, Novo Nordisk, Chai Discovery and Boltz, lab throughput up over 5x and revenue roughly 10x in a year, DNA synthesis brought in-house. The mechanism: AI design outran physical validation, so the scarce good is experiments per week and whoever industrialises the loop owns the resulting dataset.

ideas.trigger: Missing a foundry shuttle window, which costs 8-12 weeks of schedule.

ChipFoundry already sells AI-powered custom SoC design and tapeout with 2026 shuttle reservations; Cognichip, ChipAgents and Agentrys hold the agentic design layer; Cadence shipped agentic chip-design tools on 2026-02-10 and Siemens demonstrated self-verifying agent flows gated on Calibre and Questa at DAC 2026; GlobalFoundries, TSMC and SMIC run their own MPW shuttle programmes. The loop is being closed by the incumbents and by funded startups simultaneously.

ideas.summary: Adversarial engagement agents for the enterprise: when a caller or emailer fails verification at the IT help desk or in a vendor payment-change thread, do not hang up - hand them to an agent that plays the credulous employee, consumes the attacker's scarce human attention and harvests their infrastructure and tradecraft live.
ideas.source_pattern: Apate.AI A$11.4M seed on 2026-08-31 (Lobby Capital, OIF, Investible) with a US move. Deployed inside Commonwealth Bank: 2.5M+ autonomous conversations with threat actors, 250,000+ intelligence artifacts, roughly 600,000 fraudsters engaged monthly, and bank and telco deployments across Australia, the UK, South Africa and South East Asia.
ideas.buyer: CISO or fraud lead at a mid-market or enterprise company facing vendor email compromise and help-desk social engineering.
ideas.trigger: A failed help-desk identity challenge, or a flagged bank-detail change on a live invoice thread.
ideas.wedge: Apate's product engages inbound consumer-scam traffic on behalf of banks and telcos; deceiving an attacker from a corporate identity inside a customer's ITSM and identity stack is a different product, a different integration and a CISO sales motion.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the config-change test and then by the venture-scale gate. Netcraft already ships AI-powered preemptive domain disruption plus conversational engagement with attackers, and Abnormal owns the email plane where vendor email compromise - now 61% of all business email compromise - actually lands; adding engagement to an existing detection product is a feature decision, not a second company. The harder objection is the $1B gate: cost-imposition security has repeatedly failed to become a standalone category (Illusive, Attivo, TrapX all sold cheap or died) because no CISO carries a budget line for wasting an attacker's time.

ideas.summary: Retracement engine plus licensed survey firm: an AI-native land surveying company that reconstructs where a property boundary legally is - reading the deed chain, adjoining deeds, plats, prior surveys and found monument evidence, applying the legal hierarchy of evidence, and reconciling the result against LiDAR and photogrammetric field capture - then stamps and delivers the survey itself, taking the professional liability rather than selling software to the firms that carry it.

cross.ai_signal: Boundary retracement is the rare professional judgment that is simultaneously a long-context legal-document problem and a geometric constraint problem, and neither half worked before frontier models. The machine must read a chain of title and the deeds of every adjoiner - often two centuries of metes-and-bounds prose with calls to trees, stones and dead neighbours - reconcile conflicting descriptions under the surveyor's evidentiary hierarchy (senior rights, then monuments, then courses and distances, then area), and then solve the resulting constraints against measured field evidence: found pins, fences, occupation lines, and a point cloud. Transfyr's $25M seed on 2026-08-26 is the same mechanism one domain over - multimodal models turning undocumented physical reality into a machine-readable record. Nothing in the incumbent stack (Trimble Business Center, Carlson, Leica) does the reasoning; it does the drafting after a licensed human has already done the thinking.
cross.structural_signal: The profession is collapsing on a demand spike. US licensed surveyors fell from 56,200 in 2010 to 47,770 in 2020; average age of a licensee is 57-60; 94% of US construction firms reported difficulty hiring qualified surveyors in 2024. Meanwhile developers are on track to add a record 43.4 GW of new utility-scale solar in 2026 (+60% on 2025), the data-centre buildout is siting at unprecedented rate, and BEAD is putting $42.5B of fibre into the ground - every one of those projects needs boundary, topographic and ALTA/NSPS work first. On top of that a dated trigger: the 2026 ALTA/NSPS Minimum Standard Detail Requirements took effect 2026-02-23, added the Table A Item 20 encroachment summary, and moved adjoining-deed research onto the surveyor - the title insurer no longer has to supply adjoiner deeds - adding 2-4 hours of exactly the research labour a model removes. Global land surveying is a ~$14.17B market in 2026. Private equity has spent five years rolling up survey firms, which is a labour-arbitrage answer to a licensed-labour shortage and cannot remove the hours.

ideas.source_pattern: The 'agent-native professional services' cluster confirmed by the YC Summer 2026 batch (235 companies, Demo Day 2026-09-10, industrials up from 12.8% to 23%): multiple startups positioning as AI-run accounting firms, law practices and insurance carriers rather than as tools for them, alongside funded instances outside the batch - Casey and Fernstone as AI-native commercial insurance brokerages, Last Accounting Company as a full-stack AI accounting firm where agents do the work and a certified accountant signs. Separately, Transfyr launched on 2026-08-26 with a $25M seed led by General Catalyst (Lux, Breakout, SV Angel; angels including David Baker, Chris Re and Kevin Weil), founded by Ginkgo's former head of AI and the founding director of ARPA-H, proving that sensor stacks plus multimodal models can capture skilled physical work that never gets written down. Mechanism: the firm itself - licence, liability and deliverable - is the product, with agents doing the expert work and a much thinner layer of licensed humans signing.
ideas.wedge: Channel conflict at the vendors, and hourly-billing economics at the practitioners. Trimble, Hexagon/Leica, Topcon, Carlson and Bentley sell instruments, dealer services and per-seat CAD to the ~10,000 US survey firms; delivering finished stamped surveys would put them in competition with their entire customer base and their dealer channel, and would require carrying professional liability and PLS licensure in fifty states that an instrument maker has no basis for. The survey firms cannot follow either: they are 3-8 person owner-operated practices billing the licensed hours that this removes, with no capacity to build multimodal retracement models - and the PE roll-ups buying them are levered labour-arbitrage vehicles whose thesis is utilisation, not elimination. Title insurers are structurally excluded on the other side: they deliberately except survey matters from coverage precisely so they never carry boundary risk, so becoming the surveyor reverses their own risk posture.
ideas.buyer: The party who needs a stamped survey on a clock and cannot get one: a solar, storage or data-centre development manager holding a portfolio of sites; a commercial real estate lender or title agency ordering ALTA/NSPS surveys for closings; a national homebuilder or fibre builder. All of them buy in volume from one relationship, which is why the first ten are reachable without a retail motion.
ideas.trigger: A closing, permit, interconnection application or construction start is gated on a survey and the local firm quotes six to ten weeks. Secondary trigger: a title commitment raises a boundary or encroachment exception that has to be resolved before funding, now under the 2026 ALTA/NSPS standard that puts adjoiner-deed research on the surveyor.
ideas.why_incumbents_cant: See wedge. Trimble and Hexagon would have to compete with every customer and dealer they have and take on fifty-state licensure and E&O. The survey firms would have to delete their own billable hours. The PE roll-ups can buy firms but not remove the licensed labour that is the constraint. And the nearest thing to an occupant found on search is a single Georgia one-man licensed practice using LLM agents in its own back office - no funded player is niching this way.
ideas.expansion_path: Volume boundary, topographic and ALTA/NSPS work for energy, data-centre, fibre and CRE buyers (a reachable slice of a ~$14B global, ~$12-13B US surveying services market with a collapsing labour supply) -> construction staking and as-built verification on the same sites -> the accumulated by-product: a machine-readable national boundary graph carrying every deed call, found monument and resolved conflict, which is the geometric record nobody owns and which title, permitting, parcel data and land-rights products all currently approximate.

ideas.summary: The government-contract ledger: an AI-native accounting system of record that makes a twelve-person defence-tech company DCAA-adequate from day one - judging the allowability of every transaction against FAR Part 31 and the contract, maintaining segregated direct and indirect cost pools and compliant timekeeping, producing provisional billing rates and the incurred-cost submission, and standing behind the pre-award accounting system survey - instead of the outsourced govcon CPA firm that does it by hand today.

cross.ai_signal: The product is a ledger whose posting rules are natural-language regulation. Every transaction has to be judged against FAR Part 31 allowability, the contract's own terms, CAS where it applies, and the company's disclosed accounting practice - then allocated to the right direct contract or indirect pool, because that allocation is what determines billable revenue. Then the same corpus has to produce the provisional rate proposal and the incurred-cost submission and answer a DCAA auditor's questions about them five years later. That is exactly the class of work the 2026 AI-native ERP cluster proved machines can now do on a general ledger, pointed at a rulebook rather than at revenue recognition.
cross.structural_signal: Defence and dual-use venture investment exceeded $15B in 2025 and is pacing past $18B in 2026, cumulative funding across the top 60+ defence startups is over $33B, and the YC Summer 2026 batch alone has eight defence companies. Every one of them hits the same wall: a DoD SBIR Phase II - typically $1.0-$1.5M - is a federal cost-type contract carrying the same accounting standards as a $50M prime, and DCAA runs a pre-award accounting system survey (SF 1408) before the award. Today that is solved by hiring a fractional govcon CPA firm - Team 80, Jameson, Redstone GCI, Cherry Bekaert, Amerifusion - at hourly rates, or by buying Deltek Costpoint, whose realistic entry cost is a six-figure implementation through a VAR channel. Deltek was taken out at $2.8B in 2016; Unanet, JAMIS, PROCAS and BigTime split the rest.

ideas.source_pattern: Rillet raised a $100M Series C at a $1B valuation on 2026-08-19 led by Iconiq (Sequoia, a16z, Bain Capital Ventures, Oak HC/FT, Battery, FirstMark, Scale, Creandum), its third round in twelve months and $200M+ total: 600+ customers, ARR doubled in the last three months, and customers including Mercor - which is scaling past $2B ARR with a finance team of three. Two more funded companies are at the identical job: Campfire ($100M+, Accel and YC) and DualEntry ($90M Series A, Lightspeed and Khosla), inside a tracked field of 53 AI-native accounting and finance-ops companies. Mechanism: the general ledger can now be constructed and closed by agents reading source transactions, so the accounting system of record - not a tool sitting beside it - is winnable.
ideas.wedge: Two structurally blocked leaders, on different axes. Deltek is blocked on economics and channel: Costpoint's revenue model is a six-figure implementation sold and delivered through implementation partners, with the complexity itself as the product - an AI-native system that makes compliance automatic destroys both the partner channel and the seat count, and Deltek is PE-owned and levered, which makes deliberate cannibalisation harder to authorise rather than easier. The govcon CPA firms are blocked on their own business model: their revenue is billable partner and staff hours, their liability model is a partner signature on an engagement, and neither survives being productised into a system that takes standing responsibility for a client's accounting-system adequacy. And the AI-native ERP leaders - Rillet, Campfire, DualEntry - cannot follow with a config change: FAR allowability, indirect pools, incurred-cost submissions and a government audit posture are a second ledger and a second product, sold to a buyer their entire go-to-market is not pointed at.
ideas.buyer: The founder or first finance hire at a defence or dual-use hardware startup - twelve to eighty people, venture-backed, no govcon controller - at the moment a cost-type federal award is in reach. Widening from there to the small and mid-sized businesses that make up the long tail of federal contracting.
ideas.trigger: The pre-award accounting system survey. A DoD SBIR Phase II, an OTA converting to a cost-type follow-on, or a first cost-reimbursable prime or subcontract - at which point the company must demonstrate segregated cost pools, compliant timekeeping and exclusion of unallowable costs before the money can be obligated, on a timetable that will not accommodate a Costpoint implementation.
ideas.why_incumbents_cant: See wedge: Deltek's price floor and VAR channel, the CPA firms' hourly-billing and partner-liability model, and a second-product problem for the AI-native ERP leaders. Search surfaced no AI-native occupant of this segment - only the legacy vendors (Deltek, Unanet, JAMIS, PROCAS, BigTime, XTIVIA) and the CPA firms selling the work as labour.
ideas.expansion_path: Defence-tech startups at their first cost-type award (small in dollars, but the highest-growth cohort in the economy and a cohort that compounds into large contractors) -> the long tail of small and mid-sized federal contractors currently priced out of Costpoint -> up-market displacement of Costpoint and Unanet in a category whose leader was worth $2.8B a decade ago -> the adjacent govcon back office the ledger already holds the data for: pricing and proposal cost volumes, subcontractor flow-downs, closeouts and audit defence, across a federal contracting economy obligating well over $700B a year.

ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. Invisible AI and Retrocausal already sell camera-based observation of manual assembly work; Tulip ($1.3B), Augmentir and L2L hold the frontline-operations layer. The re-point is the obvious one and it was made years ago.

ideas.summary: AI-native Phase I environmental site assessment firm: generate the ASTM E1527 report - historical aerials, Sanborn maps, regulatory database review, site reconnaissance - and sign it as the Environmental Professional, taking the deliverable rather than selling tools to consultants.
ideas.source_pattern: The 'agent-native professional services' cluster confirmed by the YC Summer 2026 batch (235 companies, Demo Day 2026-09-10, industrials up from 12.8% to 23%): multiple startups positioning as AI-run accounting firms, law practices and insurance carriers rather than as tools for them, alongside funded instances outside the batch - Casey and Fernstone as AI-native commercial insurance brokerages, Last Accounting Company as a full-stack AI accounting firm where agents do the work and a certified accountant signs. Separately, Transfyr launched on 2026-08-26 with a $25M seed led by General Catalyst (Lux, Breakout, SV Angel; angels including David Baker, Chris Re and Kevin Weil), founded by Ginkgo's former head of AI and the founding director of ARPA-H, proving that sensor stacks plus multimodal models can capture skilled physical work that never gets written down. Mechanism: the firm itself - licence, liability and deliverable - is the product, with agents doing the expert work and a much thinner layer of licensed humans signing.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: LightBox and EDR sell the historical-records data to every consultant, so becoming the consultant would destroy their channel.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the config-change test. The consultancies are already doing it themselves - EKI publishes its own AI Phase I programme, LightBox is shipping AI into the workflow it already owns the data for, and generic document tooling (V7 Go) covers the extraction. Unlike boundary retracement, the Phase I is report assembly against a checklist rather than a defensible judgment, so there is no reasoning moat for a new firm to hold.

ideas.wedge: Attempted: the same shape as the surviving survey idea - a licensed stamped deliverable, fragmented hourly-billing incumbents, and a demand wave from the buildout.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. A purpose-built platform (GeoAI) already spans boring-log ingestion through subsurface modelling to PE-sealed design reports, and GroundedAI raised $2M in July 2026 for AI subsurface understanding in tunnelling. The workflow layer is taken and the remaining moat is thin.

ideas.summary: AI-native ERP for nonprofits and grant-funded organisations: fund accounting, restricted net assets, grant tracking and Uniform Guidance compliance built machine-first.
ideas.source_pattern: Rillet raised a $100M Series C at a $1B valuation on 2026-08-19 led by Iconiq (Sequoia, a16z, Bain Capital Ventures, Oak HC/FT, Battery, FirstMark, Scale, Creandum), its third round in twelve months and $200M+ total: 600+ customers, ARR doubled in the last three months, and customers including Mercor - which is scaling past $2B ARR with a finance team of three. Two more funded companies are at the identical job: Campfire ($100M+, Accel and YC) and DualEntry ($90M Series A, Lightspeed and Khosla), inside a tracked field of 53 AI-native accounting and finance-ops companies. Mechanism: the general ledger can now be constructed and closed by agents reading source transactions, so the accounting system of record - not a tool sitting beside it - is winnable.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: restricted funds and grant-level accounting looked like a ledger primitive the corporate AI-native ERPs would need a second product for.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the config-change test. Sage Intacct serves both corporate and nonprofit customers off one dimensional general ledger, and Intuit Enterprise Suite shipped fund accounting, grant tracking and multi-entity consolidation into a general product - which proves that restriction and fund tracking are a dimension, not a second ledger. Any of Rillet, Campfire or DualEntry could add the dimensions; the sector's shrinking budgets and Blackbaud's incumbency make it worse, not better.

ideas.summary: Competence as infrastructure for supervised practice: machine-assess an internationally trained physician's actual clinical competence, place them with a rural hospital or federally qualified health centre under the new state provisional-licence pathways, then run the two-year supervised period - continuously evaluating real clinical work against the six core competencies and producing the board-facing attestation record - taking the employment and the supervision liability rather than selling software to a credentialing office.

cross.ai_signal: Supervision is the constraint, and supervision is exactly what a model can now manufacture. The statutes require 'continuous observation and progressive assessment by board-certified physicians' over two years - a rural hospital with one supervising physician cannot produce that, and no amount of software scheduling fixes it. Frontier models change the arithmetic: every note, order, referral, imaging interpretation, prescription and patient message a provisional physician generates can be read against the six ACGME core competencies (patient care, medical knowledge, practice-based learning, interpersonal and communication skills, professionalism, systems-based practice), scored, and escalated to a human supervisor only where the evidence is ambiguous or adverse - so one board-certified supervisor's judgment reaches twenty physicians instead of one. The peer-reviewed ground is already laid: npj Digital Medicine published multimodal-AI competency assessment with anomaly detection in 2025, and Science published a frontier model's performance on physician reasoning tasks. The second AI-native half is the entry gate - the statutes accept a 'comprehensive Board-approved clinical assessment' in place of a US residency, and generating and scoring high-fidelity clinical simulations at scale is a model problem, not a testing-centre problem. Neither half was buildable two years ago.
cross.structural_signal: A statutory wave with dated triggers and no vendor. 27 US states now have provisional licensure pathways for internationally trained physicians and 13 have fully implemented them and are accepting applications - Arkansas, Colorado, Florida, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Minnesota, Oklahoma, Tennessee, Texas, Washington and Wisconsin - with most implementations landing in late 2025 and early 2026. Washington's SB 5185 created a clinical experience graduate pilot programme effective 2026-06-11 requiring two years of consecutive supervised practice plus satisfactory clinical evaluations. Illinois issued its first IMG Limited Licence and has 24 further applicants under review, and is standing up a Clinical Readiness Program with the Department of Public Health and the Governor's Office of New Americans to match qualified IMGs with sponsoring healthcare organisations. The implementation gap is visible in the numbers: a wave of laws, and Illinois has issued four licences. The binding constraints are the ones nobody sells - a board-acceptable competence assessment, and a sponsoring employer willing to supervise for two years. Behind it: a projected US shortfall of roughly 86,000 physicians by 2036, and an estimated 65,000+ internationally trained physicians already in the US not practising medicine. The expansion market is worse and larger - first-time NCLEX-RN pass rates for internationally educated nurses run about 47% against 87% for US-educated nurses, which is a competence-readiness gap, not a paperwork gap.

ideas.source_pattern: Mercor: less than three years old, crossed $2B in gross annualised revenue as of June 2026, four months after crossing $1B, by matching domain experts to AI labs. Mechanism: frontier models can now screen, match and continuously grade a human being's domain competence cheaply and reliably enough to support a labour business whose economics no human recruiting organisation could reach. Corroborating cluster: the YC Summer 2026 batch (235 companies, Demo Day 2026-09-10) contains an explicit 'vertical-specific AI services - professional services replacement in regulated industries' cohort, and the 2026-09-03 run found the same shape funded outside the batch. This entry carries the Mercor mechanism, not the Mercor product.
ideas.wedge: Four separate structural blocks, one per plausible follower. (1) ECFMG/Intealth is the incumbent assessor of internationally trained physicians and is in direct innovator's-dilemma conflict: its entire product is ECFMG Certification feeding the residency Match, and these state pathways exist precisely to bypass the residency requirement - building the supervised-practice assessment would legitimise the bypass and cannibalise the funnel. It is also a nonprofit credential-verification body with no placement capability, no employment vehicle and no rural-employer relationships. (2) GME evaluation software (MedHub, New Innovations) is architecturally built around an ACGME-accredited residency programme with a designated institutional official, program directors and milestone committees; a critical-access hospital or FQHC has none of those objects, so serving this segment is a different product sold to a different buyer, not a configuration. (3) Physician staffing firms (AMN, CHG, Avant) bill an hourly or placement markup and deliberately do not take competence-attestation liability - that sits with the hospital's medical staff office - so following means converting a markup business into a liability-bearing assessor. (4) The states themselves are running the matching out of government offices; they are the customer and the partner, and they have no assessment instrument and no supply of sponsoring employers.
ideas.buyer: The chief medical officer or medical staff leader at a rural hospital, critical-access hospital or federally qualified health centre in one of the 13 states with a live pathway, holding a physician vacancy that has failed a full recruiting cycle. Second buyer, and the fastest route to the first ten: the state programmes themselves - Illinois's Clinical Readiness Program (IDFPR, Department of Public Health, Governor's Office of New Americans) and Washington's CEGPP - which need sponsoring employers and an assessment instrument and currently have neither.
ideas.trigger: A vacancy that has gone unfilled through a recruiting cycle and is costing locum rates, or a newly effective state pathway that has applicants queued and no sponsoring employers - Illinois has 24 applicants under review against four licences issued.
ideas.why_incumbents_cant: See wedge. The occupancy search found no funded company selling competence assessment or supervised-practice attestation for these pathways: the field is state statutes, a nonprofit advocacy directory (WeAreDocs), university research groups, and a law firm publishing guidance on how to find a sponsor. The nearest adjacent players - ECFMG/Intealth, MedHub, AMN, Avant - are each blocked by a different one of the four structural reasons above. In the nurse expansion the picture is the same: TruMerit/CGFNS does credential evaluation and the rest of the field is exam prep and checklists.
ideas.expansion_path: Provisional-pathway physicians in the 13 live states, where the beachhead is deliberately small and the state is actively recruiting a solution -> internationally educated nurses, a far larger annual flow with a 47% first-attempt NCLEX pass rate that is a remediation-and-assessment market before it is a placement market -> allied health and advanced-practice supervision, which is a statutory requirement in most states -> becoming the employer: an AI-native medical group that employs the physicians, supplies the supervision, carries the malpractice and contracts them into rural hospitals and FQHCs, which captures the clinician's economic output rather than a software seat, against a projected 86,000-physician shortfall by 2036 -> the accumulated asset is the only dataset linking real clinical work product to verified downstream competence outcomes, which is the substrate for every future licensure, re-entry and privileging decision - including, eventually, attesting to the competence of AI-supervised practice itself.

ideas.summary: Embedded licensed installation: a single entity holding electrical and mechanical contractor licences in every jurisdiction that any hardware brand - heat pump, battery, EV charger, generator, grid-interactive water heater - can call to sell its product 'installed', with models doing remote scoping from photos, NEC load calculations, per-authority-having-jurisdiction permit determination and crew dispatch.
ideas.source_pattern: Light raised a $46M Series A led by Matrix (Activate Capital; Spark, Mischief, Gigascale, MCJ, BoxGroup returning) plus a credit facility taking the package past $100M, announced 2026-09-01. Traction: every new electricity brand entering the Texas market in the first half of 2026 launched on Light, up from more than 70% in 2025; customers include Palmetto, GoodLeap and Emporia. Mechanism: hold the licence, the wholesale procurement, the commodity risk, the billing and the per-jurisdiction regulatory filings, and expose the whole regulated entity as an API so any brand can sell a regulated product - newly viable because the per-state regulatory back office is now machine-runnable by a small team.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: contractor licensure looked like the same licence-as-API shape in a market where hardware brands visibly want to sell installed outcomes and cannot hold fifty states of licensure themselves.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test on the first search. Treehouse is a software-enabled electrification installation platform with $26.6M raised (Series A led with Eaton, MassMutual Ventures, CarMax, Holman, Virta) that explicitly 'provides the electrical expertise and scaled fulfilment capabilities required to install equipment' nationwide, and is already partnered with Elephant Energy for HVAC design and installation. Qmerit holds the referral-network position across EV charging and home electrical. The segment is not empty; it has a funded incumbent doing the identical job.

ideas.summary: Regulated-entity-as-a-service pointed off electricity: hold the licence, the balance sheet and the per-jurisdiction filings for a different regulated retail market and sell it as an API to brands - tested across direct-to-consumer alcohol shipping, home care, wholesale energy market participation, service contracts and warranties, embedded clinical entities, embedded pharmacy, customs brokerage and federal contract vehicles.
ideas.source_pattern: Light, as above: $46M Series A plus a $100M+ credit facility on 2026-09-01, and 100% of new Texas retail electricity brands in H1 2026 launched on it.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: the mechanism generalises cleanly on paper - any regulated retail market with a per-jurisdiction licence, heavy filing burden and brands that want to sell the product without becoming the regulated entity.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test, seven narrowings deep, and it is worth recording as a mechanism with no openings rather than a single idea. Every regulated retail market tested already has a named licence-as-API incumbent: direct-to-consumer alcohol (ShipCompliant/Sovos, Park Street, LibDib), home care (Honor operates as the platform behind agencies), wholesale market participation for distributed assets (Leap sells market access as an API; Voltus, CPower, Enel X), service contracts and warranties (Extend, Cover Genius, After Inc.), embedded clinical entities (Wheel, SteadyMD, OpenLoop), embedded pharmacy (Truepill, Alto, Medvantx), importer of record and customs (Passport, Zonos - and the ledger's own ts-0271 kill), and federal contract vehicles (Carahsoft, Immix, and Palantir FedStart doing precisely 'sell to government from inside our accreditation'). Embedded finance, the origin of the pattern, is denser still (Unit, Synctera, sponsor-bank networks). Meanwhile the two adjacent markets Light itself would take next - natural gas, and new deregulated states - are config changes for Light.

ideas.summary: Model-underwritten competence for the skilled construction trades: assess electricians, pipefitters, millwrights and welders by machine and supply them to the contractors ramping crews on data-centre, fab and shipyard megaprojects, where the binding constraint is qualified labour rather than capital.
ideas.source_pattern: Mercor: under three years old, $2B gross annualised revenue as of June 2026, four months after $1B, on the mechanism that models can now screen, match and grade human domain competence at a cost no human recruiting organisation can match. Corroborated by the demand side: 90% of data-centre operators name staffing shortages as a critical constraint on build and expansion in 2026, ahead of power and land.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: Mercor's supply is remote, digital and 1099 and it assesses competence from written and verbal work samples; trade labour is physical, licensed per state, union-jurisdictional and needs employment rather than gig - which looked like a second company Mercor would never build.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. Skillit does exactly this - proprietary trade-specific assessments across electricians, pipefitters, millwrights, welders and eleven other trades, hundreds of data points per worker, a taxonomised view of skilled construction labour, and sourcing through hiring, training and evaluation - with $13.6M raised and, in June 2026, strategic equity from Suffolk Technologies and a partnership with DPR Construction, which is distribution into precisely the megaproject contractors this idea would have to sell to. Workrise holds the adjacent energy-trades position.

ideas.summary: AI-native financial operating system for owner-operators whose income is a share of a harvest rather than an invoice - commercial fishing crews and vessel owners on the lay system, and the share-based harvest businesses whose money model fits neither QuickBooks nor an AI-native corporate ledger.
ideas.source_pattern: Ambrook: $30M Series B led by Lachy Groom with Thomson Reuters Ventures, Thrive, Field Ventures and Cameron Ventures, taking total funding to $59M, announced early August 2026. Traction: roughly 2,500 customers in July 2025 to more than 8,000 across all 50 states, grown by word of mouth inside the farm community, now including 1,000+ trucking businesses and hundreds of general contractors and property managers. Mechanism: an AI-native financial system that reads source transactions and produces enterprise-level profitability for physical-operation businesses that accounting software never served, distributed without a sales team.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: a share-of-production income model is a genuinely different ledger primitive, not a category setting, so it looked like the one narrowing Ambrook could not represent.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the venture-scale gate, before the occupancy test was needed. US commercial fishing is roughly 35,000 documented vessels against about $6B in annual ex-vessel value; even total capture of the segment's software spend is a rounding error against the $1B+ bar, and there is no adjacent expansion that is not simply Ambrook's own horizontal path. The config-change test would have killed it too: Ambrook has expanded from agriculture into trucking, contracting and property management in thirteen months by word of mouth, which is the definition of a leader that can follow.

ideas.summary: Conversational-native regulated services for the US Latino diaspora beyond money: the paperwork life - immigration renewals and petitions, tax filing, benefits enrolment, bill and medical-bill disputes - delivered in Spanish inside WhatsApp by agents, sold to a population that will not download an app and currently buys these services from lawyers, notarios and storefront preparers.
ideas.source_pattern: Felix Pago: $200M Series C at a $1.4B valuation on 2026-09-01, co-led by a16z ($87M equity) and General Catalyst's Customer Value Fund ($113M debt), with QED, Castle Island, Switch, Contour and Endeavor Catalyst. Traction: $8B+ processed, 6M+ people served across 11 Latin American markets since 2022, with most new users arriving by word of mouth rather than paid marketing - and a structural tailwind from the new US federal excise tax on cash-funded remittances, which exempts digital transfers. Mechanism: a messaging thread in the user's own language, staffed by agents, is a cheaper and more trusted delivery surface for a regulated service than either an app or a branch.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: Felix is regulated as a money transmitter and its brand equity is money; legal, tax and benefits work looked structurally outside what it can employ people to do, in a channel it already owns.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test and the config-change test together. Immigration is held by Boundless, which is funded and does exactly machine-assisted family and work petitions with attorney review, alongside Lawfully, Alma and Docketwise. Tax is worse than occupied: Intuit is the leader in the narrowed market with a full Spanish-language TurboTax plus assisted and full-service tiers, so the narrowing is a config change for the actual incumbent rather than for Felix. Benefits is held by Propel, whose Providers app already serves roughly five million US benefits recipients. This is the 2026-09-01 lesson repeating - the wedge statement about Felix was true and irrelevant, because the buyer does not buy from Felix.

ideas.summary: Qualified-review capacity for AI-generated regulated records: models triage every agent-drafted GMP specification, procedure and master production record, surface the genuine deficiencies with evidence, and a bench of qualified reviewers inside the customer's quality system executes and signs the review - sold per record rather than per hour, to quality heads at contract manufacturers and clinical-stage pharma.
ideas.source_pattern: A dated regulatory trigger rather than a funded company: the FDA's 2026-04-02 warning letter to Purolea Cosmetics Lab is the first enforcement action with a deficiency section headed 'Inappropriate Use of Artificial Intelligence', finding that AI agents drafted drug specifications, procedures and master production records which were then used without further human review, in violation of 21 CFR 211.22(c). The firm has since ceased drug production. Mechanism: when agents draft regulated artefacts at volume, the legally required human review becomes the bottleneck, and review capacity becomes a product.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: Veeva sells software licences to the quality unit and would have to compete with its own customer and carry GMP liability to become the reviewer; consultancies price per reviewer-hour and cannot price per record without deleting their own margin. That looked like a real innovator's-dilemma block on both sides.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. BatchCortex already detects deviations in batch records and proposes root cause before human review - it was the occupant that killed ts-0159 in an earlier run and it is still there. Qwyn AI sells GMP-aligned deviation investigation and CAPA with full evidence trails, converting batch records and raw data into review-ready analysis. MasterControl is publishing on the Purolea letter as a product hook. The trade press describes agentic deviation workflows cutting investigation time by half in validated GxP environments as mainstream 2026 practice, not an opening. The ledger's own note that the independent-assurance seam is tapped applies on top.

ideas.summary: Physical AI for the data hall: autonomous rack-side hands for the AI buildout - replacing optics, reseating drives, reconnecting copper, power-cycling and decommissioning - sold to neoclouds and colocation operators whose growth is capped by technician supply rather than by capital.
ideas.source_pattern: The buildout itself is the traction: Crusoe raised $3B Series F at $30B (Atreides, Valor, Mubadala) and Fluidstack $1.5B at $18B (Jane Street) in the week to 2026-09-04, on top of Etched at $21B and Groq's 13 global data centres; and 90% of operators name staffing shortages as a critical constraint on building and expanding, ahead of power and land. Mechanism: robot foundation models plus purpose-built perception silicon (Lyte AI, $165M Series C at $1.6B, 2026-09-04) have made semi-structured manipulation in a known environment tractable.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: the incumbent is smart-hands staffing (Salute Mission Critical, PE-backed, veteran-recruiting, selling hours), which is in direct channel conflict with anything that removes technician hours; and the humanoid companies are pointed at warehouses and homes rather than at fibre connectors, cable management and hot-aisle constraints.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. Exclaim, founded by Helen Oleynikova - previously ETH Zurich, Google, Microsoft and Nvidia robotics - is building a remote-hands automation platform for exactly this task list: cleaning and replacing optics, reconnecting copper cabling and reseating drives, navigating the data hall autonomously and working a rack front from floor to top rail with no changes to the building. Worse for the wedge, Meta has been running dual-armed Watney robots on cabling at Altoona since mid-2025 and is testing Kinova and ABB units in Iowa and Ohio, with internal estimates of automating up to 80% of specific technician workloads. The largest buyers are building it in-house.

ideas.summary: AI-native commissioning for the data-centre buildout: ingest the design basis and submittals, generate the commissioning scripts, instrument and machine-witness Level 4 and Level 5 integrated systems testing, and sell against the energisation date - so one commissioning agent covers several halls instead of one.
ideas.source_pattern: Same buildout evidence as ts-0331 (Crusoe $3B at $30B, Fluidstack $1.5B at $18B, week to 2026-09-04), with commissioning as a hard gate on revenue: integrated systems testing is the final level of data-centre commissioning and no hall earns until it passes.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: commissioning firms bill per agent per day and automating themselves destroys their revenue, and the equipment vendors (Schneider, Vertiv) are the thing being tested and so cannot be the witness.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. Commissioning management software is a mature, contested category with at least four established platforms - CxAlloy (described as the leading cloud commissioning management platform), Facility Grid (spanning asset tracking and QC through commissioning and turnover, and publishing head-to-head comparisons), Bluerithm with a dedicated data-centre commissioning product, and CxPlanner. The workflow layer this idea would enter is already owned; what remains unautomated is the physical witnessing, which is the load-bank and field-engineering business (Aggreko, LotusWorks) rather than a software wedge.

ideas.summary: Agentic operations for carload rail: hold the private railcar fleet and the shipper's rail desk - trace cars off Railinc messages, dispute demurrage and constructive placement, manage bad-order repairs and AAR interchange billing, and make the calls to the Class I - for chemical, plastics, grain and aggregates shippers running on 1980s systems.
ideas.source_pattern: A category cluster rather than a single company: HappyRobot raised a $150M Series C at $1.2B on 2026-08-04 (Prysm and Eurazeo co-leading, a16z, Base10, YC; ~$200M total) and Augment raised an $85M Series A led by Redpoint with 8VC and Autotech, both running the same job - the calls, emails and documents of freight operations executed end to end by agents. Mechanism: voice and document agents that can hold a domain conversation and then act in the system of record.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: rail's data model is genuinely alien to truckload - Railinc CLM messages and EDI 404/322 rather than load boards and a TMS, per-railroad demurrage tariffs, AAR interchange rules, private car marks - and the counterparty is a monopoly railroad rather than a competitive carrier market, which looked like a second product.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test, with the config-change test underneath. Traktive sells an AI platform for rail operations explicitly aimed at maximising fleet utilisation and reducing demurrage; Telegraph sells a rail operating system for visibility, exceptions, cycle analysis and demurrage risk; RailPulse holds railcar telemetry; IntelliTrans holds rail TMS. And ts-0293 already established that vertical re-points of HappyRobot die to config change, since it has named insurance, energy, telecoms and airlines as its own expansion path.

ideas.summary: AI-native business personal property tax: read the fixed-asset ledger and the invoices behind it, classify every asset against each jurisdiction's schedule, file the renditions, and model and argue the assessment appeal - beachhead the data centres filing billions of dollars of servers into hundreds of county appraisal districts under abatement agreements.
ideas.source_pattern: The YC Summer 2026 'agent-native back-office replacement' cluster - functions replaced entirely rather than augmented - plus the capital-expenditure wave behind data centres (Crusoe at $30B, Fluidstack at $18B) that makes personal property the fastest-growing assessment base in the country.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: Ryan LLC and the Big Four bill hours and contingency fees on this work and cannot productise without cannibalising, and the sales-tax engines have no fixed-asset data model - which looked like a clean channel-conflict wedge.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. Avalara has shipped an automated real and personal property tax compliance product since 2023 and sells it to businesses and accountants, which answers the config-change question directly. The data-centre beachhead is the most contested part of the market rather than the least: ITC Tax runs a dedicated data-centre property tax practice, Swartz + Associates publishes on data-centre appeals as a specialty, Baker Tilly sells the same, and NextAutomation already sells an AI layer that extracts assessment notices and tracks appeal deadlines across jurisdictions on top of whatever tooling or consultant the taxpayer uses.

ideas.summary: Attribution and royalty settlement for licensed generative media: for any generated output, determine which catalogue recordings materially contributed and at what weight, to an audit-grade standard, and settle the money - sold to labels, publishers and the model companies whose training licences depend on being able to account for it.
ideas.source_pattern: Stability AI's $76M Series B, announced late August 2026 and closing 2026-09-01, in which Universal Music Group, Sony Music Group and Warner Music Group all took equity in the same AI company for the first time, alongside Electronic Arts, AMD Ventures, Coatue, Greycroft, Sean Parker and Eric Schmidt - following Stable Audio 3.0, trained on licensed data. Corroborating cluster in generative media generally: Higgsfield at $400M Series B and a $5.4B valuation, doubled from $2B in under six months; Tripo AI at roughly $446M; Meshy at $400M and $1.5B.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: the majors are now inside the model companies, which implies revenue sharing that nobody can currently compute, and no model vendor can credibly audit its own attribution.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. Attribution for generative media is an established and funded category, not a gap: Sureel sells per-output attribution for AI-generated content, Musical AI sells attribution and licensing settlement for music specifically, ProRata.ai sells proportional attribution and revenue share, Vermillio sells likeness and catalogue attribution and licensing, and Human Native and Created by Humans hold the licensing-marketplace side. The buyer is also concentrated to the point of fragility - three labels and a handful of model vendors.

ideas.summary: Regulatory-grade patient interviewing: an AI-native clinical research organisation whose product is the machine-conducted qualitative patient interview - in-trial and exit interviews, concept elicitation and cognitive debriefing - run under ICH-GCP with IRB approval, 21 CFR Part 11 records and live adverse-event escalation, so that the patient's own account of a therapy becomes an evidence artefact a sponsor can file with FDA, EMA and an HTA body rather than a consultancy deliverable priced in interviewer hours.

cross.ai_signal: The instrument is the model. A concept-elicitation or cognitive-debriefing interview is an adaptive, open-ended, hour-long conversation in which the interviewer must probe without leading, recognise when a new concept has appeared, and know when saturation has been reached; it is then coded against a concept matrix by two independent human coders. Every one of those steps is a frontier-model capability that did not exist two years ago, and none of them is a form-filling task. Three further things are only possible with frontier models and are the reason this is not a cheaper version of the same service: (1) saturation can be computed live across a running cohort rather than declared after the fact, so the sample size stops being a guess; (2) every interview can be conducted in the participant's own language and coded into one concept space, which is what makes a global rare-disease cohort reachable at all; (3) a model listening to a patient describe their symptoms can detect a reportable adverse event inside the conversation and escalate it against the 24-hour clock - a duty that is precisely why a consumer research tool cannot be pointed at trial participants. Simile's and Conveo's traction is the proof the underlying interviewing capability now works at enterprise scale.
cross.structural_signal: Two funded companies at the identical job inside five weeks - Simile at a $2B valuation and Conveo at a $50M Series A - which is the market confirming that machine-conducted human inquiry is real. Both are aimed at commercial insight, and the healthcare versions that exist (User Intuition, Glaut AIMI) are aimed at pharma market research, not at evidence. The regulated half is explicitly held to be off-limits: the field's own 2026 write-ups state that IRB-governed clinical studies and vulnerable populations 'require human moderation'. Meanwhile in-trial interviewing is described in the peer-reviewed literature as growing rapidly inside clinical development while published guidelines on how to conduct it remain scarce - a fast-growing regulated practice with no settled method and no product. The regulator is moving toward this, not away: FDA published a Request for Information on 2026-04-29 for an AI-Enabled Optimization of Early-Phase Clinical Trials pilot, and announced its Real-Time Clinical Trials initiative with two proof-of-concept trials reporting endpoints to the agency in real time.

ideas.source_pattern: Simile - more than $200M Series B at a $2B post-money valuation on 2026-07-30, five months after a $100M Series A; revenue up fivefold since public launch, tens of millions of simulations run, customers including CVS Health, Wealthfront, Deloitte and Gallup. Conveo - $50M Series A announced 2026-09-02 (DST Global, Balderton, Visionaries, 6 Degrees, Y Combinator; $55.8M total), with more than 400 enterprises on the platform, infrastructure running across 50+ Fortune 500 companies, and multi-million-dollar enterprise contracts for its StoryLines product. Mechanism carried over: a model can now conduct an adaptive open-ended interview, and interpret it, well enough that the trained human interviewer stops being the constraint on how many people you can ask.
ideas.wedge: Regulatory posture plus an innovator's-dilemma conflict, one for each candidate follower. (1) Conveo and Simile cannot cross: serving this segment means becoming a GCP-regulated clinical service provider - IRB submissions and informed consent, 21 CFR Part 11 validated systems with audit trails, pharmacovigilance intake with a 24-hour adverse-event clock, site and sponsor contracts, HIPAA and GDPR special-category handling, and standing behind the data in an FDA inspection. That is a second company with a second regulatory identity, not a settings change, and their supply side is consumer panels rather than consented trial participants recruited through investigator sites and advocacy organisations. (2) The actual leaders in the narrowed market are services firms whose revenue is the interviewer hour - IQVIA Patient Centered Solutions, PPD/Thermo Fisher, RTI Health Solutions, Adelphi Values, Clinigma. Automating the interview deletes the billable unit and the CRO pass-through margin at the same time; they have had capable models for eighteen months and have shipped none. (3) The eCOA incumbents - Signant, Clario, Medidata - are built around structured questionnaire capture on provisioned devices; qualitative evidence is a different data model (free narrative coded to a concept matrix) and a different buyer inside the sponsor, so it arrives by acquisition, not by release note.
ideas.buyer: The patient-centred outcomes or clinical outcome assessment lead inside a mid-cap biotech or a specialty CRO - the person who has to defend a novel or modified endpoint. Beachhead of choice is rare disease and oncology, where cohorts are small, geographically scattered and multilingual, which is exactly where a human interviewer panel breaks and where regulators most want patient experience data.
ideas.trigger: A dated evidence obligation: an FDA or EMA meeting where the sponsor must show content validity for the endpoint it intends to use; a protocol going final that needs in-trial interviews written into it; or an EU Joint Clinical Assessment dossier that requires patient input the sponsor has not collected. Each of these has a calendar date and a budget line already attached to it.
ideas.why_incumbents_cant: See wedge. The occupancy search found the adjacent commercial market taken and the regulated market empty. AI-moderated interviewing in healthcare is occupied by User Intuition (HIPAA-aligned AI interviews with patients, caregivers and providers) and Glaut AIMI (pharma brand trackers), and Conveo publishes a pharma page - all of it commercial insight work. In-trial and exit interviewing for regulatory evidence is sold by IQVIA, PPD, RTI-HS and Clinigma as human-moderated services. Phases (YC 2026) does AI voice interviews for trial eligibility screening, which is recruitment rather than evidence. Cambridge Cognition's AQUA and Signant's central rating programme cover clinician-administered scale quality assurance, a different artefact. No funded company was found conducting GCP- and IRB-governed qualitative patient interviews with a model.
ideas.expansion_path: Rare-disease and oncology in-trial and exit interviews, plus concept elicitation and cognitive debriefing for COA development - a services pool of a few hundred million dollars, deliberately small and deliberately the place where the method gets accepted by reviewers -> become the qualitative arm of record inside the trial, sitting beside eCOA rather than beneath it, which is a $2.5B+ market growing at mid-teens and held by Signant, Clario and Medidata -> post-market and real-world evidence, where the same instrument answers effectiveness and tolerability questions payers ask after approval -> HTA and reimbursement dossiers, where the EU Joint Clinical Assessment has made patient input a mandatory input to a pricing decision across 27 countries and widens to all new medicines by 2030 -> the compounding asset is a cross-indication corpus of coded patient experience linked to outcomes: the concept libraries, the meaningful-change thresholds and the saturation curves that every future endpoint gets argued against, which is a standards position rather than a vendor position.

ideas.summary: The AI clinical rater: have a model administer and score the interview-based rating scales that are the primary endpoint in CNS trials - HAM-D, MADRS, PANSS, ADAS-Cog - eliminating the rater drift and inflated placebo response that sink psychiatric drug programmes.
ideas.source_pattern: Simile and Conveo prove machine-conducted interviewing works at enterprise scale; the CNS endpoint is an interview, and inter-rater variability is the best-documented cause of failed psychiatric trials.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: the eCOA vendors capture structured questionnaires, not clinician-administered interviews, and central rating is a human services business.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy and config-change tests together. Cambridge Cognition's AQUA already records, diarises and transcribes HAM-D, MADRS and PANSS sessions and scans them for scale-specific quality indicators - it holds the audio, the scale library and the regulatory relationships, so administering rather than auditing is a release, not a rebuild. Signant Health runs a central rating programme staffed by qualified psychiatrists across more than 1,300 CNS trials. And the sponsors are doing it themselves: MindMed scores every HAM-A and MADRS interview with five instances of a custom LLM and takes a consensus, which is the product this idea would sell, built in-house and presented at conference.

ideas.summary: RADV audit-defence engine for Medicare Advantage plans: for every submitted HCC, reconstruct the medical-record evidence against MEAT criteria, defend the supportable diagnoses and withdraw the rest, as CMS expands risk-adjustment audits from about 60 contracts a year to roughly 550.
ideas.source_pattern: CMS expanded its certified coder capacity from 40 to approximately 2,000 to audit all RADV-eligible MA contracts annually, with PY2018 findings due to start issuing mid-2026 - a dated regulatory trigger with an enormous implementation gap.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: the audit is a per-chart evidentiary reconstruction that risk-adjustment analytics vendors were not built to do.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test, decisively. RAAPID sells a RADV AI audit solution pairing an LLM with a clinical knowledge graph to validate each HCC against MEAT evidence in both directions; Reveleer's Evidence Validation Engine maps diagnoses to HCCs with claimed 99% accuracy; Martlet.ai launched a RADV audit-readiness platform explicitly for the CMS audit expansion; Inferscience sells real-time MEAT-criteria HCC validation; Charta Health sells a RADV operational layer for concurrent audits. Five named vendors on the exact narrowing. A secondary weakness: a September 2025 federal ruling vacated the extrapolation provisions, so the burning-platform economics are on appeal.

ideas.summary: Machine-conducted witness interviewing for safety-critical incidents: within hours of a recordable event, a model independently interviews every witness in their own language using a cognitive-interview protocol, cross-references contradictions and drafts the causal analysis, for operators under OSHA process safety, FRA, FAA and Joint Commission investigation duties.
ideas.source_pattern: The Conveo and Simile mechanism, pointed at the one interview whose quality determines a regulatory finding and where trained investigators are scarcest.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: EHS platforms hold the incident workflow but the industry states plainly that the witness interview is the part AI cannot do.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the config-change test, with a second block pointing the wrong way. Haven Safety AI is already an AI-native platform for incident investigation and root-cause analysis, and the EHS incumbents - VelocityEHS, Intelex, Cority, EHS Insight - ship AI copilots that draft investigation narratives, cluster contributing factors and write regulatory submissions; adding the intake conversation is an increment on a system that already owns the record. The second block is against us rather than the leader: a post-incident interview is discoverable, is often conducted under privilege by counsel, and is subject to union representation rights, so the buyer's own lawyers and labour agreements - not a technology gap - decide whether a machine may ask the question at all.

ideas.summary: Private worker interviewing as the supply-chain human-rights instrument: interview thousands of factory and farm workers privately on their own phones, in their own language, off the audited site, replacing the coached on-site worker interview that makes social audits unreliable.
ideas.source_pattern: The Conveo and Simile mechanism, pointed at the weakest evidentiary link in forced-labour due diligence under UFLPA and the EU due-diligence regime.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: an adaptive private interviewer is a different instrument from an SMS survey.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. EcoVadis ships Worker Voice, built on Ulula's technology, with risk-cadenced worker surveys - annual at well-performing sites, six-monthly where issues are flagged - plus a continuous grievance mechanism between cycles, sold into exactly the brands this would target, and reaching workers regardless of location, language or literacy. The category (Ulula, &Wider, WOVO, LRQA/ELEVATE) predates the mechanism and the distribution is already consolidated inside a ratings incumbent. Secondary weakness: the EU due-diligence obligation that would have supplied the trigger was materially weakened by the 2025-26 Omnibus.

ideas.summary: Deposition-grade claimant interviewing for mass torts: a model conducts a structured recorded intake interview with every claimant in an MDL inventory, cross-checks it against records, and produces a court-ready plaintiff fact sheet plus a defensible vetting record for the firm and its litigation funder.
ideas.source_pattern: The Conveo and Simile mechanism, pointed at an inventory of hundreds of thousands of claimants that courts are now dismissing wholesale for unvetted filings.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: privilege, admissibility and contingency-fee economics put this outside a consumer research tool's reach.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. Supio sells exactly this to mass tort firms - routing incoming records, extracting the qualifying criteria of diagnosis, exposure window and causation evidence, and flagging what is missing before a case advances, explicitly at docket scale - and sits inside a funded plaintiff-side field (EvenUp, Eve, Darrow, Alexi) that the ledger already used to kill ts-0230. Mass-tort intake qualification is described in mid-2026 trade coverage as operational rather than experimental at leading plaintiff firms.

ideas.summary: The oral examination as the credential of record: a model conducts an adaptive spoken examination on a candidate's own submitted work and issues a defensible competence record, for institutions whose written assessment stopped proving anything.
ideas.source_pattern: The Conveo and Simile interviewing mechanism plus the Mercor mechanism of model-underwritten competence, pointed at the collapse of written assessment integrity, with roughly 45% of institutions redesigning assessment by mid-2026.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: proctoring vendors verify identity, not competence.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. VivaEdu sells assessment-assurance infrastructure to universities with self-recorded oral verification at cohort scale and audit-ready evidence, backed by Durham University Venture Lab; NYU Stern runs Viva, which conducts personalised oral exams graded by a panel of three LLMs that read and revise each other; AutoViva embeds generative-AI coursework authentication inside Moodle; Eklavvya and a named tool category sell online viva delivery. Both the startup seat and the in-house institutional build are taken, and the buyer is a slow committee with a low contract value.

ideas.summary: Model-underwritten competence for forward-deployed engineers: assess, certify and supply the embedded engineers whose scarcity, not model quality, is the binding constraint on enterprise AI deployments.
ideas.source_pattern: The clearest labour signal in the scan: AWS committed $1B to a forward-deployed engineering organisation and Microsoft $2.5B to Frontier Company with roughly 6,000 embedded experts; FDE postings were up about 729% year on year by April 2026; companies planning to hire FDEs went from 5-10% to 70% within two quarters; and roughly 95% of enterprise AI pilots deliver no measurable impact, with the failures on the deployment side.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: Mercor grades experts for labs, not implementation engineers inside enterprises.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test, and by naming the wrong leader. The marketplace already exists in triplicate - WorkGenius supplies pre-vetted forward-deployed engineers in 48 hours, FDE Agency sells pre-vetted FDEs with simulation-based assessment, and offshore-arbitrage suppliers sell certified FDEs at 40-70% below US compensation - alongside Mercor, Andela and Turing. More fundamentally, the two largest buyers of this labour are building the supply themselves with $3.5B of committed capital, so the party we would sell to is the party that decided to become the competitor.

ideas.summary: AI-native actuarial firm: employ the qualified actuaries and sign the annual Statement of Actuarial Opinion for captives, risk retention groups and small carriers, reading every claim file rather than only the aggregate triangles, and own the fee instead of selling software to the people who bill it.
ideas.source_pattern: The AI-native professional firm shape proven across the 2026-09-03 run, applied to a mandatory annual signature-bound filing in a market of several thousand captives that incumbents cannot serve economically.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: Milliman and Oliver Wyman will not work a $20k engagement and the small shops are capacity-bound and paid by the hour, while a software vendor can never sign the opinion.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed as a duplicate on the ledger's own prior reasoning. ts-0166 killed claim-level reserve intelligence and recorded the governing objection explicitly: the statement of actuarial opinion is a credential-bound, explainability-constrained artefact - the ts-0122/ts-0134 standards-bound failure mode - and an actuary who cannot show the reviewer a defensible method cannot sign. The analytical half is also occupied (Lawdify on per-claim reserve development, CLARA Analytics, Gradient AI, Charlee.ai, plus an established individual-claim reserving research literature). What is left after removing the unsignable and the occupied is a small services firm.

ideas.summary: Complaint interviewing and reportability determination for medical devices: a model calls the reporter within hours of a complaint, conducts the structured interview, decides MDR reportability against 21 CFR Part 803, and produces the inspection-ready record, under the QMSR regime that took effect 2026-02-02.
ideas.source_pattern: The Conveo mechanism plus a dated regulatory trigger - FDA's new inspection programme CP 7382.850 effective 2026-02-02 - against complaint volumes the industry says have outgrown manual triage.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: QMS vendors hold the complaint record but not the conversation with the patient or clinician.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. Smarteeva sells AI post-market surveillance for medtech; Lexim.ai sells the 2026 post-market surveillance rebuild; Assyro and ComplianceQuest sell MDR complaint management with AI at every step from intake to PSUR; and AI voice agents doing MDR complaint intake with structured adverse-event capture are already described as production deployments handling 60-80% of patient support volume. The conversation and the determination are both already sold.

ideas.summary: AI-native structural engineering firm for the Florida condominium safety regime: perform milestone inspections and structural integrity reserve studies at machine speed against a 2026-12-31 statutory deadline backed by $500-a-day fines.
ideas.source_pattern: A statute with a hard date and a documented engineering backlog - exactly the trigger shape the 2026-09-05 method note asked this run to lead with.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: incumbent Florida engineering firms are capacity-bound and bill by the inspection.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed on venture scale first and occupancy second. The deliverable requires a licensed professional's physical visual inspection of a specific building, so the AI content is report assembly rather than the work; the purchase recurs on a ten-year cycle at a five-figure ticket; and the market is one state. Occupancy is dense and named on the first search page - M2E, FPAT, Building Mavens, FL Engineering and hundreds of comparable Florida firms already market milestone-plus-SIRS bundles. A one-state, once-a-decade, licence-bound inspection is the concentrated-episodic-buyer failure mode of ts-0183 and ts-0265.

ideas.summary: Neutral training-data consortium: a legally independent entity that assembles a corpus across direct competitors under a structure none of them would grant a vendor, trains a shared private model on it, and returns the model rather than the data.
ideas.source_pattern: River AI raised $1.1B led by General Catalyst and AMP with Nvidia, AMD Ventures, Y Combinator and Temasek into a two-month-old company on 2026-08-11, on the thesis that enterprises will train and own private open-weight models instead of renting frontier ones.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: River sells a training API to a single tenant and cannot be the neutral party between rivals.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. The neutral-federation seat is taken and funded: Owkin in life sciences, Rhino Federated Computing ($42.4M raised, a further $11.3M on 2026-01-27, and running the live FAITE consortium that trains biologics models across member organisations in a regulated environment), Apheris ($20.8M), Devron and integrate.ai. The consortium-as-a-product motion this idea proposed is the one Rhino already operates.
