ideas.summary: Manufacturer-funded access agent for medical devices and surgical implants: an agent network that clears benefits verification, prior authorisation and appeals for a scheduled procedure, free to the surgeon's office and paid for by the device maker whose implant only gets sold if the case goes ahead.
ideas.source_pattern: Forus raised a $150M Series C at a $3B valuation on 2026-09-08 led by Bain Capital Ventures with every existing institutional investor reinvesting (Thrive, General Catalyst, Accel, Redpoint, Pear, SV Angel), tripling its valuation months after a Series B and taking equity past $300M. Traction: thousands of medical practices and health systems in all 50 states, 9 of the 15 largest biopharma companies, approval times cut from several weeks to under 48 hours, free to doctors and patients.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: Forus's network and economics are built around the pharmacy benefit and biopharma money, not the device rep, the surgical schedule or the buy-and-bill medical benefit.
ideas.buyer: The practice administrator or device manufacturer's reimbursement lead at a mid-cap orthopaedic, cardiac-rhythm or neuromodulation company, at the moment a scheduled case is at risk of cancellation for want of an authorisation.
ideas.trigger: A procedure date set with an unresolved authorisation.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test, and the occupant proves the exact business model rather than an approximation of it. Develop Health ($14.3M Series A, $17.6M total) runs an EHR-integrated generative-AI benefits-verification and prior-authorisation platform that is explicitly free for providers because it is funded by manufacturers - the same free-to-the-constrained-party structure, already built. Around it: SamaCare holds the buy-and-bill medical-benefit authorisation workflow with Glidian, OncoHealth and NantHealth alongside, Cohere Health has raised $106M selling the payer side, Prosper AI runs healthcare voice agents across patient access and RCM, Banjo Health sells PA software, and Optum is shipping AI-powered digital prior authorisation. The device narrowing is a customer segment inside a category with at least six funded occupants, not an opening.

ideas.summary: Manufacturer-funded code-approval and specification agent for novel building products: generate and maintain the code-compliance evidence, evaluation-report application, alternate-means submission and per-project specification package for a new building product, free to the architect and the authority having jurisdiction, paid for by the manufacturer whose product cannot be specified until it is approved.
ideas.source_pattern: The Forus mechanism (see ts-0348) moved out of healthcare: the party with the margin pays for the agent that clears an administrative gauntlet sitting at a third party's desk, so the workflow is free to the person performing it.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: the software vendors sell to the specifier and the testing labs sell hours, so nobody sells the manufacturer a continuously maintained approval position.
ideas.buyer: The VP of product or codes-and-standards lead at a low-carbon cement, mass-timber connector, façade or building-integrated-storage manufacturer, at the moment a specification is lost because the product has no evaluation report for that jurisdiction.
ideas.trigger: A specification or permit rejected for want of a code-compliance basis.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the config-change test, because the leader in the narrowed market is the approval body itself and it is not blocked - it is the incumbent. ICC-ES writes the acceptance criteria, runs the evaluation and issues the report; ICC already ships generative AI against building codes (ICC AI Navigator, launched 2023, more than 140,000 code questions answered), and UL Solutions, Intertek and DrJ hold the rest of the evaluation market. A manufacturer does not buy an approval position from a startup, it buys it from the body whose stamp the authority accepts. The software seat is also taken, if thinly: Kite Compliance (New York, founded 2025, backed by Nine Four Ventures and REHAU New Ventures) sells AI-powered product-certification compliance with a construction vertical. Wrong leader, no structural block.

ideas.summary: AI-native full-stack insurance carrier for physical-AI fleets: own the paper and underwrite humanoids, autonomous mobile robots and other learned-policy machines on fleet telemetry and on what the machine is permitted to do, rather than on actuarial history that does not exist.
ideas.source_pattern: Corgi received regulatory approval to operate a full-stack carrier and has passed $40M ARR since approval in July 2025, on $108M raised (Y Combinator, Kindred, Contrary, Glade Brook, SV Angel and others) - proof that a de novo AI-run carrier can own underwriting, balance sheet and claims rather than ride someone else's paper. Alongside it, physical AI took $47.4B across 521 deals in H1 2026, roughly 4x H2 2025.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: legacy carriers have no loss history for learned policies and decline the risk.
ideas.buyer: The risk lead at a logistics or manufacturing operator taking delivery of a humanoid or AMR fleet.
ideas.trigger: Go-live of a robot fleet that the existing general-liability programme excludes.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test, decisively. Goodfault already underwrites AI agents and physical AI on one engine and prices humanoids under a dedicated peril, explicitly 'priced on what the machine is permitted to do, with credits for safeguards enforced in code' and from fleet telemetry where it exists - which is this idea's entire thesis, shipped. Armilla underwrites AI exposure without years of claims data and is backed by Lloyd's syndicates; Munich Re has run aiSure since 2018; Vouch writes AI E&O. The ledger already recorded this field as occupied in ts-0219 and the shape in ts-0178 and ts-0190.

ideas.summary: Machine-routed national infusion-capacity network sold as an API: read a specialty-drug order, understand which infusion capacity actually satisfies it, and route it in real time across free-standing suites, home infusion and hospital outpatient - the Scan.com mechanism pointed at the chair instead of the scanner.
ideas.source_pattern: Scan.com closed $220M in combined equity and debt in August 2026 ($90M equity led by Noteus Partners, $130M debt from VerisFi and Atempo) after doubling revenue past a $165M annualised run rate and serving 900,000+ patients, against a US market where 85% of scans are still booked by fax or phone.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: hospital outpatient infusion costs multiples of a free-standing suite for the identical biologic, and payers want the volume moved.
ideas.buyer: The site-of-care lead at a regional health plan or a self-funded employer, at the moment a member starts a multi-year biologic.
ideas.trigger: A new specialty-drug start priced at hospital-outpatient rates.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test, with a second and more damaging objection: routing is not the binding constraint. Optum sells site-of-care strategy for infusion therapy to payers as a named product line; Option Care Health and Optum Infusion hold the national alternate-site network; InfuSystem holds a payer network; Innovaccer is publicly marketing AI-reimagined infusion centres; and Local Infusion has gone from zero to 40 locations across eight states in three years by operating the suites rather than routing to them. The reason infusion is not a routing marketplace is structural and works against us: the drug must be acquired (buy-and-bill versus white bagging), the payer contract must be held, and 340B economics decide the margin - so the winner is an operator with contracts, not a network with a model.

ideas.summary: Machine-routed veterinary specialty and diagnostic capacity: read a general practitioner's referral, understand what specialty capacity satisfies it, and route it across the fragmented independent specialty and emergency network - the Scan.com mechanism in a market with no insurance gatekeeper and six-to-eight-week waits.
ideas.source_pattern: Scan.com (see ts-0351): $220M raised, revenue doubled to a $165M annualised run rate, 900,000+ patients, 85% of scans still booked by fax or phone.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: veterinary referral is cash-pay, fragmented and offline, and the human-healthcare networks will never localise to it.
ideas.buyer: The practice owner or medical director at an independent general veterinary practice, at the moment a case needs a specialist their usual referral centre cannot see for six weeks.
ideas.trigger: A referral that cannot be scheduled inside the animal's clinical window.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the wedge check: there is no structural block, only an unstaffed one. The leader in the narrowed market is the corporate consolidator that owns the specialty and emergency capacity (Mars/VCA, NVA, Thrive) - they are not locked out of routing their own capacity, they are the capacity. The software layer around the referral is already funded and shipping: Digitail ($23M, 10,000+ veterinarians, 3M pet parents), Lupa Pets (~$20M Series A, 200+ clinics), FirstVet (EUR 20M, doing exactly digital triage and referral to clinics), Vetstoria and Scribenote, inside a sector where veterinary software and digitally coordinated care took eight of twelve tracked funding deals. The ledger also already holds ts-0135, killed for treating veterinary regulatory asymmetry as a wedge.

ideas.summary: Sponsor-funded site-activation agent for clinical trials: an agent that carries IRB submission, budget and contract negotiation, regulatory packet and system build for every investigator site, free to the site and paid for by the sponsor whose enrolment clock only starts when the site activates.
ideas.source_pattern: The Forus mechanism (see ts-0348) applied where the sponsor has the margin and the gauntlet sits at the site's desk. Industry-average clinical trial agreement negotiation now exceeds 90 days and nearly a third of sites name contracts, budgets and system builds as the leading cause of delay.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: CROs bill the start-up hours, so automating them deletes their unit.
ideas.buyer: The study start-up lead at a mid-cap biotech or a site network, at the moment a first-patient-in date is at risk.
ideas.trigger: A protocol going final with sites unactivated.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. Florence markets AI-powered clinical trial contracting explicitly as the fix for the 90-day CTA; Tempus publicly runs AI-powered site networks pitched as the move 'from fragmentation to integration'; Advarra and WCG own IRB plus site-activation services and are shipping AI into them; and the trade press treats AI automation of site activation - IRB submissions, contract execution, lab setup, investigator training with deadline tracking - as current practice rather than an opening. Sponsor-funded is also how site start-up is already paid for, so the economic structure is not a wedge here.

ideas.summary: Machine-routed radioligand-therapy capacity: match a prostate or neuroendocrine cancer patient against licensed, shielded treatment capacity and an isotope dose that is decaying from the moment it is made - the Scan.com mechanism against a clock and a radioactive-materials licence.
ideas.source_pattern: Scan.com (see ts-0351), pointed at the fastest-growing constrained modality in oncology: radioligand therapy can only be given at licensed nuclear medicine centres, and the field names limited manufacturing capacity, transport bottlenecks and too few qualified nuclear medicine sites as the constraints that stop demand becoming treated patients.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: the dose decays, the site needs a radioactive-materials licence and an authorised user, and no general scheduling system models either.
ideas.buyer: The theranostics programme coordinator at a hospital or the site-activation lead at a radiopharmaceutical manufacturer.
ideas.trigger: A referral that cannot be matched to a licensed slot inside the isotope's half-life.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test, at the highest possible confidence. nuq.ai describes itself as the operating platform for theranostics - built for pharma companies activating treatment sites, hospitals launching programmes and coordinators running daily patient care - and Novartis, Lilly and Bristol Myers Squibb deploy it to every site they activate. The three companies that would be this business's entire demand side have already standardised on the incumbent. The premise is weakening too: Novartis states it has more than sufficient Pluvicto supply to treat within two weeks and delivers to US sites in five days, with 200+ certified US facilities and roughly 130 more being onboarded.

ideas.summary: AI-native independent charitable patient-assistance foundation: the legally independent charity that is the only anti-kickback-compliant way to fund a Medicare or Medicaid patient's specialty-drug cost-sharing, run by models - predicting who will need help, forecasting fund burn so donors size grants correctly, and auto-filing every alternative (Extra Help, the Medicare Prescription Payment Plan, state assistance) before the fund is touched.
ideas.source_pattern: Forus (see ts-0348) and Develop Health prove the manufacturer-funded access network, and simultaneously define its legal boundary: manufacturer money cannot reach a federal healthcare programme beneficiary's cost-sharing.
ideas.wedge: Real and unusually clean: independence from donors is a statutory condition, so no manufacturer-funded vendor can ever occupy this seat. Today's foundations (PAN, HealthWell, Good Days, Patient Advocate Foundation) run on phone and fax and close disease funds within hours of opening.
ideas.buyer: The pharmaceutical manufacturer as donor, and the patient as beneficiary.
ideas.trigger: A Medicare patient prescribed a specialty drug they cannot afford.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the venture-scale gate, before the occupancy test was needed. The wedge is genuinely structural - it is a legal independence requirement, the strongest kind - but the entity that holds it must be a 501(c)(3) with no owners, which cannot be venture-backed or exited. The for-profit alternative is selling software to four foundations, which is a small vendor position, not a beachhead. Recording the reasoning because the underlying legal fact (manufacturer money is barred from federal beneficiaries) is a durable boundary worth re-using on some future candidate.

ideas.summary: Machine-run pre-publication adjudication of pharmaceutical promotional material: a model reviews every piece of promotional content against the label, the claims library and the regulator's rules before it reaches the medical-legal-regulatory committee, then keeps monitoring it after launch.
ideas.source_pattern: Blee raised a $20M Series A on 2026-09-08 co-led by Fin Capital and SMBC Fin Atlas Beyond ($27M total; Y Combinator, Penny Jar, Cardumen and National Bank of Canada), selling AI-first pre-publication marketing-compliance review to legal and compliance teams. Traction: customers include SoFi and Expedia Group, and review times cut by as much as 65%. Mechanism: AI-generated content volume has outrun the human pre-publication review gate, so a model must adjudicate against the rulebook before publication and keep watching after.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: pharma's review gate is a statutory-adjacent committee with a submission obligation, not a marketing workflow.
ideas.buyer: The head of promotional review at a mid-cap pharmaceutical company.
ideas.trigger: A launch campaign whose volume the MLR committee cannot clear.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the config-change test, already executed. Veeva - which owns the system of record for pharma promotional content in Vault PromoMats - shipped the Quick Check Agent (automated pre-review of draft content for editorial, branding, regulatory and compliance issues) and the Content Agent in late 2025, and is shipping Falcon MLR, agentic MLR targeting a 70% reduction in manual review labour within five years, with further AI agents across clinical, regulatory, safety, quality and medical through 2026. The leader did not need a quarter to follow; it had already shipped before the candidate was written.

ideas.summary: Publisher-paid certification body for agent skills and connectors: the independent mark that gets a software vendor's skill or MCP server trusted inside enterprises, sold to the publisher who loses distribution when it is blocked, free to the enterprise doing the blocking - the AIR mechanism inverted onto the Forus economics.
ideas.source_pattern: AIR emerged from stealth on 2026-09-01 with $50M in two rounds weeks apart ($10M led by Sequoia, $40M led by Greenoaks), 20+ customers with about a quarter large enterprises and ~40 employees, discovering agents inside a company and continuously vetting the skills and add-ons they use - and filtering out about 27% of the add-ons and skills it finds online. Part of a cluster: $435M across 12 enterprise agent-security and governance financings between April and September 2026, including Zenity ($125M Series C) and Obsidian ($85M Series D) in 48 hours.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: a buy-side security vendor cannot take money from the parties it vets without losing the neutrality its buyers pay for.
ideas.buyer: The head of platform or partnerships at a SaaS vendor whose MCP server is being blocked by enterprise customers.
ideas.trigger: A blocked connector costing a vendor an enterprise deal.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test and by the platform-owner rule. Microsoft already runs a formal MCP server certification programme through its connector certification path, with automated validation for schema, metadata, packaging and baseline policy followed by a manual review of functionality, security, compliance, telemetry and responsible-AI readiness - the party that owns the runtime owns the gate. Below it the paid-mark tier is already commoditised: AgentSkillsHub sells a 'VERIFIED SECURE' badge with manual static analysis and a security certificate for $99, and Agensi scans every skill against an eight-point checklist covering prompt injection, data exfiltration, secret detection, dangerous commands, obfuscation, external fetches, credential access and privilege escalation before listing.

ideas.summary: AI-native global regulatory affairs firm for medical devices that also holds the legally liable in-country role: machine-generate and maintain the registration dossier for every market and stand as the EU Authorised Representative, UK Responsible Person and equivalent local legal representative, so the manufacturer buys market access rather than consulting hours.
ideas.source_pattern: The Forus structure plus the AI-native-firm shape that produced ts-0307, ts-0324 and ts-0336: the incumbent bills hours, the software vendor cannot hold the liability, and the deliverable requires a legally accountable party. Live trigger: the EUDAMED actor, device and market-surveillance modules became mandatory on 2026-05-28, and non-EU manufacturers cannot register without an Authorised Representative linked to their actor record.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: a software company will not assume Article 11 product liability, and a consultancy that automates the dossier deletes its billable unit.
ideas.buyer: The regulatory affairs lead at a mid-cap device or diagnostics manufacturer entering a new market or facing EU MDR recertification.
ideas.trigger: A market-entry decision or a recertification deadline.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test on both halves at once. Rimsys - the leading regulatory information management platform for medtech - launched Rimsys AI, a suite of embedded agents doing submission authoring, AI-powered regulatory monitoring and configurable impact workflows, tracking approvals across 100+ markets; Emergo by UL's Regulatory Affairs Management Suite is relied on by more than 1,700 companies to keep registrations and certifications valid, and Emergo also sells the in-country representation itself; and Pure Global sells AI-driven global market access bundled with EU Authorised Representative service to exactly this buyer. The combination this idea proposed as its wedge - the dossier engine plus the liable local entity - is already sold as one package.

ideas.summary: Functional-safety certification for mobile robots and humanoids: generate and maintain the ISO 10218:2025, ISO 3691-4 and IEC 61508 safety case for a learned robot policy, so the machine can operate near people without a person standing next to it and an underwriter can price it.
ideas.source_pattern: ISO 10218-1:2025 and 10218-2:2025 replaced the 2011 editions and absorbed ISO/TS 15066, elevating collaborative safety from technical specification to mandate; the mobile-robot and humanoid provisions are not expected until 2027-2028, leaving a two-year gap. Meanwhile physical AI took $47.4B across 521 deals in H1 2026 and insurers now name ISO 10218 and 3691-4 as the difference between a risk an underwriter can price and one they must decline.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: hardware certification bodies certify the chassis, not the learned policy, and the robot makers grade their own homework.
ideas.buyer: The safety lead at an enterprise deploying a humanoid or AMR fleet.
ideas.trigger: A go-live blocked by an unsigned safety case.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed as a duplicate of the operator's own book, which is the same failure ts-0292 was killed for. ts-0031 (independent behavioural-certification lab for robot foundation-model policies) and ts-0032 (test-and-evaluation assurance harness for DoD autonomous systems) have both been held at watching since 2026-06-18, and ts-0292 was killed on 2026-08-29 explicitly for being a third re-point of the same shape. Generating a fourth instance of an idea already sitting unacted-on twice is template-following. The 2026-09-10 evidence is real and valuable, and has been logged against ts-0031 rather than spent on a new entry.

ideas.summary: AI-native surety carrier for small and emerging contractors: underwrite a contractor's ability to complete the specific job from their project history, work-in-progress schedule, subcontracts and bank data rather than from an audited balance sheet, and write the bond directly - so contractors below the incumbents' economic floor can bid federal and state work.
ideas.source_pattern: Corgi (see ts-0350): regulatory approval for a full-stack AI-run carrier and $40M+ ARR in the 14 months since, proving that a de novo carrier can own underwriting, policy administration and claims with a tiny team. The narrowing target: surety is a near-zero-loss, high-expense-ratio line distributed through relationship agencies that will not look at small contractors, against roughly $1.2 trillion of authorised infrastructure spending requiring bonds on federal work.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: incumbent sureties underwrite through independent agencies earning 25-35% commission on relationship underwriting, so a small-bond book is channel conflict plus negative unit economics.
ideas.buyer: The owner of a sub-$5M-revenue specialty or minority-owned contractor, at the moment a bid requires a bond they cannot get.
ideas.trigger: A bid bond requirement on a public project.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the config-change test with occupancy alongside. The economics this idea claimed as a structural block are already fixed by statute: the SBA Surety Bond Guarantee programme exists precisely to make small-contractor bonds writable, so incumbents can serve the segment today without changing their cost structure. And the segment is served: AI Surety Bonding USA sells digital small-contractor construction and commercial bonds with approval 'in minutes'; 60% of bonding professionals report having implemented AI or automation in the bonding process; Tinubu, the surety platform incumbent, is publishing its AI roadmap; and V7 ships an off-the-shelf AI agent for surety bond processing. A crossable moat, already crossed.

ideas.summary: Neutral machine-routed network over independent accredited testing laboratories: read a hardware company's test requirement, understand which accredited chamber and scope actually satisfies it, and route it across the independent labs the big testing houses do not own - Scan.com's mechanism pointed at qualification capacity instead of clinical capacity.
ideas.source_pattern: Scan.com (see ts-0351). Supporting facts on the target market: roughly 50% of electronic products fail their initial EMC test, third-party labs are 45% of testing revenue (about $1.14B in 2025) with the rest held by the majors, and over 60% of labs are investing in AI-based data recording.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: UL, Intertek, Element, Eurofins and TUV own labs and sell their own utilisation, so routing a customer to an independent competitor's chamber is direct channel conflict, and their impartiality obligations as accredited certification bodies constrain what else they can sell.
ideas.buyer: The compliance or hardware lead at a Series A-C battery, robotics, drone or device company whose launch date depends on a test slot.
ideas.trigger: A launch date at risk for want of chamber time.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed on the AI-native gate and the segment-viability test, without needing the occupancy search to resolve. The routing layer is a marketplace over scheduling data - a model helps but the product is not impossible without frontier AI - and the genuinely AI-native version, predicting EMC or abuse-test failure from the design files before the chamber is booked, is simulation ground already held by Ansys, Cadence Clarity and Keysight. Segment viability is the harder problem: hardware companies buy a qualification campaign once or twice per product, the buying population is small and diffuse with no place it congregates, and Element is meanwhile consolidating the physical capacity (largest US battery testing capacity) that the network would need to route across.

ideas.summary: Supervisory principal for machine speech: review every outbound utterance a customer-facing agent makes in a regulated industry against the rulebook, in line and at latency, keep the immutable supervisory record, and stand behind it as the independent reviewer the agent vendor cannot be.
ideas.source_pattern: Blee (see ts-0356) proved that pre-publication compliance adjudication is a fundable category. The narrowing target: agents from Sierra, Decagon and Wonderful now send millions of customer-facing messages that constitute binding statements under UDAAP, Reg Z and E, FDCPA, TCPA and state insurance rules, with supervision today amounting to sampled QA.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: an agent vendor cannot supervise itself, exactly as a registered representative cannot be their own principal.
ideas.buyer: The compliance officer at a bank, lender or insurer deploying a customer-facing agent.
ideas.trigger: A regulator or internal audit asking who reviewed what the agent said.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the config-change test with occupancy alongside, and the config change is already shipped. The agent vendors have built supervision natively - AI Supervisor scoring every interaction with Traces replaying each decision step by step to give compliance a full reviewable audit trail, and combinable deterministic workflows so policy-critical steps run deterministically - which is the product this idea proposed to sell them. Around it: Saifr sells AI compliance for financial services, Theta Lake, Smarsh, Behavox and Shield hold communications supervision and archiving, and the core processors have moved in with Fiserv's agentOS and FIS's Financial Crimes AI Agent. The trade consensus is that real-time compliance monitoring moved from concept to deployment during 2026. The ledger also already holds ts-0301 and ts-0290 as kills on adjacent ground.

ideas.summary: Manufacturer-funded hospital value-analysis clearance engine: assemble the clinical evidence, comparative economics, the hospital's own utilisation data and the business case in each hospital's own format, free to the value analysis committee, paid for by the medtech manufacturer whose sale is not done until the committee says yes.
ideas.source_pattern: The Forus structure (see ts-0348) pointed at the gauntlet that kills more medtech revenue than any other: a surgeon's yes is followed by six to eighteen months of value analysis, contracting and group-purchasing review.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: the group purchasing organisations serve the hospital and the consultants bill hours, so nobody sells the manufacturer a maintained clearance position.
ideas.buyer: The market-access lead at a commercial-stage medtech company after FDA clearance.
ideas.trigger: A cleared product stalled at value analysis.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the segment-viability test: the product cannot solve the buyer's actual problem. Value analysis committees decline products for want of peer-reviewed evidence that the product is at least as effective as the current option - and a model cannot manufacture a randomised trial. Founders are documented as investing years and millions in products that stall at value-analysis and reimbursement review for exactly this reason, with a 2025 JAMA Health Forum study of 950 AI-enabled devices linking absent clinical validation to substantially higher recall odds. The 12-to-24-month 'reimbursement valley of death' between clearance and coverage is an evidence-generation problem, not a document-assembly problem. The document-assembly layer is also served, by health-economics consultancies selling global value dossiers and by the group purchasing organisations' own evidence services (Lumere, now inside GHX).

ideas.summary: Manufacturer-independent access engine for off-label, compendia-supported prescribing: build and file the compendia-cited authorisation and appeal for the prescriptions no manufacturer may legally fund, sold to the oncology, paediatric and rare-disease practices that eat the denial today.
ideas.source_pattern: Forus and Develop Health (see ts-0348) are both manufacturer-funded, and manufacturer money can never fund access work for an off-label use - that is promotion of an unapproved use and a False Claims Act exposure. Off-label accounts for 31% of cancer therapy denials, 73% of which turn on absent compendia citations; 88% of prior-authorisation denials are never appealed while 80% of filed appeals succeed.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: a federal criminal exposure, not a product gap - about as structural as a block gets.
ideas.buyer: The practice manager at a community oncology, paediatric specialty or rare-disease practice.
ideas.trigger: An off-label denial with a treatment window closing.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. VerityAuth.ai sells exactly this - oncology prior authorisations approved faster and every denial appealed automatically using NCCN-cited evidence, generating the compendia-cited appeal letter and peer-to-peer talking points in two minutes. Staffingly runs payer-portal navigation, J-code and CPT lookup, NCCN compendia citation matching, denial-reason pattern recognition across twelve months of decisions and clinical packet assembly from the EHR. Counterforce Health gives oncology practices free AI-powered appeals. Above them the category is dense with funded players (SamaCare, Cohere, Develop Health, Glidian, OncoHealth, CoverMyMeds). The legal wedge is real and the beachhead is nonetheless taken - which is the run's sharpest single lesson: a structural block on the leader does not imply an empty segment.

ideas.summary: Benefit of record for the pension endgame: an independent, machine-reconstructed determination of what a defined-benefit scheme actually owes each member - read the entire deed-and-rules history, every amendment, announcement and trustee minute, work out which provisions bound which member on which date, recompute the entitlement against sixty years of administration data, and stand behind the answer - sold to the bulk-annuity insurer and the trustee board at the moment a buy-in has to become a buyout.

cross.ai_signal: The determination is not a data-cleansing task and it is not a calculation task; it is a reading task that ends in a number. A scheme's benefit basis lives in a definitive trust deed plus forty years of deeds of amendment, announcements to members, board minutes, actuarial certificates and correspondence, written by different lawyers in different decades, frequently contradicting each other and frequently defective in execution. Establishing which provision governed a given member on a given date - and therefore what that member's pension increase, normal retirement age, spouse's benefit and GMP offset actually are - is precisely the layered document judgement that frontier models became able to perform this cycle, and it is why Trafalgar House's own eight-month trial concluded that models can support rules interpretation and write the calculation code but that the specification still needs a human: that is a statement about 2025 models and about a mid-size administrator's engineering, not about the ceiling. Three further things are only possible with a model in the loop: the reconstruction can be run for every member rather than a sample, so error rates stop being estimated and start being counted; it can be re-run instantly against a proposed benefit specification, which is what collapses the buy-in-to-buyout timetable; and the derivation for each member can be emitted with its evidence chain attached, which is what makes it something an insurer will price against rather than a consultant's opinion.
cross.structural_signal: The bottleneck is stated openly by the market. XPS's Q3 2026 trustee update has around 300 schemes reaching buyout in 2026 against more than 40bn pounds of deal volume, after roughly 160 buy-in-to-buyout conversions in 2025 (up 30% year on year) - and simultaneously reports that schemes are taking longer to get to buyout and that the backlog at insurers is increasing, with data and governance demands named as the cause. PASA has had to reissue data-readiness guidance for buy-ins and buyouts. Standard Life's four-month full buyout of the 700m pound Deloitte scheme is held up as remarkable, which tells you what the norm is. The Pensions Regulator has published an AI plan telling trustees they remain accountable for outcomes, which is an invitation to buy an assured determination rather than a tool. And the 31 October 2026 dashboards connection deadline forces every occupational scheme with 100 or more members that has not fully bought out to expose its benefit data to members - roughly 85% of pension records are already live on dashboards, which means the remaining schemes are the ones whose data is worst.

ideas.source_pattern: Harvey - 550M dollar growth round at a 15.5bn dollar valuation announced 2026-09-09 (Diffusion and Lightspeed leading; Sequoia, Kleiner Perkins, a16z, Coatue, Conviction, GIC, Goldman Sachs Alternatives), with revenue above 400M dollars and use inside 80% of the top 100 US law firms. Mechanism carried over: a frontier model can read a large, messy, historical private document corpus and produce the output a senior professional would have produced, to a standard the profession is willing to sign its name to. Harvey proves the capability and sells it as seats to the professionals; the re-point sells the determination itself, with the liability attached, to the party who pays when it is wrong.
ideas.wedge: Both candidate followers are conflicted in the same direction, and the conflict is the product. (1) The administrators - Capita, Equiniti, Aptia, Trafalgar House - wrote the calculation code and made the payments that a reconstruction re-derives. An honest machine audit of a scheme's benefits is an itemised inventory of that administrator's own historical errors, and the rectification exercise that follows is billed by the firm that caused it. They cannot credibly sell 'we independently checked ourselves', and their own trial write-ups position AI as an aid to their administrators rather than as an external check on them. (2) The actuarial consultancies - WTW, Aon, Mercer, Hymans Robertson, Barnett Waddingham, XPS - authored the benefit specifications and ran the data cleanse being audited. They are the drafter, not the auditor, and the manual project fees are the revenue being deleted. (3) Harvey cannot follow at all: it sells seats to law firms, has no basis to carry a calculation liability, and cannot be the counterparty an insurer prices a data-risk loading against. Independence here is a structural property of who you are not, which is the one thing an incumbent cannot ship in a release note.
ideas.buyer: Two people on the same transaction who split the cost of getting it wrong: the pricing actuary at a bulk-annuity insurer (Standard Life, Legal & General, Rothesay, Pension Insurance Corporation, M&G/Prudential, Aviva, Just), who today prices a data-risk loading and a post-transaction true-up because the scheme's own benefit specification cannot be trusted; and the endgame lead on the trustee board, whose sponsor pays that loading. The first ten are reachable without a retail motion - there are fewer than ten insurers writing UK bulk annuities and they are all at the same conferences.
ideas.trigger: A buy-in has completed and the scheme must now reach buyout: every member's entitlement has to be specified exactly, verified, and accepted by the insurer before the policy converts and the trustees are discharged. Secondary triggers with dates attached: the 31 October 2026 dashboards connection deadline for occupational schemes with 100 or more members that have not fully bought out; and a sponsor seeking to release surplus under the Pensions Regulator's 2026 defined-benefit surplus flexibilities, which is impossible to justify without first knowing what is actually owed.
ideas.why_incumbents_cant: See wedge. The occupancy search found no funded startup anywhere in this segment. What exists is (a) incumbent administrators experimenting internally - Trafalgar House's eight-month trial on rules interpretation and calculation specification, and public-sector systems reporting that 35% now use AI for at least one purpose, overwhelmingly member-service call deflection; (b) data-specialist arms of the consultancies (PwC's pensions data specialist practice, ITM, Heywood's de-risking tooling), which are the conflicted parties named above; and (c) generic 'AI agents for pension plans' content with no product behind it. Nobody is selling an independent reconstruction of the benefit itself to the insurer.
ideas.expansion_path: UK defined-benefit buyout - 40bn pounds a year of premium, ~300 schemes a year, with 5,000 schemes and 1.2 trillion pounds still to transact - is the beachhead, and it is a beachhead precisely because the insurer is a repeat buyer with a quantified loss from the status quo -> run-on and surplus release under the 2026 flexibilities, where the same reconstruction is the precondition for taking money out -> becoming the administrator once the benefits are re-derived and machine-readable, against a UK administration market of well over a billion pounds a year held by firms whose cost base is people -> the Netherlands, where the Wet toekomst pensioenen forces every scheme to convert roughly 1.5 trillion euros of accrued entitlement into individual pots before 2028, the largest forced benefit-reconstruction event in the world -> US pension risk transfer at roughly 40-50bn dollars a year, already carrying its own litigation over annuity-provider selection, plus the US public-plan world -> the compounding asset is a cross-scheme corpus of deeds, amendments and the benefit interpretations that insurers and their lawyers have already accepted, which is a standards position rather than a vendor position.

ideas.summary: Coverage archaeology as a machine: reconstruct a company's pre-1986 liability insurance programme out of its own historical paper - decades of board minutes, purchase ledgers, broker correspondence, litigation files, acquisition schedules and microfilm - resolve sixty years of carrier renamings and corporate successions, rebuild the standard-form terms year by year where the policy itself is gone, and produce the evidentiary coverage chart that funds a PFAS, environmental or abuse settlement; paid out of the coverage recovered rather than by the hour.

cross.ai_signal: This is the single most model-shaped task found in this run, and the reason it has never been productised is that until now the only available method was a human reading boxes. Four things have to happen at once: multimodal reading of degraded scans, microfilm, carbon copies and handwritten purchase ledgers; entity resolution across sixty years of carrier mergers, redomestications, pool arrangements and corporate reorganisations, so that a 1968 premium payment to a name that no longer exists is tied to the balance sheet that must answer for it today; inference of a missing policy's actual terms from its form number, issuing carrier and year, exploiting the fact that pre-1986 comprehensive general liability was written on standardised bureau forms; and assembly of the whole thing into a chronological chart with an evidence chain per cell, defensible in court as secondary evidence of coverage. Each step is a frontier-model capability and none of them is document search. The economic asymmetry is what makes it a company rather than a feature: a single reconstruction can unlock nine figures of occurrence-based limits, so the work is worth paying for even at a low hit rate.
cross.structural_signal: The demand is dated, enormous and simultaneous. Total PFAS liability is estimated at 120-165bn dollars, of which 18-20bn has settled with water systems and 100bn-plus of personal-injury exposure is unresolved; the aqueous film-forming foam multidistrict litigation held 15,246 filed cases as of August 2026. The insurance industry added the absolute pollution exclusion in about 1986, so the only policies that respond to contamination that began in the 1950s-1980s are pre-1986 occurrence-based comprehensive general liability policies - which is exactly the paper that has been lost. In parallel, three childhood sexual abuse lookback windows are open at once: New York City to 29 July 2027, California to 31 December 2027, Rhode Island to 30 June 2028, against dioceses, school systems, youth organisations and municipalities whose plans of reorganisation are funded by historical insurance and by nothing else. The Archdiocese of San Francisco's 395m dollar settlement of 530 claims in June 2026 - the largest ever in a Catholic diocese bankruptcy - is what that looks like when the policies are found. The trade press has moved the field from 'niche' to 'necessity' in its own words.

ideas.source_pattern: Two patterns, one for the capability and one for the economics. Capability: Harvey - 550M dollars at a 15.5bn dollar valuation on 2026-09-09, revenue above 400M dollars, in use at 80% of the top 100 US law firms - proves that frontier models perform senior-professional document judgement over a large private historical corpus at a standard the profession will sign. Economics: Forus - 150M dollar Series C at a 3bn dollar valuation on 2026-09-08, thousands of practices, 9 of the 15 largest biopharma companies, free to both doctors and patients - proves the model where the party who profits when the transaction completes pays for the agent network that clears the paperwork blocking it. Here the party who profits is the policyholder recovering limits, and they will happily pay out of the recovery.
ideas.wedge: Four separate parties are blocked, each for a different structural reason. (1) The occupants are not technology companies and cannot become them: PolicyFind, Restorical Research, Arcina Risk Group and the Insurance Archaeology Group are hourly research boutiques whose published technology stacks are WordPress, PHP, Cloudflare and Google Fonts, with no venture funding, no engineering and - billing by the hour on a task whose value is the recovery - no incentive to delete their own unit. (2) The brokers who would be the natural owners of the historical record, Marsh, Aon and Gallagher, are the parties whose record-keeping failure created the gap; putting their own archives under systematic machine reconstruction manufactures discoverable evidence against themselves, which is a board-level veto, not a roadmap decision. (3) The carriers are the adverse party by construction - the chart is built to be used against them - so no insurer-side vendor can sell it. (4) Harvey and the legal-AI category sell per-seat software to firms that bill by the hour; taking a contingent position in someone else's insurance asset is a different balance sheet, a different regulatory posture and a different risk appetite, not a pricing tier.
ideas.buyer: The general counsel or risk officer of a company that has just been tendered a legacy claim - a CERCLA potentially-responsible-party letter or a PFAS suit at a manufacturer, metal finisher, airport, military-adjacent fire-training site, textile mill or paper mill - and, as the second beachhead, the restructuring officer or plan trustee of a diocese, school system, youth organisation or municipality inside an open abuse lookback window, whose reorganisation plan is funded by historical insurance and nothing else. Both are reachable through the same twenty policyholder-side coverage law firms (Anderson Kill, Reed Smith, Covington, Blank Rome, Pillsbury), which is how the first ten arrive.
ideas.trigger: A tender with a deadline: a PRP letter, an AFFF complaint served, an abuse claims bar date in a bankruptcy, or an acquirer's diligence finding assumed legacy liability with no identified coverage. The clock is the point - coverage counsel cannot brief a coverage position they cannot document, and the boutiques quote months.
ideas.why_incumbents_cant: See wedge. The occupancy search was run first and run twice: on the segment (insurance archaeology, coverage reconstruction, PFAS and abuse coverage recovery) and on the category plus AI. It returned four named boutiques, all human-labour research shops, zero funded startups, zero AI-native entrants, and an insurtech funding picture in which 95.2% of Q1 2026 insurtech dollars went to AI startups pointed at claims processing and underwriting for carriers - that is, at the adverse party's side of this transaction.
ideas.expansion_path: Contingent-fee reconstruction for PFAS and abuse defendants is the beachhead, chosen because the trigger is dated and the payoff per engagement is large enough to fund the corpus -> the standing coverage-asset register for any company carrying legacy liability, sold into M&A diligence, successor-liability disputes and environmental reserve setting, which converts a project business into a subscription over the same data -> valuing and then financing the recovery, and finally buying the coverage claim outright, which puts the company on the policyholder side of a pool estimated at 120-165bn dollars for PFAS alone, opposite the legacy-liability acquirers (Enstar, RiverStone, Marco) who have built multi-billion-dollar businesses on the carrier side of exactly this asset class -> the compounding asset is a corpus nobody else can assemble: carrier form libraries indexed by year and bureau form number, historical policy-number schemas, broker and agency record layouts, and a corporate-successor graph, all of which make each engagement cheaper than the last and none of which can be bought.

ideas.summary: Quote and feasibility agent for high-mix precision machining: read the customer's model and the shop's machine list and price the job, collapsing the estimator who is the real constraint on a machine shop's throughput.
ideas.source_pattern: CloudNC - 20M dollar Series B extension on 2026-09-08 (Nimble Ventures, with Lockheed Martin Ventures participating), total funding 128M dollars, CAM Assist in use at more than 1,000 machine shops worldwide including Lockheed Martin and Major Tool and Machine.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: the estimator is a different person from the programmer, so a CAM vendor would need a commercial data model rather than a geometric one.
ideas.buyer: The owner or estimator at a 10-80 person contract machine shop.
ideas.trigger: An RFQ arrives with a 48-hour response window and the estimator is three days behind.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the config-change test, in the most literal form available: CloudNC has publicly announced Quote Agent, addressing 'one of the most manual and commercially important steps in machining: assessing new jobs and preparing quotes', shipping later in 2026. The leader is not merely able to follow, it has already announced the follow. Paperless Parts and Xometry hold the rest of the segment.

ideas.summary: Casting methoding engine: generate the gating, riser and process design for a shape casting from part geometry, alloy and requirement, so a foundry can quote and pour a new part without the retiring metallurgist who is currently the only person who can do it.
ideas.source_pattern: CloudNC (see ts-0367) proves that geometry-to-process-plan generation sells into fragmented metalworking; defence demand for complex castings is described by the trade as unprecedented and foundry lead times are the binding constraint.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: subtractive toolpath generation and solidification physics are different disciplines with different data models, so CloudNC would be starting a second company.
ideas.buyer: The chief metallurgist or owner of an independent sand or investment foundry.
ideas.trigger: A defence or aerospace customer asks for a new casting and the shop cannot quote it without weeks of trial-and-error simulation.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. PhysicsX publishes 'Real-Time Intelligence in the Foundry: AI for Casting Quality and Efficiency' and is explicitly making casting optimisation AI-native across aerospace, defence and automotive; Foundry Lab has sold its digital metal casting system to the New Jersey Innovation Institute in partnership with US Army DEVCOM, on the claim that its castings need no requalification; Fabri has raised 13.5M dollars for 'new-age casting'. Underneath them MAGMA, ESI ProCAST and Flow-3D Cast own the simulation record and have shipped autonomous optimisation for years - the platform-owner question answers itself.

ideas.summary: Adaptive repair-machining engine for aerospace maintenance, repair and overhaul: scan the worn part, infer the as-found geometry against a nominal that no longer applies, and generate the blend, weld-prep and finish toolpaths for turbine airfoil repair.
ideas.source_pattern: CloudNC (see ts-0367), re-pointed from making new parts to repairing worn ones, where there is no valid nominal model and the scarce expertise is worse.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: CloudNC's product assumes a nominal CAD model, and MRO by definition has none.
ideas.buyer: The repair engineering lead at an engine or industrial gas turbine MRO shop.
ideas.trigger: A repair scheme has to be developed for a part the shop has not seen before, against an airline's turnaround clock.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test, and the occupant has been there for years. Acme Manufacturing sells Robotic Auto Path Generation specifically for aerospace MRO engine blade repair, claiming 3-4x faster than CNC grinding or manual finishing, and runs a joint blade-repair cell with Optomec combining directed energy deposition with automated abrasive blending driven by a vision system. Adaptive machining from touch and laser scanning of worn components is described in the trade press as established practice, not an opening.

ideas.summary: Weld program generation for high-mix structural fabrication: scan the fit-up, generate the robot path and the parameters, and produce the weld procedure evidence, so a job-shop fabricator can robot-weld batches of one.
ideas.source_pattern: CloudNC (see ts-0367) plus a welder shortage that the trade calls the 2026 inflection point for robotic welding adoption.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: the leader in robotic welding is a hardware channel, not a software company.
ideas.buyer: The operations manager at a structural or miscellaneous-metals fabricator running batches under twenty.
ideas.trigger: A skilled welder retires and the shop cannot fill the seat.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test, densely. Forge Robotics (YC) builds robot-mounted vision and AI feature detection producing a real-time 3D map that drives the arm through every step from raw stock to welded part; AMR builds American-made robotic welding cells with computer-vision seam tracking and post-weld inspection; EVS-AI ships 3D auto-scan to path generation claiming 80-95% reduction in first-piece programming time; Valk Welding ships AI product recognition inside its automatic robot programming software. Four credible occupants, one of them YC-funded.

ideas.summary: Harvey for the firms Harvey will not sell to: the same document-judgement capability priced and packaged for solo attorneys and boutiques, self-serve and published, below the enterprise floor.
ideas.source_pattern: Harvey - 550M dollars at 15.5bn dollars on 2026-09-09, revenue above 400M dollars, 80% of the top 100 US law firms.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: Harvey is roughly 1,200 dollars per seat per month with an approximately 25-seat minimum, about 360,000 dollars a year to start, sold demo-first through a sales team on negotiated annual contracts - economics that genuinely cannot reach a ten-lawyer boutique.
ideas.buyer: The managing partner of a solo or sub-twenty-lawyer firm.
ideas.trigger: A matter arrives that needs document review the firm cannot staff.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. The pricing wedge is real and everybody found it: Bind ships AI-native contract lifecycle management at a published 90 dollars per seat per month with no minimums; General Legal (YC W26) is building AI legal services for exactly this tier; Legora is named as Harvey's closest competitor and takes the firms too small for Harvey's sales motion; and there is now an entire comparison-content industry ('best Harvey alternatives for solo and small firms') which is what a saturated segment looks like from the outside.

ideas.summary: Agency-side procurement intelligence: an agent that drafts the solicitation, runs the required market research and evaluates the bids for the public body doing the buying, on the argument that the vendors selling bid-writing to contractors are conflicted out of ever selling evaluation to the buyer.
ideas.source_pattern: Cato - 6M euro seed announced 2026-09-07 (Keen Venture Partners, Vento, Heartfelt, Moonstone, BHeroes and others; 7.6M euros total), automating public tender discovery and bidding against Italy's 309.7bn euro public procurement market.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: procurement-integrity rules and plain commercial conflict stop AutogenAI, GovDash, SamSearch, GovEagle and Civio from selling evaluation to the agency they help contractors beat.
ideas.buyer: The procurement director at a city, county, school district or state agency.
ideas.trigger: A solicitation has to go out and the department has no one who can write it.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the platform-owner rule, which the 2026-09-10 method note added to the config-change test for exactly this case. The buyer's system of record is agency-side eProcurement, and it has already shipped: PlanetBids launched AI drafting and editing of RFx documents and scopes of work in 2025 for the small cities, school districts and water districts that are the beachhead, and OpenGov, Jaggaer, Euna, Bonfire and Periscope own the rest of the record. The conflict argument is sound and irrelevant - the party that is not conflicted is the one that already owns the workflow.

ideas.summary: AI-native third-party administrator for retirement plans: hold the nondiscrimination testing, plan documents, Form 5500 filings and correction work for small and mid-size 401(k) plans, against a TPA industry of thousands of tiny firms with retiring analysts.
ideas.source_pattern: Savvy Wealth - 100M dollar Series C at a 600M dollar valuation announced 2026-09-09 (up from 225M dollars in July 2025), 150-plus advisers on the platform, an average of 19 hours a week saved per adviser - proof that an AI-native operating platform can recruit licensed practitioners out of an incumbent back office.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: recordkeepers only serve the plans they record-keep, and bundled providers avoid cross-tested, cash-balance and multiple-employer complexity.
ideas.buyer: The principal of an independent TPA firm, or the plan sponsor buying around one.
ideas.trigger: Year-end testing season, or an operational failure that needs an EPCRS correction.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. Stax.ai is an AI-powered retirement and 401(k) platform built for TPAs, pushing census data into compliance workflows with algorithms flagging risks before they become violations; Payroll Integrations launched TPA Connect off a 20M dollar round specifically to automate year-end Form 5500 and compliance testing across employers, payroll and recordkeepers, with ADP, QuickBooks Online, Empower and Transamerica wired in; Human Interest unveiled AI 401(k) compliance monitoring in August 2026 behind a compliance guarantee; BotMinds does the document extraction layer.

ideas.summary: Ambient documentation for the child welfare caseworker: capture the home visit and produce the case note, the court report and the federal data submission, against the 4.3 hours a day a federal study found caseworkers spend on paperwork.
ideas.source_pattern: The ambient clinical documentation cluster (Abridge, Ambience) proves the mechanism; the re-point moves it to a workforce with worse turnover and a note that is a legal document.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: clinical scribes are built on HIPAA and EHR integration, while the child welfare record lives in a state CCWIS system under different confidentiality law and ends up in front of a judge.
ideas.buyer: The deputy director of a state or county child welfare agency.
ideas.trigger: A caseworker vacancy rate that has stopped being survivable, or an ACF technology grant landing.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. Binti - already the established child welfare software vendor - ships Smart Dictation, which listens and turns shorthand or audio into professional narratives and prompts when information is missing, and publishes the buyer-education content for the whole category. The federal money is flowing to the incumbent's customers: ACF awarded 6M dollars across 10 jurisdictions in 2026 to advance technology use. Platform owner plus occupant, same company.

ideas.summary: Agentic control code for industrial automation: generate, verify and maintain IEC 61131-3 ladder and structured text for machine builders and plant engineers, on the argument that the coding-agent leaders cannot touch vendor-proprietary project files on air-gapped networks where a bug injures someone.
ideas.source_pattern: Cognition's 2bn dollar round and Replit at 9bn dollars establish that coding agents are the fastest-compounding software category; the re-point takes them to code with no GitHub corpus.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: no public training corpus, binary project formats, air-gapped deployment and physical-injury consequences.
ideas.buyer: The controls engineering manager at a machine builder or a process plant.
ideas.trigger: A line changeover or a retiring controls engineer.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the platform-owner rule. Siemens ships AI PLC code generation inside TIA Portal across SCL, ladder and FBD; Rockwell ships a copilot in FactoryTalk Design Studio; PLC Copilot is a purpose-built commercial tool reading IEC 61131-3 from real projects; Wipro PARI, with AWS, reports cutting PLC code generation from 3-4 days to about 10 minutes per requirement at up to 85% accuracy. The parties that own the engineering toolchain have all shipped, which is the answer the checklist item exists to produce.

ideas.summary: State and local counter-drone: detection, classification and pilot attribution built for the agencies that may legally detect but not mitigate, funded out of FEMA's 500M dollar counter-UAS grant programme for FY2026-27.
ideas.source_pattern: 9 Mothers - YC, roughly 200M dollar valuation, 1.6M dollars of booked sales and a single contract expected to expand to 35M dollars, having delivered multiple EDDA autonomous counter-drone systems to the Department of War.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: mitigation authority under 6 U.S.C. 124n sits with four federal departments, so an effector company legally cannot sell its actual product to a police department, and the segment needs prosecution-grade attribution instead.
ideas.buyer: The emergency management or aviation security lead at a county, port authority, airport or prison system.
ideas.trigger: A FEMA counter-UAS grant award, or a drone incursion that made the local news.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test and duplicative of ts-0187. Motorola Solutions completed its 1.5bn dollar acquisition of D-Fend Solutions on 2026-08-20 and now sells detection into precisely the public-safety channel it already owns; Axon owns Dedrone; DroneShield, Hidden Level and Airsight hold the rest, and the trade catalogues 45 counter-UAS vendors. More than 4bn dollars of US counter-drone spend in 2026 has produced a crowd, not a gap.

ideas.summary: Deployment and field service for physical AI: an independent company that installs, integrates, safety-validates and keeps running the humanoid and autonomous mobile robot fleets that robot makers are shipping faster than they can support.
ideas.source_pattern: The physical-AI cluster: Mind Robotics 500M dollar Series A, Rhoda AI 450M dollar Series A, 8.6bn dollars into humanoid startups by mid-2026 (1.8x all of 2025), Agility's Digit past 65,000 operating hours across nine customer facilities including GXO, Schaeffler, Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada and Mercado Libre.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: robot makers should not want a low-margin services business, and legacy system integrators cannot hire machine-learning engineers.
ideas.buyer: The plant or distribution centre operations director taking delivery of a first robot fleet.
ideas.trigger: Go-live, when a humanoid's 14-month payback assumes 80% uptime nobody has committed to.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the config-change test. Uptime is not an unserved need, it is the business model the robot makers already chose: robots-as-a-service bundles deployment, service and uptime into the subscription because that is how the category sells past procurement, and Formic has built exactly this - financing plus service for deployed industrial robots - as a funded company. Whatever a robot maker's theoretical margin objection, they are already doing it.

ideas.summary: Right-of-way entitlement reconstruction for utilities and pipelines: determine from the deed record what a given easement actually permits, so a transmission upgrade, reconductoring project or fibre build is not stopped by rights nobody can find.
ideas.source_pattern: Harvey (see ts-0365) for the reading capability; the transmission buildout for the demand, with Oncor and LCRA CCN filings pending at the PUCT and 500kV approvals moving through state commissions in 2026.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: Trimble and Esri sell software, land-services firms bill hourly, and the utility cannot staff it.
ideas.buyer: The right-of-way manager at an investor-owned utility, transmission developer or pipeline operator.
ideas.trigger: A line upgrade or new corridor where the easement file will not support the work planned.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the platform-owner rule, and materially overlapping ts-0307. Quorum owns right-of-way and land management for pipelines and utilities; On Demand Land is a cloud right-of-way platform that already applies OCR on import to link documents to parcels and corridors. The system of record exists, the record holders have started machine-reading it, and the remaining judgement layer is a feature release for them.

ideas.summary: Independent audit of agentic advertising: measure what an autonomous media-buying agent actually bought and what it was worth, sold to the advertiser, on the argument that agencies own the trading desks and ad-tech vendors cannot audit the supply chain they sit in.
ideas.source_pattern: Clay - 115M dollar Series D at 7.1bn dollars on 2026-09-09, up from 3.1bn dollars in August 2025 - plus a 2026 in which two thirds of US ad buyers say they will pay closer attention to agentic buying.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: a genuine conflict of interest at both the agency and the verification vendor.
ideas.buyer: The marketing procurement lead at a large advertiser.
ideas.trigger: The annual media audit, or the first quarter of autonomous spend.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. Independent audit of agentic supply chains is already being performed and published: Jounce audited H1 2026 agentic campaign results, measuring made-for-advertising inventory under 1% with 80% of inventory above DoubleVerify's benchmark. DoubleVerify and IAS hold verification, and the industry has settled on 'governed autonomy' - spend caps, approval gates and audit trails inside the buying platforms - which puts the audit trail where the money already is.

ideas.summary: The machine forward-deployed engineer: an agent that performs the deployment work itself - mapping the customer's data, writing the integration, standing the system up inside the customer's environment - sold to AI vendors whose revenue is gated on deployment labour that costs 300-550k dollars a head.
ideas.source_pattern: Forward-deployed engineer hiring grew more than 1,000% year on year through early 2026, with Google Cloud, OpenAI, Anthropic, Palantir, Salesforce, Adobe, Accenture and EY all launching or expanding FDE practices; posted comp bands cluster at 300-550k dollars with frontier-lab principal roles clearing 1M dollars.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: coding-agent vendors sell seats to a customer's own developers and cannot enter a third party's production environment under someone else's liability, and the consultancies bill hours.
ideas.buyer: The VP of customer engineering at a vertical AI company with signed pilots that have not gone live.
ideas.trigger: A pilot with a six-week go-live and no engineer to send.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test, and previously approached from the supply side in ts-0343. 8090 Solutions raised 135M dollars led by Salesforce Ventures for an AI agent platform that delivers enterprise software; Distyl AI and Fractional AI sell AI delivery as a business; and the frontier labs and Palantir run their own FDE practices as a competitive weapon rather than a cost they want removed. The bottleneck is real and it is the thing everybody is already selling into.

ideas.summary: AI-native correctional health provider: bid for and run county jail medical and mental-health contracts as an AI-native clinical organisation - reconstructing a person's medication list and acute risk at 3am booking from fragmentary county, pharmacy and hospital records, documenting care where nobody types, and converting custodial care into the Medicaid claims that section 1115 reentry waivers made billable for the first time - entering as the three largest incumbent contractors emerge from or sit in bankruptcy and counties re-tender.

cross.ai_signal: Three tasks in this setting are frontier-model tasks and were not solvable before. (1) Intake reconstruction: a person arrives at booking at 3am, often intoxicated, withdrawing or psychotic, unable to give a reliable history, and the evidence of what they take and what will kill them in 72 hours is scattered across a county EHR, a state prescription drug monitoring database, a homeless-services record, prior bookings and a hospital discharge summary - assembling a defensible medication and risk list out of that is entity resolution plus clinical judgement over fragments, not a form. (2) Documentation where there is no workstation: care happens at a cell door, in a transport van, in a segregation unit, so the record has to be captured by voice and camera and turned into a clinical note, a sick-call disposition and a billable encounter. (3) Release-timing prediction: jails have an average length of stay under thirty days and no predetermined release date, which is exactly why CMS itself describes county jails as the hard case for the pre-release benefit - deciding today who will leave inside the ninety-day pre-release window, from charge, bail status, court calendar and history, is a prediction problem and it is what makes jail reentry billing possible at all.
cross.structural_signal: Three of the largest correctional healthcare contractors went bankrupt inside two years: Corizon with more than a billion dollars of settlements on its balance sheet, Armor Health liquidated, and Wellpath - the largest, with more than 2bn dollars of 2023 revenue - filing in November 2024 with 644M dollars of debt against roughly 1,500 lawsuits, exiting in 2025 with an HIG settlement. Counties are actively switching: Shasta County, California signed a three-year 25M dollar contract with a new provider after deaths under Wellpath, and Lackawanna County declined to renew. On the money side, CMS has approved 19 section 1115 reentry demonstrations with nine more pending, letting jails and prisons bill Medicaid for pre-release services for the first time in the programme's history, and is offering enhanced federal match for the IT systems needed to do it; California's Justice-Involved Reentry Initiative has been bringing facilities live quarterly through 1 October 2026. Meanwhile the correctional EHRs that exist were never designed to produce a billable claim - the public record is explicit that many do not track procedures, services, devices or drugs by CPT code at all.

ideas.source_pattern: The mechanism is the YC Summer 2026 batch's clearest structural shift - 'AI-run X' replacing 'AI copilot for X', with agent-native firms Rational, Billow AI and Last Accounting Company in accounting and Osmaura and Erinys in law, and YC's own request for startups stating it plainly: sell the service, not the software, because the spend on services is many times the spend on software and most services are already outsourced. The paying evidence that the shape works at scale is Savvy Wealth - 100M dollar Series C at a 600M dollar valuation on 2026-09-09, up from 225M dollars in July 2025, 150-plus advisers, 19 hours a week saved each - an AI-native operating company that recruits licensed practitioners off incumbents rather than selling them software.
ideas.wedge: Four blocks, each structural. (1) The big EHRs cannot follow: Epic and Oracle Health model a patient and an encounter, while a jail is modelled on custody - housing location, cell moves, segregation status, transport, court dates, sick-call kites, use-of-force events - so serving it is a second product and a second compliance posture, sold through sheriffs and county boards of supervisors, a procurement motion neither company runs. (2) The incumbent correctional contractors are conflicted against their own product: their margin comes from a fixed per-inmate-per-month capitation, and a system that documents every unmet clinical need manufactures the evidence for the deliberate-indifference litigation that has already bankrupted three of them - they cannot buy an honest record. (3) The incumbent correctional EHR vendors are small, unfunded and have no claims engine; the public record says many cannot generate a superbill. (4) The ambient-scribe leaders sell seats into health systems running Epic, have no custody data model, no Medicaid reentry claim path, and no way to operate where there is no clinician workstation.
ideas.buyer: The county sheriff or jail administrator and the county board of supervisors who together hold the jail medical contract, plus the county health director where the jail sits under health-department control; secondarily the state Medicaid agency standing up the reentry benefit and looking for facilities that can actually bill.
ideas.trigger: A jail medical contract coming up for re-tender or non-renewal - most often after an in-custody death, a settlement or a Department of Justice or state inspection finding - landing in the same period the state's section 1115 reentry benefit goes live for that facility, which turns an unfunded mandate into a revenue line the incumbent cannot collect.
ideas.why_incumbents_cant: The occupancy test was run first and three ways: correctional or jail health plus AI startup plus 2026 funding; jail Medicaid billing and pre-release services software vendors; and the Y Combinator directory for corrections and justice-involved healthcare. It returned incumbent contractors (NaphCare, Advanced Correctional Healthcare, Mediko, YesCare), legacy correctional EHRs (CorrecTek, CorEMR, NextGen corrections), policy and advocacy organisations, one nonprofit YC company in supervision analytics (Recidiviz) - and no venture-backed AI-native entrant of any kind. The one AI story in corrections in the public record is agencies surveilling inmate phone calls, which is the opposite side of the building.
ideas.expansion_path: County jails, of which there are roughly 3,000 in the United States against a US correctional healthcare spend of about 9bn dollars, are the beachhead because the contract is small enough to win, the incumbent is distressed and the reentry benefit is new money -> state prison systems and regional jail authorities, where contracts are eight and nine figures and the same clinical record and billing engine apply -> the reentry care-coordination layer itself, paid by Medicaid managed-care plans who inherit a very high-cost member at the gate and will pay for a warm handoff, which converts a government-procurement business into a payer-funded one -> the general case of care for people the state is responsible for: juvenile facilities, state psychiatric hospitals, civil commitment, and the health-related social needs population under the same 1115 authority -> the compounding asset is longitudinal clinical and outcome data on the least-documented population in American healthcare, which nobody else is assembling and which is exactly what prices the risk when this becomes a capitated business.

ideas.summary: AI-native arbodienst: become a certified Dutch occupational health service where a machine conducts the structured functional assessment, drafts the statutory problem analysis and reintegration plan on the Wet verbetering poortwachter clock, predicts return-to-work trajectory and wage-sanction risk, and a scarce registered company doctor reviews and signs under the task-delegation the law already permits - sold to employers who are paying 250 to 400 euros a day per absent employee and facing a third year of wage liability if the file is inadequate.

cross.ai_signal: The binding constraint in this market is a licensed human whose supply is fixed by a training pipeline, and frontier models attack exactly the part of that human's work that is not the licensed judgement. The machine conducts the structured absence interview by voice in Dutch, builds a functional-capacity picture from what the employee says and from the employer's job description, drafts the statutory problem analysis and the action plan against the protocol, tracks every poortwachter deadline across a whole employer's caseload, predicts which cases are drifting toward the two-year mark and which files will fail a UWV review, and presents the doctor a decision rather than a blank form. Dutch practice already recognises the delegation route - task-delegated case managers and practice supporters working under the company doctor's responsibility are the profession's own proposed answer to the shortage - so the legal shape exists and the missing piece was a system good enough to delegate to. Certified European clinical AI now exists as proof: Tandem Health's coding assistant reached EU MDR Class IIa in February 2026 and its scribe followed, the first in Europe, and InterSystems IntelliCare became the first AI-native medical record system certified Class IIa in May 2026.
cross.structural_signal: The Dutch obligation is absolute and expensive: an employer must continue paying a sick employee for 104 weeks at 70% of wages, commonly topped to 100% by collective agreement, at an all-in cost of 250 to 400 euros per absent employee per day, and if the UWV judges the reintegration file inadequate it can impose a loonsanctie extending payment by up to a further year. The professional supply is collapsing against that: the Dutch capacity plan for 2024-2027 states that at least 258 new company doctors a year are needed and only about 90 start, and the wait to see one has stretched from one or two weeks to four or five against a statutory six-week deadline for the problem analysis. That is a legally mandated service whose supply is falling, whose deadline is fixed, and whose failure has a priced consequence.

ideas.source_pattern: Tandem Health - 86.49M euro (100M dollar) Series B on 2026-09-14 led by the EQT Scaleup Europe Fund with Kinnevik, Northzone, Amino Collective and Visionaries - supporting more than 10,000 care organisations, the first AI scribe in Europe certified as an EU MDR Class IIa medical device and delivered through Accurx to more than 5,000 NHS customers. The mechanism it proves is that a frontier model's clinical output can now carry regulated standing in Europe, and that European clinical AI is a fundable category on its own rather than a localisation of a US product. The 'own the licensed firm rather than sell it software' half of the shape is proven by the YC Summer 2026 agent-native services cluster and by Savvy Wealth's 100M dollar Series C at a 600M dollar valuation on 2026-09-09.
ideas.wedge: Geography plus an incumbent whose revenue is the thing being automated. A certified arbodienst must be accredited, must employ company doctors registered in the Dutch BIG and NVAB registers, and carries statutory liability for a reintegration file that is assessed by the UWV under Dutch employment law - a posture no US health-AI company has any standing to assume and no amount of localisation confers. The incumbent arbodiensten (ArboNed and HumanCapitalCare, Zorg van de Zaak, 365) are staffing businesses: their revenue is the company doctor's hour and their competitive advantage is the size of their doctor roster, so a system that makes one doctor do the work of ten deletes their pricing model and their moat at once - they are adopting AI as a productivity tool precisely because they cannot adopt it as a business model. The ambient-documentation leaders, Tandem included, sell into care organisations where the output is a clinical note; here the output is a legal document in an employment dispute, judged by a benefits agency, and the customer is the employer.
