ideas.buyer: The HR director or owner of a Dutch employer with 50 to 1,000 employees - the segment large enough to have continuous long-term absence and too small to run its own occupational health function - buying the statutory arbo contract; and the case manager inside larger employers who is personally accountable for the poortwachter file.
ideas.trigger: An employee passes six weeks of absence, which is the statutory deadline for the problem analysis, at a moment when the incumbent arbodienst cannot offer a company doctor appointment for four or five weeks; and, once a year, the renewal date of the employer's arbo contract, which is when switching is frictionless.
ideas.why_incumbents_cant: Occupancy was searched in Dutch and in English across arbodienst, bedrijfsarts, verzuim and poortwachter plus startup, AI-native and funding. What exists is incumbent arbodiensten publishing about adopting AI tools, small absence-management software vendors and consultancies, and an SME-focused arbo service - no venture-backed AI-native occupational health provider in the Netherlands, and no US entrant, which is what the certification and liability posture predicts.
ideas.expansion_path: Dutch SME employers buying a statutory arbo contract are the beachhead because the purchase is mandatory, annual and switchable -> up-market to large Dutch employers and to the absence-heavy sectors (healthcare, education, logistics, government) where a single employer's sick-pay bill runs into tens of millions -> take the risk rather than the fee: Dutch verzuimverzekering, the insurance employers buy against exactly the 104-week wage obligation, is priced today on payroll and sector because no one can price duration, and the party that shortens duration and holds the outcome data can underwrite it - this is the leg that makes the company large rather than merely good -> Europe, where occupational health provision is statutory almost everywhere and the doctor shortage is not confined to the Netherlands: Belgium's external prevention services, Germany's mandatory works-doctor coverage under the ASiG and the six-week reintegration management duty under section 167 SGB IX, France's mandatory prevention and occupational health services, and Italy's competent physician - a mandated market covering most of the EU workforce -> the compounding asset is longitudinal return-to-work outcome data by diagnosis, occupation and employer, which no incumbent has assembled because none of them ever had a structured record.

ideas.summary: AI-native Steuerberater practice: hold the German tax-adviser licence and run the statutorily reserved bookkeeping, payroll and tax work for the Mittelstand with agents, entering through the profession's succession crisis rather than selling software into DATEV.
ideas.source_pattern: The YC Summer 2026 agent-native professional services cluster (Rational, Billow AI, Last Accounting Company in accounting; Osmaura and Erinys in law) plus YC's own request for startups instruction to sell the service rather than the software.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: the German Steuerberatungsgesetz reserves the work to licensed advisers, which excludes every US AI accounting company outright, and DATEV is a cooperative owned by the Steuerberater themselves and therefore structurally unable to ship anything that deletes its owners' billable hours.
ideas.buyer: The owner of a German tax practice facing retirement with no successor, and the Mittelstand company whose adviser has just dropped it.
ideas.trigger: A practice succession or an adviser terminating an engagement.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test on the first search. Taxforce, a Berlin company, has raised a 5M euro seed led by Tenet to build what it describes as Germany's first AI-native tax consultancy, already operating as a digital AI-native Steuerberatung for freelancers, professionals and companies and starting from the medical sector. The wedge argument is correct and someone funded is already standing in it.

ideas.summary: Works-council clearance and continuous monitoring for AI deployment in Germany: determine what a deployed AI system actually does with employee data, generate the evidence pack a Betriebsrat needs to agree a Betriebsvereinbarung under section 87(1)(6) BetrVG, and monitor the live system against the agreement on every model change.
ideas.source_pattern: Mistral AI's 3bn euro Series D on 2026-09-08 at a post-money above 21bn euro, with roughly 1bn euro of ARR expected by year end, 125-plus enterprise customers and framework agreements with the French and German governments through 2030 - European enterprise AI deployment at scale is now real.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: German co-determination is an enforceable veto (a works council can obtain an injunction and an AI rollout is legally ineffective without an agreement), the works council may engage an expert at the employer's expense under section 80(3) BetrVG, and the vendor selling the employer's AI is conflicted out of advising the body that must approve it.
ideas.buyer: The works council chair and the HR or IT lead at a German employer with more than a few hundred employees.
ideas.trigger: An AI rollout blocked at the works-council stage.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed on the venture-scale gate, and on the config-change test underneath it. The negotiated artefact is a document produced once per deployment, and the market around it is already served by law firms, template vendors and AI-governance content (paperclipped, eu-konform, skill-sprinters and every German employment practice), which is the shape of a consulting market rather than a compounding product. The continuous-monitoring half, which is the only part with venture shape, is a feature any German HR system of record - Personio owns the employee record at 14,000-plus companies - or any AI-governance platform can ship, and the EU AI Act deadline that would have forced it has been deferred to 2027-12-02 by the Digital Omnibus (see ts-0278).

ideas.summary: Independent diagnostics and service for mixed-brand lifts and escalators, built on the EU Data Act right to redirect a machine's own controller data to a third party, attacking the elevator OEMs' service-contract monopoly.
ideas.source_pattern: The EU Data Act's access-by-design duty under Article 3(1) became applicable to connected products placed on the EU market after 2026-09-12, three days before this run, with the Chapter II user access and third-party redirection rights already live since 2025-09-12.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: elevator OEM profit is concentrated in service contracts on their own installed base and they have historically locked independents out through proprietary controller tooling, so opening the data is a direct attack on their own highest-margin revenue and they will not arm the attacker.
ideas.buyer: The building owner or facility manager with a mixed-brand portfolio, and the independent lift maintenance company serving them.
ideas.trigger: A service contract renewal, or a lift lockout.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. Independents already solved the data problem without the regulation: iFactory sells an OEM-agnostic retrofit sensor mesh and gateway explicitly designed to attach to Otis, Schindler, KONE and ThyssenKrupp controllers by reading physical telemetry rather than proprietary data boards, and uptime.ac has been publishing operating elevator predictive-maintenance practice for years. The market routed around the data moat with hardware long before the Data Act removed it, which means the regulation confers no advantage on a new entrant.

ideas.summary: Independent extended warranty and uptime cover for post-warranty mixed-brand industrial and construction equipment, priced per machine from the machine's own newly accessible telemetry rather than from a table.
ideas.source_pattern: The EU Data Act access-by-design duty live from 2026-09-12, against OEM aftermarket economics in which extended warranty and service plans are among the highest-margin lines in the industry.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: an OEM can only underwrite its own machines and will not undercut its own extended-warranty margin, so a mixed-brand fleet is a customer no OEM can serve.
ideas.buyer: The owner of a mixed-brand equipment fleet at the moment the factory warranty expires.
ideas.trigger: Factory warranty expiry, typically in year two or three.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. Machinery Scope already sells independent extended warranty across equipment types, makes and models in agriculture and construction; AmTrust Warranty and Specialty Risk is a leading underwriter of equipment service contracts and physical damage for exactly this equipment; EPG Global runs multi-jurisdictional extended warranty programmes for many of the world's ten largest agricultural and construction machinery manufacturers; and Circuitry.ai already sells AI decision models trained on lifecycle transactions and real-time connected product data to optimise service outcomes. Behind all of them sits HSB and Munich Re, who have underwritten equipment breakdown with inspection engineers for a century.

ideas.summary: Independent service and uptime for hospital medical equipment fleets, using the EU Data Act and US right-to-repair pressure to break the OEM service monopoly on imaging, infusion and ventilator estates.
ideas.source_pattern: The EU Data Act access-by-design duty live from 2026-09-12, plus the long-running independent-service-organisation fight over OEM servicing restrictions in medical devices.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: OEM medical-device service contracts are a high-margin annuity and the OEM cannot service a competitor's estate, while the hospital's fleet is mixed by construction.
ideas.buyer: The clinical engineering or biomedical director at a hospital system.
ideas.trigger: OEM service contract renewal, or a capital equipment refresh.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. Healthcare predictive maintenance is an established funded category - 21 disclosed equity rounds across 17 companies raising 784M dollars between August 2022 and July 2026 - and the hospital-side asset layer is held by Nuvolo, Glassbeam and the outsourced clinical-engineering incumbents TRIMEDX and Agiliti, who already run mixed-brand estates as a service. There is no empty seat here, only a well-capitalised one.

ideas.summary: Condition truth for equipment lessors: read a machine's real lifetime duty cycle out of its own data and price residual value and end-of-lease condition per asset instead of from a depreciation table.
ideas.source_pattern: The EU Data Act access-by-design duty live from 2026-09-12; lessors carry residual risk on open-end books and price it from backward-looking curves.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: OEM captive finance arms profit from residual opacity and from certified-pre-owned margin, and can only see their own machines, while a lessor's book is mixed-brand.
ideas.buyer: The residual-value or remarketing head at an equipment lessor or captive finance arm.
ideas.trigger: Lease maturity or a portfolio refinance.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. Telematics-driven residual-value work is already a product line, not an opening: Targa Telematics markets converting journey data into preserved asset value, Geotab publishes the leasing-profit thesis directly, envue sells digital twins for fleet remarketing, Trackunit holds the mixed-brand construction fleet layer, and Simon-Kucher is selling AI-enhanced residual-value forecasting to leasing companies as a named multi-billion-euro pricing lever. When the strategy consultancies are selling the idea, the wedge has closed.

ideas.summary: The AI-native importer and distributor of record for the EU Cyber Resilience Act: take the Article 19 and 20 obligations for non-EU hardware brands - verify the conformity assessment, hold the declaration for ten years, and run the vulnerability reporting - by machine-assessing firmware the importer did not build.
ideas.source_pattern: CRA Article 14 reporting obligations became applicable on 2026-09-11, four days before this run, carrying fines up to 15M euro or 2.5% of worldwide turnover, with pre-market importer verification following on 2027-12-11.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: the obligations carry no SME threshold, the importer has no source code and no engineering, and the manufacturer-side tooling is built for people who own the build.
ideas.buyer: The EU entity of a non-EU connected-product brand, and EU distributors of imported hardware.
ideas.trigger: A product being placed on the EU market, or a vulnerability disclosure.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test with the trigger date working against it. The obligation that actually bites now is manufacturer reporting; the importer verification duty is fifteen months away, which makes this a 2027 sale. Meanwhile the CRA services market already exists - iCertifi sells the CRA authorised representative role, Carra Globe and getreadycompliance sell importer compliance, the Big Four are selling CRA readiness, and ONEKEY, Exein and Cybellum hold the firmware and SBOM product layer. The ledger has also already killed the two halves of this shape separately at ts-0271 (importer of record for customs) and ts-0358 (holding the in-country regulatory role).

ideas.summary: The European integration estate for AI applications: the write-capable connectivity layer into nationally fragmented European accounting, payroll and back-office systems, sold to US AI companies whose agents cannot act inside a European customer's system of record.
ideas.source_pattern: Chift - 10.5M euro Series A on 2026-09-14 led by BlackFin Capital Partners - connects more than 120 European financial systems for 150-plus software companies serving over 50,000 SMEs across 10-plus countries, with revenue up tenfold since its 2024 seed.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: Europe's back office is nationally fragmented with no dominant vendor, so the per-country integration estate is uneconomic for a US company to build and is the real barrier to US AI applications entering Europe.
ideas.buyer: The VP of engineering or international GM at a US AI application company opening in Europe.
ideas.trigger: A European launch or a first large European customer.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test, which is also the source pattern - the company that proves the mechanism is the company sitting in the seat. Chift is funded, growing tenfold a year and already aggregating the exact estate; Kombo holds the European HR and payroll equivalent; and the US unified-API vendors (Merge, Codat, Rutter) are the ones who would be buying rather than competing. There is no version of this that is not 'be Chift, later'.

ideas.summary: AI-native indigent defence: an evidence and motion engine for public defenders, built on the structural fact that the company selling the police their body-camera record cannot sell to the defence.
ideas.source_pattern: Harvey - 550M dollars at a 15.5bn dollar valuation on 2026-09-09, revenue above 400M dollars, 80% of the top 100 US law firms - proves frontier-model document judgement at professional standard, at a price (roughly 1,200 dollars per seat per month, 25-seat minimum) that excludes every public defender office in the country.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: an absolute channel conflict - Axon owns the body-camera evidence record and sells Draft One to police, so it can never sell to the adverse party - plus a procurement motion and a CJIS data posture the legal-AI leaders do not have.
ideas.buyer: The chief public defender of a county or statewide system, and contract-defender panels.
ideas.trigger: A caseload crisis, a consent decree, or an indigent-defence grant cycle.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test, decisively. JusticeText is exclusive to public defenders, is at 4.0M dollars of ARR across more than 4,100 attorneys, supports 7 of the 22 statewide-administered public defender systems in the United States, and has already expanded from body-camera and interrogation video into written discovery as a multimodal evidence platform. The wedge is real, it was found first, and it is being executed.

ideas.summary: A machine-made clearing market for short-dated and returned pharmaceutical inventory: read the serialised pedigree and predict where a nearly expired pack will actually be dispensed, so it is redistributed rather than destroyed.
ideas.source_pattern: Highstock - 30M dollar Series A on 2026-09-14 led by Andreessen Horowitz with Greylock, 35.5M dollars total - proves that a model can match stranded physical inventory to a buyer discreetly enough that the seller's pricing is not damaged.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: the reverse-distribution oligopoly is paid to destroy product and licensing plus serialisation requirements make cross-entity redistribution hard, which should keep generalist marketplaces out.
ideas.buyer: The pharmacy director of a hospital system or a wholesaler's inventory lead.
ideas.trigger: An expiry horizon on high-value stock.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test and by the AI-native gate together. Hospital-side expiry and redistribution is Bluesight's published product line, distribution ERPs already sell expiry and batch control as a feature, and the 'expiry exchange marketplace' is a well-worn opportunity-blog concept rather than an unworked seam. What remains after the matching is a licensed physical distribution business with thin margins, not a frontier-model company.

ideas.summary: A priced secondary market for decommissioned AI datacentre hardware: predict residual performance and failure risk of retired accelerators from their own operating telemetry and underwrite the resale, as 2023-vintage fleets roll off lease.
ideas.source_pattern: Highstock's 30M dollar a16z-led Series A for machine-matched stranded inventory, against AI server refresh cycles compressing from five to seven years down to eighteen to thirty-six months.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: hyperscalers reuse or destroy rather than resell, OEMs will not cannibalise new sales, and brokers cannot price burn-in condition.
ideas.buyer: The infrastructure lead retiring a fleet, and the neocloud buying secondary capacity.
ideas.trigger: Lease expiry or a generation refresh.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. Compute Exchange opened a secondary market for used H100 and A100 GPUs in July 2026 with order sizes from hundreds to tens of thousands of units; the certified-refurbishment market already prices H100s at 15,000-20,000 dollars with documented warranty and burn-in premia of 8-12%; and CoreWeave, Lambda and Crusoe are already the well-capitalised buyers of retired hyperscaler fleets. The pricing layer this idea proposed to build is published market commentary.

ideas.summary: Certified clinical AI for the pharmacy counter: structured consultation, decision support and the auditable clinical record for community pharmacists now making treatment decisions under NHS Pharmacy First and its European equivalents.
ideas.source_pattern: Tandem Health - 86.49M euro Series B on 2026-09-14, 10,000-plus care organisations, first AI scribe in Europe certified EU MDR Class IIa, delivered through Accurx to more than 5,000 NHS customers - proves a frontier model's clinical output can carry regulated standing in Europe.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: pharmacy runs on different patient medication record systems and reports clinical services into a different NHS system, so the scribe leaders' integration estate does not reach it.
ideas.buyer: The owner of an independent community pharmacy group delivering Pharmacy First.
ideas.trigger: A commissioned clinical service with a payment and an audit trail attached.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test and the config-change test together. PharmBot AI, founded by a UK pharmacist, is already running structured Pharmacy First consultations with reported savings of 15 to 20 minutes per consultation; Community Pharmacy England is publishing formal AI and ambient-scribing guidance for the sector, which is what a market with vendors in it looks like. And the integration argument is not structural: Accurx already sits inside NHS primary care and Pharmacy First is entering its clinical-records phase, so the leader reaches this counter with a roadmap item, not a second company.

ideas.summary: AI-native independent medical examination and disability determination: conduct the assessment and produce the defensible determination on a claimant's file, sold to disability insurers and state determination services drowning in backlog.
ideas.source_pattern: Harvey and Rogo (30M dollars from Barclays, Citi Ventures, Societe Generale and MUFG Innovation Partners, 344M dollars total) prove institutions will fund and adopt the vendor that automates their most expensive analyst labour over unstructured documents.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: the examination is a licensed act and the determination carries appeal exposure, which should exclude generalist document AI.
ideas.buyer: The claims operations lead at a disability carrier, and state disability determination services.
ideas.trigger: A claim backlog or an appeal reversal rate.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. EvolutionIQ's AI claims guidance platform has been expanded across all of The Standard's disability products after a 2024 implementation; Wisedocs, DigitalOwl and Medrecords AI hold structured medical-record review for adjusters and reviewers; and insurer full-scale AI adoption went from 8% to 34% between 2024 and 2025, with unstructured document processing named the top AI investment priority by 64% of insurers. This is the most heavily vendored corner of insurance operations.

ideas.summary: AI-native Japanese inheritance-registration firm: hold the judicial-scrivener (shiho-shoshi) licence and clear the backlog of unregistered inherited land by machine-reading handwritten pre-war family registers, reconstructing the heir tree across multiple succession events and filing the registration - against the 2024 mandatory-registration duty and its 2027-03-31 grace-period cliff.
ideas.source_pattern: Integral (18M euro Series A on 2026-09-16 from Mosaic Ventures, Reid Hoffman, Cherry, General Catalyst and Puzzle) and the YC Summer 2026 agent-native services cluster: own the licensed firm rather than sell it software.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: Japanese law reserves registration-for-a-fee to licensed judicial scriveners, and the source records (koseki family registers) can only be pulled under a statutory professional-request privilege - so no US legal-AI leader can acquire standing, and the 23-24% of Japanese land with unidentified owners plus the 2027-03-31 grace-period cliff is a dated, fixed demand.
ideas.buyer: Heirs, regional banks and municipalities holding land that cannot transact until title clears; secondarily scrivener firms whose capacity is the bottleneck.
ideas.trigger: The 2027-03-31 expiry of the grace period for inheritances that occurred before 2024-04-01, and the separate change-of-name/address registration duty live from 2026-04-01.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test, on the first search, three deep. AGE technologies (Sozoku.com) closed a Series B of 590M yen and has handled 55,000 cumulative real-estate cases as of January 2026, doing online koseki acquisition and auto-generated registration documents. Sampaulo ships "AI Sozoku Mitsuro-kun", a patented koseki AI-OCR that determines heirs, draws the relationship chart and computes statutory shares, cutting average work from 60 minutes to 10, sold into scrivener firms and 12 municipalities in FY2026. AI Data ships "AI Registration Loop on IDX" for scrivener offices, and e-koseki sells nationwide koseki collection. The licence gate is real; the segment behind it is already served.

ideas.summary: Nursing-home-funded long-term-care Medicaid eligibility agent: reconstruct five years of an elderly resident's financial life from paper statements, asset traces and spend-down evidence and carry the Medicaid application to approval, paid by the skilled-nursing facility that is eating 8-12k dollars a month while the application is pending.
ideas.source_pattern: Ferry Health - 9M dollar seed on 2026-09-16 led by Andreessen Horowitz and Index Ventures, with over 1M patients on the platform and partnerships with health systems and insurers - proves an agent doing the individual's side of healthcare administration, paid by the institution that profits when it completes.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: the five-year lookback is a document-reconstruction problem no consumer health-admin product models, and the payer is the facility rather than the patient.
ideas.buyer: The admissions or business-office director at a skilled-nursing facility carrying pending-Medicaid residents.
ideas.trigger: A resident admitted private-pay whose funds are exhausting, or a denial requiring a full spend-down reconstruction.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test on the first search. CoreCare automates Medicare and Medicaid eligibility and authorisation workflows for skilled nursing and is used by more than 500 facilities, explicitly to accelerate and protect pending revenue; MedFlo AI runs automated nursing-home admissions with eligibility and authorisation verification on every referral. The party who profits is already buying this from funded vendors.

ideas.summary: Machine reverse-engineering of obsolete parts: turn a plant or fleet owner's legacy paper drawings, photographs and scans into manufacturable models and specifications for parts whose maker is gone or will not supply them, built on the channel conflict that stops an OEM-facing drawing platform from ever serving the OEM's customers.
ideas.source_pattern: CADDi - 17.7bn yen Series D on 2026-09-16 at a 182bn yen valuation, deployed in 22 countries and used by more than half the discrete-manufacturing companies in Japan's Nikkei 225 - proves that an enterprise's accumulated unstructured engineering record can become the substrate for every new sourcing decision.
ideas.wedge: Attempted channel conflict: CADDi's customers are the OEMs, so building a part-cloning engine for those OEMs' customers would attack its own base.
ideas.buyer: The maintenance and reliability manager at a process plant, utility or fleet owner facing an unobtainable part.
ideas.trigger: A failed part with no drawing, no supplier and a line down.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. Novineer sells AI reverse engineering for sustainment (NoviVision for rapid model generation, NoviPath, NoviDesign) with claimed 80%+ reductions in assessment time and defence primes reporting 40-60% faster turnaround on obsolete components; 3D Spark's Voluminate turns old drawings, DXFs and photographs into 3D models; Leo AI identifies any part from an image or description; TechDraw AI converts broken parts with no paperwork into manufacturable drawings. Also duplicates ts-0318.

ideas.summary: Certification-evidence coding agent for safety-critical software: generate not only the code but the requirements-to-test traceability, verification evidence and tool-qualification artefacts that DO-178C, IEC 62304 and ISO 26262 require, for the software that a coding-agent vendor structurally cannot certify.
ideas.source_pattern: Cognition - over 2bn dollars raised at a 48bn dollar valuation with roughly 900M dollars of ARR and customers including Citi, Goldman Sachs, Mercedes-Benz, NASA and the US military - proves autonomous software engineering is now bought at institutional scale.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: a coding agent ships code; certified software is an evidence artefact, and the tool that produces it must itself be qualified (DO-330), which is a different product and a different liability posture.
ideas.buyer: The head of software engineering at an avionics, medical-device or rail supplier.
ideas.trigger: A certification audit or a change that forces re-verification of a certified baseline.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test and then the config-change test. Ketryx raised a 39M dollar Series B (total over 55M) and has launched validated AI agents for regulated industries claiming a 90% reduction in manual compliance work, built for IEC 62304, ISO 13485, GMP and 21 CFR Part 820/11 with FDA and EU MDR-ready documentation - the medical half is taken outright. The avionics half sits with qualified-toolchain incumbents (Ansys SCADE, LDRA, Vector, Parasoft) who already hold the DO-178C tool qualifications an entrant would have to earn from scratch, and Ketryx crossing into DO-178C is a roadmap item, not a second company.

ideas.summary: AI-native modernisation of US state and local government legacy systems: absorb a state's COBOL unemployment, Medicaid or child-support estate, extract the business rules the statute actually encodes, and rebuild it - aimed at the buyer that enterprise modernisation vendors cannot reach through an enterprise sales motion.
ideas.source_pattern: Hang Ten Systems - 85M dollars of seed capital (32M plus a 53M extension) within four months of being founded in May 2026, from Xora Innovation, Mayfield, Aramco Ventures and Lip-Bu Tan, targeting enterprises above 10bn dollars of revenue - proves agents absorbing and rewriting a large software estate is a fundable category.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: government procurement, StateRAMP and the systems-integrator channel are a different motion than a 10bn-dollar-revenue enterprise sale.
ideas.buyer: A state CIO or agency secretary under a consent decree or a federal certification deadline.
ideas.trigger: The December 2026 deadline for liquidating pandemic-era funding, or a failed benefits system.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test and the config-change test together. The 2026 ISG Provider Lens for US public-sector mainframe services documents an established field of vendors already applying AI to document legacy applications and extract business rules; EvolveWare sells exactly the Medicaid-claims business-rule extraction described here, Karsun and the large integrators hold the contracts, and IBM ships watsonx Code Assistant for Z into the same accounts. The incumbent integrators own the procurement relationship and are shipping the capability.

ideas.summary: AI-native German statutory audit firm: hold the Wirtschaftspruefer licence and run mid-market Abschlusspruefungen as an AI-native Pruefungsgesellschaft, built on the statutory independence rule that bars a firm doing a client's bookkeeping from also auditing it.
ideas.source_pattern: Integral - 18M euro Series A on 2026-09-16 (Mosaic Ventures, Reid Hoffman, Cherry Ventures, General Catalyst, Puzzle Ventures) operating as an AI-native accounting and tax firm in Germany through licensed professionals.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: section 319 HGB independence means the AI-native bookkeeping firms cannot become their own clients' auditors, and the Wirtschaftspruefer licence is the scarcer of the two.
ideas.buyer: The CFO or managing director of a German Mittelstand company above the statutory audit thresholds.
ideas.trigger: The annual audit engagement letter, or an incumbent firm resigning the engagement.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. Cortea (Berlin) closed a 12M euro seed in June 2026 and has a technology partnership with dhpg, the largest German audit and advisory firm focused on the Mittelstand; its report-critique agent has been in production since August 2026 and more than 450 audit reports have been reviewed through Cortea since the joint development phase began in February 2026. EY and PwC Germany are publishing agentic-audit programmes above it. The independence conflict is real; the seat behind it is occupied.

ideas.summary: The certified clinical model as a component: train, freeze, document and CE-mark a clinical language model under EU MDR and the AI Act, then license it to European health-AI companies and device manufacturers with a full technical file, an ISO 13485 quality agreement and a decade-long change-control commitment that no frontier lab will sign.
ideas.source_pattern: Arcee AI (over 150M dollars Series B led by Vista Equity on 2026-09-16, having trained four models including a 400bn-parameter Trinity Large for roughly 20M dollars) shows owning a frontier-adjacent model is now a 20M dollar capital decision; Tandem Health (86.49M euro Series B, first EU MDR Class IIa certified AI scribe in Europe) shows the market pays for regulated standing.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: a general-purpose AI provider will not accept medical-device supplier obligations, expose training-data provenance to a notified body, or freeze checkpoints for a decade, because continuous deprecation is its business model.
ideas.buyer: The regulatory lead at a European health-AI company or medtech manufacturer placing an AI-enabled device on the EU market.
ideas.trigger: A notified body asking for the model's technical documentation, or a model deprecation notice breaking a validated device.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test, and softened further by the trigger not being live. Corti has opened its clinical-AI stack to startups explicitly on this proposition - a specialised clinical model plus direct engagement with its clinical and regulatory teams on EU AI Act, MDR and data-residency questions - which is the seat this idea wanted; Scarlet already sells notified-body certification for AI medical devices and publishes the guidance on using third-party LLMs inside an AIaMD. On timing, AI embedded in products already covered by EU product-safety law has been deferred to December 2027 and August 2028, so the forcing event is more than a year out.

ideas.summary: AI-native investment bank for lower-middle-market sell-side M&A: hold the broker-dealer licence and run the whole sale process by machine for owners whose deal is too small for a bank to staff, built on the channel conflict that stops bank-funded AI vendors from ever disintermediating their own investors.
ideas.source_pattern: Rogo - 30M dollars from Barclays, Citi Ventures, Societe Generale, MUFG Innovation Partners and Opera Tech Ventures, 344M dollars total - proves institutions fund the vendor automating their most expensive analyst labour, and by doing so bind it to their side of the table.
ideas.wedge: Attempted channel conflict: a vendor with four banks on its cap table cannot build the product that removes the banker.
ideas.buyer: The owner of a 5-50M dollar revenue business preparing to sell.
ideas.trigger: An unsolicited approach, a retirement, or a broken process with a regional advisor.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test on the first search. OffDeal is a Y Combinator-backed AI-native investment bank for small businesses, running AI brokers that source targets, conduct diligence and do outreach at a scale of thousands of companies at a time using LLM-powered semantic search over millions of SMBs. The narrowed segment has a funded, named, identically-shaped occupant.

ideas.summary: AI-native special-education evaluation provider: take over a district's initial evaluations as a licensed provider organisation against the IDEA 60-day statutory clock, where blowing the clock creates compensatory-education liability and the supply of school psychologists is collapsing.
ideas.source_pattern: The YC Summer 2026 agent-native services cluster and Savvy Wealth (100M dollar Series C at 600M on 2026-09-09) prove the own-the-licensed-firm shape; the register instruction from 2026-09-15 pointed at professions whose supply is falling against a fixed statutory workload.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: the 60-day clock is statutory with a priced consequence, and the incumbents are teletherapy staffing marketplaces whose revenue is the clinician hour.
ideas.buyer: The special-education director at a district with an evaluation backlog past the statutory deadline.
ideas.trigger: A state monitoring finding, a due-process complaint, or a compensatory-education award.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test, decisively. The sector has 569 K-12 special-education startups of which 132 are funded and 27 have raised Series A or later - Parallel Learning, Rethink, Presence, Poppins and Panorama among them - and roughly 60% of special-education teachers already reported using AI to develop an IEP or 504 plan in the 2024-25 school year. This is one of the most heavily vendored segments examined in this book.

ideas.summary: AI-native professional fiduciary firm: hold court appointments as guardian or conservator for incapacitated adults and run hundreds of cases at once - marshalling assets, maximising benefits and producing the statutory annual accountings - against public-guardian caseloads far beyond any published standard.
ideas.source_pattern: The agent-native services cluster (YC Summer 2026; Integral; Savvy Wealth) proves owning the licensed firm; guardianship reform activity in 2026 (Idaho and Kansas adopting the Uniform Guardianship Act, the federal Guardianship Bill of Rights Act reintroduced) makes the compliance burden heavier.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: a software vendor cannot hold a court-appointed fiduciary role, and the incumbents are hour-billing private fiduciaries.
ideas.buyer: Probate courts making appointments, and county offices of the public guardian.
ideas.trigger: A caseload crisis or a court-ordered accounting deficiency.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test and then by the venture-scale gate. Conservatorship.com already sells an AI-assisted compliance, accounting and court-workflow platform for professional conservators, guardians and fiduciaries across all 51 US jurisdictions, alongside GuardianPad, Advocord and My Junna. Underneath that, fiduciary compensation is set and capped by the appointing court, the appointment itself is discretionary and non-transferable, and the segment carries acute reputational exposure - the revenue cannot compound into a billion-dollar company.

ideas.summary: AI-native heir search and unclaimed-estate administration: reconstruct heir trees from public records at machine speed and claim the statutory finder's share on estates heading for escheatment, sold to probate courts, public administrators and estate attorneys.
ideas.source_pattern: The same agent-native services mechanism, applied to a document-reconstruction task that frontier models do well.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: the work is pure genealogical entity resolution over fragmentary records, and the incumbents are manual research houses.
ideas.buyer: Probate attorneys, county public administrators and trust departments facing an unknown-heir estate.
ideas.trigger: An estate filing with no identified next of kin, or an approaching escheatment deadline.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. HeirSearch has been in the business since 1967 and describes itself as the leading heir-finding firm, alongside HeirPros, Finders International and AncestryProGenealogists; the trade literature already describes AI extracting executor names, property details and estate value from probate filings and cross-referencing public records to identify secondary heirs. Sixty years of proprietary research files is exactly the compounding asset an entrant would need and cannot buy.

ideas.summary: AI-native attest firm for the audits nobody wants: hold the CPA licence and run ERISA employee-benefit-plan audits and Uniform Guidance single audits at volume, built on the independence rule that bars recordkeepers and third-party administrators from auditing the plans they administer.
ideas.source_pattern: Integral (18M euro Series A, 2026-09-16) and the YC Summer 2026 AI-run accounting firms (Rational, Billow AI, Last Accounting Company) prove the AI-native licensed accounting firm is a funded category.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: auditor independence structurally bars Fidelity, Empower and the plan TPAs from the engagement, and the US CPA supply collapse is pushing small firms out of a low-margin statutory audit that roughly 85,000 plans must buy every year.
ideas.buyer: The plan sponsor or HR leader at a company with a large 401(k) plan, and grant-funded organisations needing a single audit.
ideas.trigger: The Form 5500 filing deadline, or an incumbent CPA firm resigning the engagement.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. Arrya sells an AI staff auditor purpose-built for employee-benefit-plan and 401(k) audits - taking recordkeeper packages, payroll reports and plan documents and producing participant-level testing workpapers, remittance timeliness testing, tie-outs and a cited exception list - and is onboarding its founding pilot cohort for the Fall 2026 busy season on plan-year 2025 audits. Fieldguide, Caseware and Suralink hold the surrounding software layer. The exact segment, the exact workflow, the exact busy season.

ideas.summary: AI-native remote operator of record for small municipal water and wastewater systems: hold the licensed responsible-charge role across dozens of small plants at once, with a learned model of each plant predicting permit exceedances from SCADA, weather and influent and driving setpoints, as one-third of the water workforce retires.
ideas.source_pattern: Noetive - 41M dollar seed led by Eclipse with Craft Ventures, building world models of physical industrial environments, with early customer Steuben Foods reporting a 10-15% line-capacity improvement - proves a learned model of a physical process is fundable and is starting to pay.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: the permit requires a named licensed operator, the supply of those operators is collapsing, and the incumbent contract operators are staffing businesses.
ideas.buyer: A small town council or rural water district whose licensed operator just retired, or that is under a state or EPA compliance order.
ideas.trigger: An operator retirement, or a significant-non-compliance finding.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the config-change test in its strongest form - the incumbent has already shipped it - and then by occupancy. Veolia has opened its North America Hubgrade centre, a digital command centre combining human expertise with real-time data and AI to run municipal water and wastewater remotely across the West. Ainwater serves over 100 treatment plants across Chile, Mexico, Brazil and Spain; Aquasight's APOLLO sells a real-time digital twin framed explicitly at institutional knowledge lost to retirements; Opseyes and Cattron hold adjacent layers. The general lesson: a contract operator on a fixed-fee contract is not structurally blocked from automating itself, because automation raises its margin - unlike a firm that bills per unit of professional time.

ideas.summary: Death-certificate completion agent: chase, complete and file the certifying physician's portion of the death certificate inside the statutory filing window, paid by the funeral home that cannot obtain a disposition permit or get paid until it is registered.
ideas.source_pattern: Ferry Health (9M dollar seed on 2026-09-16 led by a16z and Index, 1M+ patients) proves the administrative-gauntlet agent paid by the party that profits on completion.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: most states now mandate electronic death registration with a 72-hour filing window, a missing physician signature blocks release of the body, and no health-AI vendor has any reason to build for a funeral home.
ideas.buyer: The funeral director at an independent funeral home.
ideas.trigger: A certificate stalled on a physician signature, delaying a burial or cremation.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. ClosureMD sells AI voice agents purpose-built for funeral homes to obtain physician sign-off on death certificates, handling both inbound family calls and outbound follow-up with hospitals and physicians; Affinda holds the document-extraction layer. Logged here because it also bounds the expansion path of ts-0410, which should not assume this adjacency is open.

ideas.summary: AI-native medicolegal death investigation firm: contract with counties to run their medical examiner or coroner death investigations end to end - reconstructing a decedent's medical, pharmacy and EMS history from records with no patient identifier and no consent path, triaging with postmortem CT which cases need a full autopsy, and producing the certified report and cause-of-death determination - priced as a fixed annual contract rather than per autopsy, into a market where 850 forensic pathologists must cover work that needs about 1,250 and accreditation caps how many autopsies each may perform.

cross.ai_signal: Three jobs here are frontier-model jobs and none of them were doable before. (1) Decedent reconstruction: a body arrives with a name, an age and a scene report, and the evidence of what killed them sits in a hospital record at another system, a state prescription drug monitoring database, EMS run sheets, prior admissions and a pharmacy history - all of it retrieved with no medical record number at the investigating institution, no living patient to consent, and no payer relationship to route through. It is entity resolution plus clinical judgement over contradictory fragments, and it is today done by hand by an investigator on the phone. (2) Imaging-led triage: postmortem CT is described in the 2026 literature as the most mature and extensively validated component of contemporary forensic investigation, and a model that reads the scan against the scene and the history is what decides whether a case needs a full autopsy at all - which is the only lever that moves capacity, because the number of pathologists is fixed. (3) Report and certification: the output is a legal document that must survive cross-examination - cause and manner of death, the toxicology interpretation in context, and a death certificate whose coding feeds national mortality statistics - and generating a defensible draft for a pathologist to interrogate and sign is the highest-value use of the scarce hour in the building.
cross.structural_signal: The supply side is collapsing against a fixed statutory workload. About 850 forensic pathologists are practising in the United States, roughly 400 fewer than needed, against more than 3 million deaths a year, 1.3 million referrals to medical examiner and coroner offices and about 605,000 accepted cases. The National Association of Medical Examiners caps accredited practice at 250 autopsies per pathologist per year, with 325 as an absolute ceiling - so an incumbent legally cannot add capacity by working its people harder. Offices now average well over 100 days to complete autopsy reports, prosecutors in North Carolina say the backlog is delaying justice, West Virginia has publicly attributed its backlog to the shortage, and Maryland sought federal assistance for a body backlog. Counties are already outsourcing and the arrangements are visibly failing: Kootenai County was sending about 70 cases a year to Spokane at roughly 2,000 dollars each until the relationship ended in December 2025; Mohave County contracts its medical examiner administration to a private memorial group; Franklin County spent millions on outside contracts after four of its five pathologists resigned.

ideas.source_pattern: Two funded proofs of the same mechanism, both from this scan. Integral raised an 18M euro Series A on 2026-09-16 from Mosaic Ventures, Reid Hoffman, Cherry Ventures, General Catalyst and Puzzle Ventures to operate as an AI-native accounting and tax firm in Germany delivering through licensed professionals. Behind it, the YC Summer 2026 batch's agent-native services cluster (Rational, Billow AI and Last Accounting Company in accounting; Osmaura and Erinys in law) and YC's own request for startups state the thesis outright - sell the service, not the software - with Savvy Wealth as the paying evidence that it scales (100M dollar Series C at a 600M dollar valuation on 2026-09-09, up from 225M in July 2025, 150+ advisers, 19 hours a week saved each). Ferry Health (9M dollar seed on 2026-09-16 led by Andreessen Horowitz and Index Ventures, over 1M patients) is the third funded datapoint that an agent can now carry the administrative half of a clinical process.
ideas.wedge: Four blocks, and the first is the load-bearing one. (1) The incumbent private forensic pathology groups price a la carte and their revenue line is the procedure the wedge replaces. ProPublica documented Forensic Medical Group's model in detail: minimal overhead, clients supply the facilities, tools and scene investigators, headquarters functions as an invoice processing centre, and pricing is per procedure - 1,250 dollars for a full autopsy against 600 dollars for an external examination. Converting autopsies into imaging-led external examinations, which is the only way to lift capacity, roughly halves their revenue per case; and they own no scanners, no imaging pipeline and no software to do it with. (2) The accreditation ceiling forbids the incumbent's actual growth strategy: NAME caps 250 autopsies per pathologist per year (325 absolute), and the same ProPublica reporting has that firm's five doctors each handling 300 cases a year or more. Their scaling model is already outside the standard. (3) The health-AI leaders have the wrong data model and no revenue path: Epic, Oracle Health and the ambient-scribe vendors model a living, insured patient inside a billable encounter, and a decedent has no medical record number at the investigating office, no payer, no consent and no claim - there is no revenue-cycle machinery to attach to, which is precisely what funds every health-AI product. Serving this is a second product sold through county procurement. (4) The pricing motion is the wedge: a fixed annual contract to run a county's death investigation requires absorbing volume risk, which a firm whose only asset is a roster of pathologists cannot do.
ideas.buyer: The county board of supervisors or commissioners, together with the elected coroner or sheriff-coroner (or the appointed chief medical examiner) who holds the death investigation contract, in a county large enough to have continuous caseload and too small to hold a full accredited office - roughly the 1,500 US jurisdictions in that band. The district attorney is the co-signer in practice, because the backlog is their problem.
ideas.trigger: The death investigation or forensic pathology contract coming up for re-tender or non-renewal - typically after the county's contract pathologist retires or resigns, after an accreditation lapse, or after a prosecutor or judge puts the report backlog on the record in a pending homicide case.
ideas.why_incumbents_cant: Occupancy was searched first and four ways: forensic pathology and death investigation AI startups funded in 2026; the Y Combinator directory and seed-round coverage for coroner and death-investigation software; private forensic pathology service companies scaling on county contracts; and the academic literature on AI in forensic pathology. The result: the academic reviews state plainly that applications specific to medicolegal death investigation remain largely experimental, supported by retrospective proof-of-concept studies, with AI best regarded today as assistive. The commercial field is entirely non-AI staffing: Forensic Pathology Services LLC, founded 2018, sells scalable staffing to medical examiner and coroner offices nationwide; Forensic Medical Group grew from three counties to more than a dozen on the per-procedure model above; case-management software is held by small unfunded vendors. No venture-backed AI-native entrant was found anywhere in the segment.
ideas.expansion_path: About 605,000 accepted cases a year at an average budget of roughly 3,000 dollars per accepted case is a standing public spend on the order of 1.8bn dollars across about 2,000 offices, and the beachhead is the mid-sized county that cannot staff an accredited office -> the large metropolitan and statewide systems, where a single contract is eight figures and the same imaging, records and reporting engine applies -> forensic toxicology and postmortem imaging, today bought separately from national reference laboratories, which become margin the moment you own the case -> the hospital and attending-physician side of death certification, where roughly 2.5 million deaths a year are certified by clinicians with no training in it and the resulting cause-of-death data is known to be poor -> the compounding asset, which is the only linked national dataset of scene, imaging, toxicology, medical history and certified cause of death: the thing that prices mortality for life insurers, detects drug-supply changes for public health weeks before anyone else, and supplies post-market signal to pharmacovigilance -> the same system sold into the coronial services of the UK, Canada, Australia and the Nordics, all of which have the same statutory duty and the same workforce arithmetic.

ideas.summary: Non-promotional machine-answer record for regulated medicine: continuously interrogate the major AI assistants about a manufacturer's drug or device, detect factual error and off-label drift in what the machines tell patients and prescribers, and produce an audit-trailed correction file owned by medical affairs rather than by marketing.
ideas.source_pattern: Profound - 180M dollar Series D on 2026-09-15 at a 1.8bn dollar valuation led by Sequoia and Kleiner Perkins, seven months after its 96M dollar Series C, with more than 1,000 enterprise brands including over a third of the Fortune 100 and revenue tripled in six months. Mechanism: what a machine says about you is now a measurable, steerable demand channel.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: a prescription-medicine manufacturer cannot lawfully buy 'increase how often the model recommends our drug' - promotion of an Rx product carries fair-balance duties and FDA submission obligations - so the same mechanism has to be rebuilt as non-promotional surveillance and correction, sold to medical affairs and regulatory rather than to brand marketing.
ideas.buyer: Medical affairs or regulatory lead at a pharmaceutical or medical-device manufacturer.
ideas.trigger: A prescriber or patient-facing answer that misstates the label, omits a contraindication, or describes an unapproved use.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test, in its strongest form: the leader has already shipped into the segment. Profound itself is sold to pharma teams for brand planning, communications and medical review with a published 99-dollar-a-month entry tier, and the pharma-specific AI-visibility layer is already crowded around it - Otterly publishes pharmaceutical visibility benchmarks, Finseo sells a named pharma solution tracking drug recommendations and clinical citations, and Trakkr, Gravton and PharmaForward all sell pharma AI-search visibility. The compliance framing is a repositioning of a product the leader already sells. Consistent with ts-0037, ts-0225 and ts-0235: this ledger has now killed in the answer-engine category four times.

ideas.summary: Counterparty-defence agent for the industrial supplier: when a Global 500 customer deploys procurement agents that raise claims, deductions and price-down demands at machine speed, give the mid-size supplier on the other end a machine that contests them against its own contract, cost model and delivery evidence.
ideas.source_pattern: Magentic - 18M dollar Series A on 2026-09-17 led by Felicis with Sequoia and the Westly Group, 23.5M dollars total. Traction: Global 500 customers including three of the world's ten largest beverage producers, one customer running more than a million orders a year through its agents, 4M dollars of savings found at another, reported savings of 2-5 percent. Mechanism: an agent executes a large industrial company's transactional supply-chain work end to end inside its existing systems and communication rails, paid out of the money it recovers.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: channel conflict in its purest form - Magentic's revenue is the supplier's loss, so it can never represent both sides of the same transaction.
ideas.buyer: The commercial or finance lead at a Tier-2 industrial or consumer-goods supplier.
ideas.trigger: The first quarter in which claim and deduction volume from the largest customer triples with no change in the underlying shipments.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. Supplier-side dispute automation is a named 2026 category with the same agentic framing: Emagia's Deductions Management agent runs autonomous research across more than 100 retailer portals with full order-to-cash context, RetailPath sells autonomous agents for the end-to-end dispute process, and the trade summary of 2026 is explicitly 'from workflow software that helps analysts work faster to agentic AI that researches, validates and disputes deductions with minimal human touch.' The industrial-versus-retail distinction is a segment label, not a second product.

ideas.summary: The screened party's own continuously maintained diligence file: invert the due-diligence engine so the business being onboarded holds a machine-built, continuously refreshed evidence pack about itself - ownership, adverse media, sanctions exposure, source of funds - and presents it to every counterparty that would otherwise re-investigate it from scratch.
ideas.source_pattern: Xapien - 56M dollar Series B announced 2026-09-11 led by Spectrum Equity. Traction: 350 clients and partners across 15 countries including Greenberg Traurig, ABB, Dow Jones Risk and Compliance and KPMG, ARR up more than 350 percent in two years, roughly 90 percent of onboarding cases automated, half of revenue already in the US. Mechanism: a point-in-time analyst report becomes a continuously maintained live determination.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: channel conflict - Xapien's customers are the screeners, so it cannot sell exoneration to the screened without destroying the trust its determinations depend on.
ideas.buyer: The finance lead at a business that keeps failing or stalling counterparty onboarding - money-services businesses, charities operating in sanctioned regions, diaspora-facing firms, crypto-adjacent operators.
ideas.trigger: An account frozen, a bank exit letter, or an onboarding that has sat unresolved past the point where the commercial deal dies.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. Reusable and portable KYC is an established, contested category rather than an opening: CLEAR1 sells a reusable identity layer, Affinidi sells reusable KYC on holder-held credentials, and Shufti, IDfy, AiPrise and Binderr's reviewed field all sit in the same square - with banks' roughly 500M dollars a year of redundant verification as the standard pitch. The regulatory tide is also already assigned: eIDAS 2.0 obliges EU member states to provide interoperable European Digital Identity Wallets from 2026, which is the state building the credential rail this idea would have sold.

ideas.summary: Video-trained manipulation policies pointed at nuclear decommissioning: autonomous handling, size-reduction and sorting of legacy radioactive waste inside gloveboxes and cells, where every object is different, no two facilities are alike and teleoperation is still the state of the art.
ideas.source_pattern: Rhoda AI - 450M dollar Series A at a 1.7bn dollar valuation (Premji Invest), a Direct Video Action model pretrained on hundreds of millions of videos, already running autonomously in production environments and beating a customer KPI at under two minutes a cycle; alongside Mind Robotics' 500M dollar Series A (Accel, Andreessen Horowitz) deploying in Rivian plants. Mechanism: high-variability physical work no longer has to be programmed.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: the robot foundation-model companies sell models and cells into high-volume structured manufacturing and logistics; a contaminated cell with a regulator, a radiation-degraded electronics budget and no two objects alike is a different product and a different safety case.
ideas.buyer: The site licence company or its decommissioning programme lead at a legacy nuclear site.
ideas.trigger: A glovebox or waste-retrieval campaign whose schedule depends on manual operator hours that the workforce cannot supply.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test plus segment viability. AtkinsRealis and the Oxford Robotics Institute have partnered specifically to develop autonomous robots and physical AI for hazardous nuclear environments, and the UK Nuclear Decommissioning Authority is funding the RAICo teleoperation programme at 9.5M pounds over four years with a stated goal of taking over 50 percent of glovebox operations by 2030. The work is also procured through site licence companies and their framework primes rather than bought by a startup's buyer, so even an empty technical square would not be reachable.

ideas.summary: Answer-channel fraud defence: detect and remediate the case where an AI assistant hands a customer a scammer's support number, a spoofed checkout link or a fabricated policy in the brand's name, and escalate it into the model providers' correction paths.
ideas.source_pattern: Profound's category evidence plus the documented failure surface - Perplexity returning a scam call centre as the official Emirates reservations number, Google AI Overviews serving fake Southwest numbers, ChatGPT pulling fraudulent contact details from poisoned pages, and China Central Television's 2026-03-15 consumer gala exposing a commercial generative-engine-optimisation black market that could surface a fake brand in mainstream AI assistants within hours.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: channel conflict - the visibility platforms are paid by brands to influence model answers, so policing manipulation of those same answers sets them against their own product.
ideas.buyer: Fraud or trust-and-safety lead at a consumer-facing brand with a high-value support channel - airlines, banks, utilities, marketplaces.
ideas.trigger: The first wave of customers who reached a scammer after asking an assistant for the company's phone number.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test. Doppel is an AI-native social-engineering defence platform that maps fake accounts, spoofed sites, malicious ads and dark-web infrastructure into a live threat graph and runs agentic takedowns through platform APIs and escalation paths with its own SOC; Bolster sells the same detection-and-removal loop for phishing, impersonation and AI-generated fraud campaigns, and Bitsight and MarqVision hold the enterprise brand-protection seat. The AI answer surface is a new channel for an owned category, not a new category.

ideas.summary: Robotic electrical and fibre installation for the AI data-centre buildout: hold the electrical contractor licences, put learned deformable-object manipulation on cable pulling, termination and fibre work, and sell installed capacity against the energisation date rather than selling robots to a subcontractor.
ideas.source_pattern: The buildout's labour arithmetic - more than 66GW of North American data-centre capacity under construction, a projected shortfall of up to 499,000 construction workers, roughly 81,000 open electrician positions - against Rhoda AI and Mind Robotics proving that high-variability manipulation policies now work in production.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: the robot foundation-model companies license models to integrators and factory owners; a jobsite has no owner to buy the cell, and being a licensed, bonded electrical contractor under prevailing-wage and project-labour agreements is a different company that would cannibalise their software margin.
ideas.buyer: The electrical subcontractor or the owner's construction director on a hyperscale campus.
ideas.trigger: A hall whose energisation date is slipping on trade labour rather than on equipment.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test at both ends, and duplicative. The largest buyer is building it in-house - Meta has been running dual-armed Watney robots on data-hall cabling since mid-2025 with internal estimates of automating up to 80 percent of some technician workloads - and ULC Technologies already sells a robotic cable-splicing machine to utilities as robots-as-a-service with Con Edison. It also restates ts-0331 (data-hall remote hands, killed on Exclaim and Meta) and ts-0325 (a single licensed installation entity, killed on Treehouse and Qmerit).

ideas.summary: Subsurface of record: fuse historical aerials, fire-insurance maps, city directories, regulatory databases, geology and every prior boring into a predictive model of what is in the ground under a specific parcel, then monetise the determination by underwriting the environmental indemnity rather than selling the report.
ideas.source_pattern: Xapien's continuous-determination mechanism re-pointed at a report with a statutory shelf life - the ASTM Phase I environmental site assessment, priced at roughly 2,200 to 4,000 dollars, produced by an environmental professional billing per hour, and stale within 180 days.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: the incumbent consultants bill per report and per hour, so the efficient path deletes their own revenue, and the carriers underwrite from those same reports with no data asset of their own.
ideas.buyer: The developer, lender or acquirer blocked on a site with a recognised environmental condition.
ideas.trigger: A deal held up by a Phase I finding with no priced path to closing.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the config-change test - the leaders have already executed it - reinforced by a physical gate. Environmental underwriters in 2025-2026 already use GIS overlays, historical aerial imagery and AI predictive models to estimate the probability of unknown contamination; V7 sells a packaged AI environmental-impairment underwriting agent that extracts findings and recognised environmental conditions for pollution-liability decisions; Cretelligent holds the commercial-real-estate ESA data and workflow position. And the part that would have been the moat cannot be automated at all: Phase II still requires on-site sampling and laboratory analysis, because no model replaces a soil core.

ideas.summary: Royalty truth engine: reconstruct what a licensee should have reported from its own external footprint - shipments, listings, usage, filings - against what it did report, and take the recovery on contingency instead of billing an audit.
ideas.source_pattern: Magentic's recovery-funded mechanism applied to self-reporting agreements, where the published audit experience is that 87 percent of audited licensees underreport and underpay and average underreporting runs 15 to 20 percent.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: the incumbent royalty auditors are forensic accountants billing hourly, so compressing the audit deletes the fee it is paid for.
ideas.buyer: The licensing or business-development head at a brand, university, biotech or music rights holder with dozens of self-reporting licensees.
ideas.trigger: An audit clause about to expire, or a statement whose numbers moved without an explanation.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test plus platform ownership. Licensing-management platforms already ship the detection half - automated error detection that cross-checks reported royalties against calculated amounts and flags discrepancies before statements are finalised is the named 2026 capability at MyMediabox and its peers, and those platforms sit on the licensor's data by default - while Stout, Astute and the forensic boutiques hold the contingent audit relationship. The remaining wedge is a fee structure, not a structural block.

ideas.summary: AI-native home-dialysis provider: take patients out of the chair and run their treatment at home with continuous machine monitoring and remote clinical judgement, against a duopoly whose asset base is in-centre chair utilisation.
ideas.source_pattern: Rhoda-era remote monitoring plus the value-based kidney-care wave; the structural claim was an innovator's dilemma, with more than 30 percent of patients who start peritoneal dialysis transferring back to in-centre haemodialysis within two years.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: DaVita and Fresenius own roughly four fifths of US dialysis in physical clinics, so moving patients home strands their own capital.
ideas.buyer: The nephrologist and the patient at the moment of modality choice.
ideas.trigger: A new end-stage kidney disease diagnosis, or a failed home start about to revert to in-centre care.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the config-change test, already executed. DaVita and Fresenius have publicly teamed up to bring dialysis care out of their clinics and into the home; DaVita has built and deployed machine-learning models specifically to anticipate the complications that push home patients back into the chair, and is investing in AI-powered chronic-care platforms and AI scheduling. The claimed dilemma is being managed by the incumbents in the open, and the value-based flank is held by Somatus, Strive and InterWell, with an NEA-backed team of former DaVita executives claiming tripled home adoption.

ideas.summary: Airline-side machine listener for the radio: transcribe and understand controller-pilot voice in real time for a Part 121 operator's own flights, catching readback and hearback errors, mis-set clearances and runway-incursion setups, and feeding the carrier's flight-safety record.
ideas.source_pattern: The frontier-audio capability jump - purpose-tuned recognition has cut word error rates on clipped, noisy, jargon-dense aviation radio from roughly 80 percent to under 15 percent - against an air traffic system short thousands of controllers.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: the air-navigation ground vendors sell certified systems into multi-year state acquisition programmes and cannot ship an advisory product into an airline's own operation; the airline flight-safety department is a different buyer with a different procurement.
ideas.buyer: The director of flight safety at a Part 121 carrier.
ideas.trigger: A reportable runway incursion or an altitude bust traced to a readback the crew did not catch.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test plus platform ownership. Universal Avionics already ships Universal Taxi Assist, which listens to flight-deck communications over Bluetooth from the electronic flight bag, resolves the callsign and renders ground control's taxi instructions as text precisely to prevent miscommunication; the controller side is held by the SESAR HAAWAII programme, which reports detecting 81 percent of readback errors on real recorded voice, and by Frequentis and DLR. The avionics OEMs own the flight deck and the air-navigation vendors own the tower.

ideas.summary: Condo project of record: an AI-native determination of whether a specific condominium project is eligible for secondary-market financing - read the association's budget, reserve study, milestone and engineering reports, minutes, insurance and litigation, issue the warranted determination, and keep it current so the second loan in the building is free.
ideas.source_pattern: Xapien's continuous-determination mechanism against a dated cliff: on 2026-08-03 Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac retired the Limited and Streamlined review pathways, which had covered roughly 40 percent of condo project reviews, pushing every loan in a project of more than ten units into Full Review, with the reserve contribution requirement scheduled to rise from 10 to 15 percent from 2027 and projects whose critical repairs exceed 10,000 dollars a unit rendered ineligible outright.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: the incumbent condo-document businesses sell a per-package human review on three-to-five-day turns, so automating it deletes their fee, and the government-sponsored enterprises deliberately push the determination and its representation-and-warranty liability onto the lender rather than publishing a project database.
ideas.buyer: The condo underwriting lead at a mortgage lender.
ideas.trigger: A purchase contract failing because the project cannot be warranted under the post-August-2026 Full Review standard.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the occupancy test, decisively, and it is the cleanest example this run of a moat opening and someone already walking in. Rexera, formerly InspectHOA, has shipped Condo Project Review for lenders as a fully warranted project review on top of its AI-agent document-acquisition stack, was named an ALTA Elite Provider for 2026, and is now carried as a RealPage company - which puts the platform owner of property-management data behind the exact product. CondoTek, which is acquiring National Condo Advisors and supplies DataVerify, holds the document-and-questionnaire flank.

ideas.summary: The condo repair balance sheet: underwrite an association's critical-repair loan by machine-reading its engineering reports, reserve study, minutes, delinquency history and unit-level mortgage record, and price it on the warrantability the repair restores, since an ineligible project loses 5 to 30 percent of unit value.
ideas.source_pattern: The same 2026-08-03 Fannie and Freddie cliff, from the capital side rather than the determination side, with the reserve requirement stepping to 15 percent from 2027.
ideas.wedge: Attempted: specialist community-association banks underwrite from a few financial statements and lend to well-run associations, so the buildings that need the money most sit outside every credit box.
ideas.buyer: The board treasurer or community manager of an association facing a critical-repair finding it cannot fund.
ideas.trigger: A reserve study or milestone inspection that lands with a repair bill larger than the association's entire reserve.
ideas.kill_reason: Killed by the config-change test - there is no structural block, only a risk-appetite difference - with occupancy alongside. Community-association lending is an established specialty with a dozen credible balance sheets already marketing reserve-shortfall and restoration loans (Axos, NCB, Truist, Byline, First Citizens, Popular, plus non-bank lenders such as Gelt Financial), the segment is described in the trade as low-default, and HOA Loan Services launched an AI loan portal in June 2025. Competing on price against insured deposits with venture equity points the economics the wrong way; 'we would take more risk' is a credit decision any of them can make next quarter.

ideas.summary: AI-native municipal advisor for small and rural public issuers: register as a municipal advisor, take the statutory fiduciary seat on the issuer's side of the table, and run the whole pre-issuance job by machine - reading the audited financials, the existing debt and its covenants, the rate and enrolment studies, the budget and the prior official statements to produce the debt-capacity analysis, the structuring recommendation, the drafted disclosure and the continuing-disclosure calendar - for the tens of thousands of school districts, water and sewer districts, small cities and special districts whose deals are too small to pay for a banker's week.
ideas.source_pattern: Corridor: 25M dollar seed announced 2026-09-21 led by Bain Capital Ventures with BoxGroup and Definition Capital, plus angels from OpenAI, Ramp, Scale AI, Oscar, Medallion, Reducto and Tennr, built on the explicit observation that small accounts generate lower commissions while taking the same amount of a licensed advisor's time, so the licensed advisory industry ignores them. The mechanism sits in a six-company cluster: American Growth Insurance (about 70M dollars of committed equity, an AI-first operating model tested across 10 agencies reporting more than 50 percent higher agency profitability, targeting 10M dollars of revenue by end-2026), Beacon (225M dollar Series C, more than 500M dollars raised in a year, roughly one acquisition a week, more than 50 percent EBITDA growth across the portfolio), Long Lake (about 670M dollars raised, 100M dollars of EBITDA inside two years), Current formerly Crete (more than 300M dollars of revenue across 30-plus accounting firms) and Integral (18M euro Series A, Mosaic Ventures and Reid Hoffman, agents do the work and licensed experts stand behind the result).

cross.ai_signal: Three jobs here were not doable at this price before. (1) Reading the issuer: a small district's financial reality lives in a 200-page annual comprehensive financial report as a scanned PDF, a decade of board minutes, a rate study, an enrolment projection, existing bond covenants with additional-bonds tests and rate covenants, and state debt-limit statutes - and the analysis of what this issuer can actually afford, at what structure, is document reasoning across all of it. (2) Drafting the disclosure: the SEC's Office of Municipal Securities said on 2026-09-16 that a municipal advisor participating in preparing an official statement faces primary and secondary antifraud liability under Securities Act Section 17(a) and Exchange Act Section 10(b) regardless of contractual disclaimers, and must perform an appropriate level of inquiry into accuracy and completeness - an inquiry that is exactly a machine's job to run exhaustively across the issuer's own record and exactly what no human can afford to do on a 4M dollar issue. (3) Maintaining it: continuing-disclosure obligations under Rule 15c2-12, material event notices, arbitrage rebate computations and covenant compliance are persistent low-intensity vigilance across thousands of issuers, which is the capability that repriced in 2026.
cross.structural_signal: A 4 trillion dollar market with roughly 50,000 distinct issuers and about 500bn dollars of annual issuance, in which advisory capacity is concentrated on the large deals because the fee is a function of par. The small issuer's practical alternatives are to take a bank's direct-placement terms with no fiduciary on its side, or to rely on the underwriter - who under the SEC Municipal Advisor Rule owes it no fiduciary duty at all.

ideas.wedge: Three different structural blocks, one per class of would-be follower. (a) The underwriters and placement banks are barred: under the SEC Municipal Advisor Rule a broker-dealer acting as underwriter to an issue owes the issuer no fiduciary duty and cannot simultaneously be its municipal advisor on that issue, so the institution that wants to buy or place the paper can never sit in this seat. Serving the segment properly means telling the issuer not to take the bank's loan. (b) The established municipal advisory firms (PFM, Hilltop, Baker Tilly, Stifel, the regional shops) are priced out: their unit of production is a senior banker's week and their fee schedule is tied to par, so a 3-5M dollar issue cannot carry a staffed engagement. Pointing existing salespeople at 30,000 small issuers is not a configuration change; it is a different cost structure. (c) The issuer-software vendors (BondLink, on the 2026 GovTech 100 and supporting more than 100bn dollars of client par in 2025; DebtBook, which shipped AI briefing and AI-analyst features in 2026) sell tools to the finance office and are structurally reluctant to register: becoming a municipal advisor means assuming a statutory fiduciary duty and, per the 2026-09-16 SEC statement, direct antifraud liability for disclosure - a different liability posture, a different insurance programme, and direct competition with the advisory firms that are today their channel into issuers.
